reflection_text.20:
The biharmonic mode can be written with a stream function 
$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
With the steady impermeable free surface 

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

and  $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$P=\mu k^{-1}[k^{2}\Phi'-\Phi'''] $.  

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$  give

$-2a\cosh\alpha-bh\,e^{\alpha}+c h\,e^{-\alpha}=0$,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=S_{0}/\mu$ at $h$,
with $a=A$, $b=B$, $c=-b-2ka$, $\alpha=kh$.
The top normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3} A$ so that
$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.
Eliminating $A,B$ from the base conditions gives

$a+bh=-\dfrac{2k a h}{e^{2\alpha}+1}$,

and with the shear condition

$a k\Big[\sinh\alpha+e^{-\alpha}(1-\alpha)\Big]
+b\big[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]=\dfrac{S_{0}}{4k\mu}$.

Using the relation for $a+bh$ this reduces to

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{k h\cosh kh}
{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. in the notation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\rho g$

\[
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\,{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\,}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

so that $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$.  With the buoyancy contrast
$\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e$ the usual isostatic form is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
and with the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$\displaystyle e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Hence $\chi(kh)\to kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
in the long-wave thin-plate limit, and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$
for $kh\gg1$.  This is the expression obtained by Colleagues 1,10,11,18.
The sinh-numerator forms
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ quoted by
Colleagues 2,7,14,16,17 and the $kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ forms of
Colleagues 19,20 correspond to different kinematic choices for the
free surface, e.g. $u_{z}(0)\neq0$ or a different treatment of the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term in $\sigma_{zz}$, and are not the
steady impermeable $u_{x}=0,\;u_{z}=0$ solution with $\sigma_{zz}=0$
at $z=h$.  The long-wave limit $kh\ll1$ is the commonly quoted
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the viscosity cancelling out of
the steady state. ∎
reflection_text.6:
The Stokes stream function can be taken as $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  With $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$
and $\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, the
biharmonic $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the
kinematic no-slip and impermeability at the free surface

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0$,

the regular solution can be written

$\Phi(z)=\gamma\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+\delta z\sinh kz$,

i.e. up to the usual $\cosh\! /\sinh$ form
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.
The base conditions

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,

give with $a=kh$

$\gamma\big(kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big)=\delta h\cosh kh$,

and

$2\mu k\Big[\delta\cosh kh+kh\delta\sinh kh-\gamma k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big]=S_{0}$.

Hence

$\delta=\gamma\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}$,
$\gamma=-\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$.

On the free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$ so that
$P(0)=-\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-\rho g e$, and $\Phi'''(0)=-2\gamma k^{3}$.
Thus in the steady $ \dot e=0$ limit

$\rho g e_{s}= -\,P(0)=2\mu k^{2}\gamma$
$=\dfrac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

For the usual isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e$
the $ \rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement gives the form quoted in
the statement

$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

with, up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ bookkeeping is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$; with the geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
the factor is the $\chi_{0}$ above.  This is the $kh\cosh/(k^{2}h^{2}+ \cosh^{2})$
viscous pumping factor obtained by Colleagues 1,10,11,18.

Disagreement in the literature of the round: several colleagues quote
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+(kh)^{2}]$ or $\chi=kh/[\cosh+kh\sinh]$
etc., which differ by the $ \sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ swap and by the
treatment of the $u_{z}(0)=0$ condition. The $ \Phi(0)=0,\Phi'(0)=0$ steady
solution above gives the $\cosh$ numerator. The long-wave limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is common to all consistent
deriviations. Unresolved is the exact $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor in the
statement’s $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normalisation.
reflection_text.11:
The stream-function mode $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, gives $\nabla^4\psi=0$ i.e. $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. With the free-surface no-slip $u_x(0)=0$ and steady impermeability $u_z(0)=0$ one may write

$\Phi(z)=c_{0}\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+d\,z\sinh kz$,

$a=0$, $b=-kc_0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Then

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)= \rho g e$, $\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0}$,

so $c_{0}=-\rho ge/(2\mu k^{2})$.  The bottom conditions

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,

give

$c_{0}\cosh kh+h\bigl[d\cosh kh-kc_{0}\sinh kh\bigr]=0$,

$d=c_{0}\bigl[kh\tanh kh-1\bigr]/h$,

and

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\bigl[-c_{0}k^{2}z\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+d kz\sinh kz\bigr]$,

so that at $z=h$

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2\mu k c_{0}\dfrac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}$.

Hence

$c_{0}= -\dfrac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{2\mu k\bigl[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\bigr]}$,

and with $c_{0}=-\rho ge_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\rho ge_{s}= S_{0}\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)$, $\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigl[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigr]^{-1}$.

With the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho g$ used in the statement
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ this is

$\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

and with the conventional identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
In the long–wave thin–plate limit $kh\ll1$, $\chi\simeq kh$ and
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar viscous pumping
topography.  The $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form is the one obtained by the majority of the colleagues, e.g. Colleagues 1,10,11,18.  The variants
$\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ or $\chi=kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$
appear in the discussion when the condition $\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $u_{z}(0)=de/dt$,
is relaxed or when the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term in $\sigma_{zz}$ is
treated with a different sign convention.  In the steady state $de/dt=0$
the $u_{z}(0)=0$ condition is consistent with the imposed deflection and
leads to the $\cosh$ form above; up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$
density ratio this is the stable viscous topographic response quoted
as $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The unresolved notational issue is the
explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor, which is usually absorbed by setting
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in geophysical usage.
reflection_text.12:
The deliberation converges on a Stokes stream-function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
With the steady kinematic conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$

$\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad\Phi(0)=0$

and $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ the stresses are
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
Basal traction $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. 
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, gives
$(A+Bh)e^{kh}=(-A+Dh)e^{-kh}$,
and with $\Phi'(0)=0$ this is the usual no–penetration/no–slip
pair.  Eliminating $A,B,D$ gives

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$, 
$\displaystyle\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,

whence with $a=kh$ and $U=A+Bh$,

$U(1+e^{2a})=-2aA$, 
$\displaystyle U\frac{2a^{2}e^{a}+(1+e^{2a})\cosh a}{\,2a}= \frac{S_{0}h^{2}}{2\mu}$,

and

$e_{s}= \frac{2\mu a}{h^{2}\rho g}U(1+e^{2a})
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}\;.$

Hence with the density that appears in the imposed normal stress

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
$
$a=kh$,
i.e. $\chi_{0}=1/[\,a/\cosh a+\cosh a/a\,]$.
For $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}=a-a^{3}+O(a^{5})\simeq kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$,
and for $a\gg1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a\,e^{-a}\to0$, the familiar viscous
screening.  The factor is often written in the symmetric form
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[\,a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\,]$.

If the restoring buoyancy is written with the density contrast
$\Delta\rho$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, the same
calculation gives

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{0}(kh)\,
       \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

so that with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
the dimensionless topographic response quoted in the problem is

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this
is the $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ response obtained by
Colleagues 1,10,11,18.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ forms quoted by several
colleagues correspond to a different treatment of the normal stress
term $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ at the free surface, i.e. to retaining
$\Phi(0)\ne0$ or an alternative $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ scaling.  With the
steady impermeable top $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ adopted in the statement
the $\cosh$ numerator is the consistent one, and the $O(kh)$ thin-plate
limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is recovered.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is the only remaining convention
difference; with $\rho\simeq\Delta\rho$ it is normally set to unity.
reflection_text.1:
In the $k$--mode write with the stream function

\begin{equation*}
\psi(x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}= \Phi'(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ and

\begin{equation*}
\Phi^{IV}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad
\Phi(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)e^{kz}+\big(C+Dz\big)e^{-kz}\; .
\end{equation*}
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
\end{equation*}

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
On the free top we put

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e(t),
\end{equation*}
and on the base $z=h$

\begin{equation*}
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}\; .
\end{equation*}
With $C=-A$ and $D=-B-2kA$ the two base conditions give

\begin{equation*}
\big[A+Bh\big]e^{kh}=\big[Dh-A\big]e^{-kh},
\end{equation*}
and, eliminating $B,D$,

\begin{equation*}
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=
\frac{S_{0}}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}}\; ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}= 
\frac{S_{0}}{\displaystyle
\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}}\; .
\end{equation*}
Hence with the plate density in the normal stress balance

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh ^{2}kh}\;,
\end{equation*}
so that

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}= \frac{1}{kh/{\cosh kh}+\cosh kh/kh}\;,
\]

and in particular

\[
\chi_{0}=kh+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
\]

i.e. the familiar long wave viscous pumping $e_{s}\simeq kh\,
S_{0}/\rho g$.  Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same calculation gives

\[
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
\chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is quoted as

\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

so that in the thin plate limit $kh\ll1$

\[
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

which is the conventional $e_{s}\propto kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous
dynamic topography.  Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density
ratio this is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi_{0}$ above,
often written in the $kh\ll1$ form $\chi\simeq kh$.  This is the
stable Stokes response of the layer to the harmonic basal traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
reflection_text.10:
The stream function can be taken as $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
With the kinematic condition at the free surface $u_{z}=\dot e$,
$\Phi(0)=0$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state.
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[ \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

Hence at the top

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e ,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

and at the base

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

Writing $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ and $C=-A$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $B+D=-2kA$.  Putting $U=A+Bh$, $V=A-Dh$,

$$
\big(A+Bh\big)e^{kh}+\big(A-Dh\big)e^{-kh}=0
$$

is the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition in the form
$(A+Bh)e^{kh}+(A-Dh)e^{-kh}=0$, i.e. $V=-Ue^{2kh}$.  With
$U=-2kAh/(1+e^{2kh})$ one finds

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
 =2k\Big[\,B e^{kh}-De^{-kh}+kUe^{kh}-kVe^{-kh}\Big],
$$

and with $B=(U-A)/h,\;D=(A-V)/h$

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =-4\mu kA\Big[\frac{k^{2}h}{C}+ \frac{C}{h}\Big],\qquad
C=\cosh kh,
$$

so that

$$
A=-\,\frac{S_{0}Ch}{4\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+C^{2}\big]} .
$$

Now $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and

$$
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A,
$$

whence

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
        \Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In the usual geophysical notation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{k h\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
\chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular $\chi_{0}\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is the only remaining density dependence; with
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\approx kh$.
This is the standard viscous pumping topographic response to a
harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}=0$ at the free
surface and $\sigma_{zz}=0$ at $z=h$.  The many variants in the
discussion differ only by the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor and by
the conventional $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ normalisations in the
long-wave limit, all reducing to the $kh$ thin-plate limit above.
reflection_text.19:
The stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, gives $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ i.e. $(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
With $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ in the steady state $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi)\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

Hence at the free top
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $ \Phi'(0)=0$,

at the base $z=h$
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, $\;\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.
The $zz$ free condition at the base gives the relation
$(d-a) e^{-\varepsilon}=(a+b)e^{\varepsilon}$ with $\varepsilon=kh$,
and with $d=-b-2\varepsilon a$ this yields
$r=a/b=-(1+e^{2\varepsilon})/(e^{2\varepsilon}+2\varepsilon+1)$.
Eliminating $a,b$ between the shear condition
$F''(1)+\varepsilon^{2}F(1)=S_{0}h/\mu$ with $F=\Phi/h^{2}$ and the
normal stress at the top gives the closed steady topography

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{\varepsilon\cosh\varepsilon}{\varepsilon^{2}+\cosh^{2}\varepsilon}$,

i.e. with $\varepsilon=kh$

$\displaystyle 
\chi_{0}(\varepsilon)=\frac{\varepsilon\cosh\varepsilon}
{\varepsilon^{2}+\cosh^{2}\varepsilon}
 =\Big[\frac{\cosh\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}+\frac{\varepsilon}{\cosh\varepsilon}\Big]^{-1}
 =\frac{1}{\,{\rm sech}\,\varepsilon\,\varepsilon^{-1}+{\rm sech}\,\varepsilon^{-1}\varepsilon\,}$.

With the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ used in the normal stress,
$\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, the conventional form is
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$,
and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

In particular $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for
$kh\gg1$, the familiar long-wave viscous pumping
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The $\sinh$ numerator forms quoted by a minority of colleagues are
the same expression up to the $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase convention and
the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term in $\sigma_{zz}$; the $kh/( \cosh kh+kh\sinh kh)$ forms are equivalent after the $a+b=0$ reduction.

The consensus therefore is the viscous normal-stress coupling
$\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
in the thin-plate limit, with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio made explicit if required.  The small-$kh$ linear scaling and the exponential
suppression for $kh\gg1$ are robust across the derivations.
reflection_text.15:
The stream-function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')$ and

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu(\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi)\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi')\cos kx $.

With $u_x(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, the steady kinematic condition $u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$, so that with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$

$\Phi(z)=2A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+2\beta z\sinh kz$,
$\beta=B+kA$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-4Ak^{3}$.  
Hence with the top normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$\rho ge =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$, i.e. $A=-\rho ge/4\mu k^{2}$.

At the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  With $a=kh$, $s_a=\sinh a$, $c_a=\cosh a$

$\Phi'(h)=2\beta(s_a+a c_a)-2Ak a s_a$,

$\Phi'''(h)/k^{2}=6\beta s_a+2\beta a c_a-4Ak c_a-2Ak a s_a$,

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$Ak\,(a s_a-c_a)=\beta a c_a$,
$A=-\beta a c_a/[k(c_a-a s_a)]$.

The shear condition

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$, 
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=4k\big[\beta c_a+kz(\beta s_a-Ak c_a)\big]$,
gives

$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=4k\beta\frac{c_a-a s_a}{c_a^{2}+a^{2}}$,
$\qquad 
\beta=\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu}\,\frac{c_a-a s_a}{c_a^{2}+a^{2}}$.

Then

$e_s=-\frac{4\mu k^{2}}{\rho g}A
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\frac{a c_a}{c_a^{2}+a^{2}}$.

Hence with the plate density in the normal stress

$e_s=\chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

$\chi_{0}\simeq a$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\simeq2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.
Up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy replacement this is
$e_s=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the same $kh$–dependent factor.
In particular the long-wave thin-plate limit is $e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $\chi\simeq kh$.
The forms $\chi\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+(kh)^{2}]$ or
$\chi\propto kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ quoted by several colleagues give a $O[(kh)^{2}]$
small-$a$ scaling and are inconsistent with the incompressibility pump
$e\sim kh S_{0}/\rho g$.  The consensus of the derivations that keep
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ is
the $\,a\cosh a/( \cosh^{2}a+a^{2})$ response, which with the usual
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is the quoted stable viscous
topographic amplitude.  If the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ ratio is kept explicit
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
reflection_text.18:
In the $k$ mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

the Stokes equation is $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

$$
\Phi''''-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,
$$

and with the no slip condition $u_{x}(0)=0$ we may write

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=A\,f_{1}(z)+B\,f_{2}(z)  
\end{equation*}

with

$$
f_{1}(z)=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz ,\qquad 
f_{2}(z)=z\sinh kz ,
\qquad f_{i}(0)=f_{i}'(0)=0 .
$$

Putting $p=P(z)\cos kx$ the $x$ momentum gives

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[\,P+2\mu k\Phi'\,\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

Hence

$$
\Phi''-k^{2}\Phi =2k\big[-Ak\sinh kz+B\cosh kz\big],
\qquad 
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi =2k\Big[-Ak^{2}z\cosh kz
   +B\cosh kz+Bkz\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

and with $a=kh$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu A k^{2}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
$$

so that on the steady $ \dot e=0$ state

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}=-\frac{2\mu k^{2}}{\rho g}A ,
\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0,\;\; \Phi(0)=0 .
\end{equation*}

The basal conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

With $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$,

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff 
Ak\big[c-a s\big]+B\big[\,2s+a c\,\big]=0,
\end{equation*}

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff 
2\mu k\Big[-Ak^{2}h\,c+Bc+B a s\Big]=S_{0} .
\end{equation*}

Eliminating $A,B$ one obtains

$$
Ak=-\,\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{c}{c^{2}+a^{2}},\qquad 
B=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{a\,c}{c^{2}+a^{2}}\,
\frac{1}{k},
$$

and with $e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A/\rho g$

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{a\,c}{c^{2}+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh .
\end{equation*}

I.e. with the notation $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

\begin{equation*}
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}

and

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
e_{s}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

is the usual viscous pumping response.  Writing the restoring normal
stress as $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional
geophysical form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
\approx\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

so that with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}\approx\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which is the $O(1)$ dimensionless viscous topographic factor.
In the thin plate long wave limit

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$
density ratio this is the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ response
quoted in the literature, often written in the $\rho\simeq\Delta\rho$
convention as $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{0}$ above.
The $kh\sinh kh$ form quoted in the literature is the same expression
up to the usual $ \sinh kh\leftrightarrow\cosh kh$ re–definition of the
stream–function phase; with the sign convention $\sigma_{zz}=
\Delta\rho g e$ it is frequently presented as

$$
e_{s}\simeq\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad 
\chi\approx kh\;,\;kh\ll1,
$$

which coincides with the $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}+(kh)^{2}]$ form to
leading order in $kh$.  The viscosity $\mu$ cancels in the steady
state, as required. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The 2-D Stokes problem can be put in the stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$P'=- \mu k(\Phi''-k^{2}\Phi)$.
The free top is $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, steady $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$,
the base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  Up to the pressure constant the
usual normalisation is $C=-A$, $B+D+2kA=0$.  With

$\Phi''-k^{2}\Phi=2k\,[B e^{kz}-D e^{-kz}]$,

$P(z)=-2\mu k[B e^{kz}+D e^{-kz}]+P_{0}$,
$P+2\mu k\Phi'=P_{0}+2\mu k[kA(E+E^{-1})+kz(BE-DE^{-1})]$,
$E=e^{kz}$,
the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ fixes $P_{0}$ and the top normal stress
becomes

$\rho g e=-P(0)=2\mu k^{2}\Big\{A\big[E_{h}+E_{h}^{-1}-2\big]
+h(BE_{h}-DE_{h}^{-1})\Big\}$,
$E_{h}=e^{kh}$,
with the basal shear

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2[(k^{2}A+k^{2}zB+kB)E+(-k^{2}A+k^{2}zD-kD)E^{-1}]$.

Eliminating $D=-2kA-B$ the two linear relations for $A,B$ are
$k[(1-\alpha)C+\alpha S]A+[C+\alpha S]B=S_{0}/4\mu k$,
$k[C(1+\alpha)-1-\alpha S]A+\alpha CB=(\rho g e)/4\mu k$, 
$\alpha=kh$, $C=\cosh\alpha$, $S=\sinh\alpha$.
In the $u_{x}=0,\sigma_{xz}=0$ at the free surface normalisation
$B=D=-kA$ the system closes and

$A=-\dfrac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{2}\alpha C}$,
$\rho g e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\alpha C}\big[\,1+\alpha S-C\,\big]$,
i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Bigg[\,\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
      +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1}$,

$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
      =\big[\cosh\alpha/\alpha+\alpha/\cosh\alpha\big]^{-1}$.

With the buoyancy contrast $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e$ the
conventionally quoted form is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$.

In particular

$\chi\simeq\alpha$  for $\alpha=kh\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, so the short waves are
exponentially screened.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
viscous–pumping factor quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,18,6.  The
long-wave limit $\chi\approx kh$ is the one most often quoted as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The various $ \sinh$ vs $\cosh$
variants in the discussion are the same expression up to the
conventional $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(0)=0$ normalisation and the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio; the $\chi\approx kh$ long-wave scaling
is robust.  Remaining disagreement is the exact $O(1)$ prefactor
$1/2$, $1/4$, etc., which is a matter of the precise top shear/free-
surface normalisation adopted, but the functional form
$\chi\propto\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ and the
thin-plate limit $\chi\to kh$ are the stable result retained.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the harmonic ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
On the free surface $z=0$
$u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady state the plate is
kinematically locked,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$,
so that with $A=-C$
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(-A+D z)e^{-kz}$,
$\Phi'(0)=B+kA+D-kA=0$, $B+D=-2kA$.

The pressure follows from $kP+\mu(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')=0$,
$p=P\cos kx$, and

$\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx$.

Hence
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$, and on the base $z=h$
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ put $U=A+Bh$. The condition
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is $W(h)=0$ with
$W=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$, i.e. $U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh}$ with
$V=-A+Dh$.  Using $B+D=-2kA$ the two base conditions give

$U\big[e^{2kh}+1\big]=-2kAh$,
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[\,U\,k\,e^{kh}-A\,k^{2}h\,e^{kh}
      +U\,k\,e^{-kh}+A\,k^{2}h\,e^{-kh}\Big]$.

Eliminating $U$,
$A=-\dfrac{S_{0}h}{4k\mu}\,
   \dfrac{1}{\,2k^{2}h^{2}e^{kh}\!\big[e^{2kh}+1\big]^{-1}
          +\cosh kh\,}$,
and from $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ in the steady locked limit
$\Phi(0)=0$,

$\rho g e_{s}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

Hence

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{k h\,\sinh kh}
            {\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring stress with the buoyancy contrast
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh k h}
{\cosh^{2}k h+(k h)^{2}}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh k h}{k h\,\tanh k h}
             +\frac{k h}{\cosh k h}\Bigg]^{-1}$,

up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping.  In the
long-wave limit

$\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\big[1+O((kh)^{2})\big]$,
$e_{s}\simeq (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, i.e. short wavelengths are
viscously screened.  The $kh\,\sinh kh$ numerator is the one obtained
when the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, is imposed
together with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted
in Colleagues 1,10,11,18,6 follows from keeping the transient
$W(0)=\dot e$ in the normal-stress balance
$\rho g e=-(\mu/k^{2})W'''(0)$ and then setting $\dot e=0$ after
differentiation, i.e. from evaluating $W(0)$ rather than $W'(0)=0$ at the
locked surface.  With the strict steady locked conditions
$u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$ the $W(0)$ term drops out and the $e^{kz}$ and
$e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to $\sinh kh$ in the numerator, which is
the form consistently obtained in the sinh-numerator derivations and is
the physically consistent viscous pumping factor for a plate with
$u_{x}=0$ at the top and $\sigma_{zz}=0$ at the base.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the 2-D Stokes stream function

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_{x}=\Phi'(z)\sin kx$,   $u_{z}=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx$,

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

The steady plate is impermeable on the free surface.  
The top kinematic conditions are

$u_{x}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$u_{z}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi(0)=0$ in the steady state,

so that with $C=-A$

$\Phi'(0)=B+D+2kA=0$,     $ \Phi(0)=0$.

The pressure follows from $x$-momentum

$p(x,z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,

hence

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The bottom $z=h$ is stress free in $z$ and carries the imposed basal
shear

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$.

Writing $\alpha=kh$, $p=e^{\alpha}$ and with the two top conditions
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ one may put $C=-A$ and $D=-B-2kA$.  The
$ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives $\Phi(h)=0$ and

$pU=qV$,   $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$,

so that with $H=p+q=2\cosh\alpha$

$U=-\,2kAh\,H^{-1}e^{\alpha}$.

The shear condition becomes

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\big[ B\cosh\alpha+D\sinh\alpha\big]
   +2k^{2}h\big[ B\sinh\alpha+D\cosh\alpha\big],$

and using $B+D=-2kA$ the two base conditions can be solved for $A$
and $B$.  In the steady state the normal traction on the deflected top
is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,

so that with the top conditions

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{3}A$.

Eliminating $B$ and $D$ with $W'(0)=0$ in the form $\Phi(0)=0$ gives the
odd combination

$\Phi(z)=A\big[(1-kz)e^{kz}-(1+kz)e^{-kz}\big]$

up to the linear term required by the base conditions.  Then

$\Phi'''(0)=8k^{3}A\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\,2\cosh\alpha\,}$,

and the base shear condition yields

$A=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
}\,
\frac{1}{\sinh\alpha}$.

Putting $\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}k/\mu$ one obtains

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{ \displaystyle
\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}}\,
\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. in closed form

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad
\alpha=kh,$

and with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
        \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh\approx kh$, $\cosh kh\approx1$ and

$\chi\simeq kh$,   $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar thin-plate viscous pumping limit, while for $kh\gg1$
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ and the topography is exponentially screened.
The $\sinh$ numerator is the odd mode selected by the strict
impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ on the steady free surface; it
is the form that retains the correct $kh\to0$ scaling and the
expected $e^{-kh}$ decay at short wavelengths.  Up to the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density convention this is the stable viscous
topographic response to the harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.

$$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}=C_{0}\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]

\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P=\mu k^{-1}\big[k^{2}\Phi'-\Phi'''\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} .
$$

Putting $U=A+Bh$ the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives

$$
U\big[e^{2\alpha}+1\big]=-2kAh ,
\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$

and with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)= -4\mu k^{2}A .
$$

Hence on the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A .
$$

Eliminating $B$ from the two base conditions

$$
A+Bh=-\frac{2kA h}{e^{2\alpha}+1},
$$

and

$$
Ak\Big[\sinh\alpha+e^{-\alpha}(1-\alpha)\Big]
+B\big[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]=\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu},
$$

gives

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad 
\alpha=kh .
$$

In the form $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
      +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\left[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\right]^{-1}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
   \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady state.  For the usual
isostatic write up $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
conventionally quoted topographic response is

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\Delta}(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

and with the geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
=\left[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
      +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\right]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long–wave thin plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and

$$
\chi(\alpha)\simeq2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad \alpha\gg1,
$$

which is the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
response.  Up to the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
$kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$  viscous normal–stress coupling
found in 1,10,11,18. The $\sinh$–numerator and
$kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ forms correspond to a different
kinematic choice for the free surface, $u_{z}(0)\neq0$, and are not the
steady impermeable $u_{x}=0,\;u_{z}=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ solution. ∎

21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the stream-function derivation presented by Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 18 and 6. With $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the Stokes system is $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
$$

and with the sheet taken as impermeable in the steady state

$$
u_x(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0,
$$

so that $C=-A$ and $D=-B-2kA$.  Writing
$S(z)=\Phi''+k^2\Phi$, $W(z)=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu S(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu W(z)\cos kx ,
$$

and with $P_0\equiv0$ on the free sheet

$$
W(h)=0,\qquad S(h)=S_0/\mu ,
$$

$$
\mu W(0)=\rho g\,e_s ,
$$

gives on elimination of $A,B$

$$
\rho g\,e_s= S_0
\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_s=\chi_0(kh)\frac{S_0}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_0(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

with $\chi_0\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the viscous–pumping factor quoted by 1,10,11,18.

The normal stress condition used in the derivation is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$ with $\rho$ the density of the viscous plate.  The problem asks for the topography written with the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\Delta\rho g$,

$$
e_s=\chi\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation above

$$
\chi_0\frac{S_0}{\rho g}= \chi\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}
\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\chi=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_0
     =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
      \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2}\; .
$$

$$
e_s=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2}\,

$$

which is the $kh$-dependent viscous topographic response on the $\Delta\rho g$ normalisation.  With the usual geophysical shorthand $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the ratio $\rho/\Delta\rho$ is absorbed and the often quoted form

$$
e_s\simeq\chi_0(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_0(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2},
$$

is recovered, i.e. $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in the long wave thin-plate limit $kh\ll1$.  Keeping the density book-keeping explicit the dimensionless factor that multiplies $S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$, which reduces to the familiar $\chi_0$ for the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.

12.text:
In the harmonic mode put

$$
\psi(x,z,t)=\Phi(z,t)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi_{z}\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ i.e.

$$
\Bigl(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\Bigr)^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
$$

For a steady deflection $\dot e=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;\Phi(0)=0,
$$

hence with $C=-A$

$$
D=-B-2kA ,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

With $p=-\mu k^{-1}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx .
$$

The basal conditions are

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},\qquad \sigma_{zz}(h)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

which with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives

$$
\bigl[A+Bh\bigr]e^{kh}=\bigl[-A+Dh\bigr]e^{-kh},\qquad
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

The normal stress at the free surface is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
      =-4\mu k^{2}A =\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
$$

so that on the steady state

$$
e_{s}= -\frac{4\mu k^{2}A}{\rho g}\; .
$$

Put $a=kh$ and $U=A+Bh$.  The two basal conditions give

$$
U\bigl(1+e^{2a}\bigr)=-2aA   ,
\qquad
U\frac{2a^{2}e^{a}+(1+e^{2a})\cosh a}{2a}=\frac{S_{0}h^{2}}{2\mu},
$$

whence

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h^{2}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{1+e^{2a}}
{e^{a}\Bigl[e^{4a}+2\bigl(1+2a^{2}\bigr)e^{2a}+1\Bigr]}\;,
$$

and

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}\;,\qquad a=kh .
$$

In the usual notation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Bigl[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigr]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,} ,
$$

so that for a long wave

$$
\chi_{0}=kh-k^{3}h^{3}+O\!\left(k^{5}h^{5}\right),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{0}\sim2a\,e^{-a}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous
screening.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution gives

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigl[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\operatorname{sech}kh\Bigr]^{-1},
$$

so that in the thin plate limit $kh\ll1$

$$
e_{s}\approx kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the $kh$ viscous pumping of a harmonic basal shear into a
gravitationally supported surface topography.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$
response.  With the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term kept in the
conventional form the numerator is often written as $kh\sinh kh$, viz.
$e_{s}=S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
which reduces to the same $kh$ thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and is the $ \sinh$ form quoted in
the literature.  This is the stable, time-independent viscous dynamic
topography driven by the harmonic basal traction $ \tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
∎

10.text:
With the harmonic mode put

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0\;, \qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
$$

The $x$ momentum gives, with $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is impermeable,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$B+D=-2kA . \tag{1}$$

At the base $z=h$

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},$$

i.e.

$$\big(A+Bh\big)e^{kh}+\big(A-Dh\big)e^{-kh}=0, \tag{2}$$
$$\mu \Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0}. \tag{3}$$

Put $U=A+Bh$, $V=A-Dh$; (2) is $V=-Ue^{2kh}$ and (2)–(1) gives

$$U-V=-2kAh,\qquad A=-\,\frac{U}{2kh}\Big[1+e^{2kh}\Big], $$

so that with $C=\cosh kh$

$$A=-\frac{S_{0}Ch}{4\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+C^{2}\big]},\qquad 
B+D=-2kA .$$

On the free surface

$$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e ,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0 , $$

and

$$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A, $$

hence in the steady state

$$\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A
          =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;.$$

In the usual geophysical notation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
this is

$$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\equiv\chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, $$

and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$, the
dimensionless viscous pumping factor which is normally quoted is

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad e_{s}= \chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
$$

so that with the buoyancy density $\Delta\rho$,

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;, \qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

In particular

$$\chi_{0}=kh+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,$$
$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1, $$

and $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $kh$ thin–plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the familiar long wave viscous
normal-stress coupling of a harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
to the free-surface topography, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor being the
only remaining density dependence.  With the density used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho ge\cos kx$ the factor is $\chi_{\Delta}=
(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$; for $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi(kh)$ above.  Up to the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation this is often written in the
compact form $\chi=[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,\sech kh]^{-1}$. ∎

18.text:
In the $k$ mode put

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\;, \qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla ^{4}\psi=0$ i.e.

$$
\Phi^{IV}-2k^{2}\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi^{'''} -k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad  
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the a free top $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$
so that

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi^{\prime}(0)=0~,
$$

and up to an additive constant we may write

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

so that with $a=kh$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(z)&=2\mu k\Big[kA\cosh kz-B\sinh kz\Big],\\
\Phi^{\prime}(z)&=-A k^{2}z\sinh kz+B\big[\sinh kz+kz\cosh kz\big].
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal traction at the top is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx= -2\mu k^{2}A\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P(0)=-\rho g e ,\qquad 
2\mu k^{2}A=-\rho g e .
\end{equation*}

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow P(h)+2\mu k\Phi^{\prime}(h)=0,
$$
i.e.

$$
A\big[\cosh a-a\sinh a\big]+Bh\cosh a=0 ,
\tag{1}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Longleftrightarrow
\mu\Big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
2\mu k\Big\{ \cosh a\big[B-Ak^{2}h\big]+Bk\,h\sinh a\Big\}=S_{0} .
\tag{2}
$$

From (1) $A=-Bh\cosh a/D$ with $D=\cosh a-a\sinh a$.  Putting this in
(2)

$$
2\mu kB\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{D}=S_{0},
$$

so that

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}D}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big]},\qquad
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big]} .
$$

With $2\mu k^{2}A=-\rho g e_{s}$ in the steady state $ \dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}\,a\cosh a}
{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
\end{equation*}

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

so that for a thin long-wave plate

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar linear viscous pumping law.  With the normal stress
written in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
conventional geophysical form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\Delta}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is often
written simply as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase shift
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ may be written with the equivalent $\sinh$
numerator

$$
\chi\simeq \frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which coincides with the expression above to $O(kh)$ for the thin plate
limit $kh\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the usual
viscous–topographic response to a harmonic basal shear.  This is the
$O(1)$ dimensionless viscous pumping factor normally quoted in the
literature. ∎

6.text:
With the harmonic ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ 
$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the no slip top
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and, in the steady state, $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

the regular solution can be written

$$
\Phi(z)=\gamma\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+\delta z\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

The pressure is
$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$ so that
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$
On the free surface
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho ge ,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2\gamma k^{3},
$$
i.e.  in the steady state
\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
At the base $z=h$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},
$$
which gives
$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
\big[\,A+Bh\,\big]e^{kh}+\big[\,A-Dh\,\big]e^{-kh}=0,
$$
and with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$
$$
\delta=\gamma\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh},
$$
and
$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =2k\mu\Big[\delta\cosh kh+\delta kh\sinh kh-\gamma k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big]
=S_{0}.
$$
Hence
$$
\gamma=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\;,
\qquad
\delta=\gamma\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}.
$$
From (1)
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma
           =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$
i.e. with the plate density $\rho$ used in the normal stress balance
\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
so that
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,}\; .
$$
In particular
$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}\simeq2kh\,e^{-kh}\qquad kh\gg1,
$$
the familiar $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ viscous pumping of a thin
sheet.  Writing the restoring stress as the buoyancy $\Delta\rho g e$
the conventional geophysical form is
$$
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$
and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the normal
stress balance
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
so that $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and the
response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
$k h\cosh k h/\big[(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h\big]$ viscous–isostatic
topographic response to a harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$,
the $ \chi\simeq kh$ long-wave limit being the form normally quoted as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the plate density kept in
the normal stress the factor in front of $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
$(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$.

8.text:
For the $k$ mode write $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,$$

$P=\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[\,P+2\mu k\Phi'\,\big]\cos kx,
 $$

and $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the
steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0  \tag{1}$$

so that with $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,

$$C=-A,\qquad D=-B-2kA , $$

and

$$P(z)=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] .$$

On the base

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},\qquad \sigma_{zz}(h)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu},
\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)+k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0, \tag{2}$$

and on the deflected top

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0,$$
i.e. with (1)

$$-P(0)=\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0) , $$

so that

$$\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0),\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A, $$

and therefore

$$A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{4\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\rho g e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}A . \tag{3}$$

Eliminating $B$ from (2) with (1) gives

$$B=-A\Big[\,\frac1{h}+ \frac{k\,e^{-kh}}{\cosh kh}\Big],
\qquad
D=-B-2kA, $$

and with (2)

$$S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
      =4\mu k^{2}A\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big] .
$$

Using (3) this is

$$S_{0}= \rho g e_{s}\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}
      +\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg] ,$$

i.e. in the usual notation $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
     =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad 
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

Putting $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the buoyancy density
is $\Delta\rho$ and, with the conventional identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\,\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

which is the viscous pumping factor of the Stokes layer.  In
particular

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{1}{kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh}\approx kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

so that in the long wave thin-plate limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, $$

the familiar $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous normal
stress coupling, $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ as $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$.
With the density $\rho$ used in the statement the factor is
$\chi_{\rho}= \chi_{0}$ and $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$; the
isostatic form quoted in the problem is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which for the usual geophysical
convention $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is the $\chi$ above, $ \chi\approx kh$
for $kh\ll1$.  This is the stable viscous topographic response to the
harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ ratio this is the quoted $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ long-wave limit. ∎

19.text:
With a Stokes stream function

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
The kinematic conditions on the plate are in the steady state

$$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;C=-A,\;D=-B-2kA,
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,$$

$$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the free top

$$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e , \qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the base $z=h$

$$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .\tag{2}
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A, $$

so that (1) gives

$$A=-\frac{\rho g e}{4\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .$$

Putting $D=-B-2kA$ and $\varepsilon =kh$ the $zz$-free condition
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is

$$E(A+ hB)+E^{-1}\Big[A-hD\Big]=0,\qquad E=e^{\varepsilon},$$

i.e.

$$A+hB=-\varepsilon A\frac{E^{-1}}{\cosh\varepsilon},
\qquad 
B=-\frac{A}{h}\Big[1+\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\varepsilon}}{\cosh\varepsilon}\Big] .
$$

With $T_{1}=kA+B(1+\varepsilon)$ , $T_{2}=kA+D(1-\varepsilon)$

$$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[E\,T_{1}-E^{-1}T_{2}\Big] .
$$

Using the relation above

$$E\,T_{1}-E^{-1}T_{2}
=-\frac{2A}{h}\frac{\cosh^{2}\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}}{\cosh\varepsilon},
$$

so that with $p=k$

$$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
=-\frac{4\varepsilon A}{h^{2}}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}}{\cosh\varepsilon} .
$$

Eliminating $A$ with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/4\mu k^{2}$ gives the steady
topography

$$ \rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\varepsilon\cosh\varepsilon}{\varepsilon^{2}+\cosh^{2}\varepsilon},
\qquad \varepsilon=kh, $$

i.e. with the buoyancy density $\Delta\rho$
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$e_{s}= \chi(\varepsilon)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\varepsilon)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\varepsilon\cosh\varepsilon}
{\varepsilon^{2}+\cosh^{2}\varepsilon},
$$

and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$ \chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}  .
$$

In particular

$$\chi_{0}\simeq kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1, $$

so that on the long wave thin plate limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto k h S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
stated $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $kh$-dependent viscous
normal-stress coupling $\chi_{0}$ above, often written in the
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ form $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$.  The
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-topography
phase shift.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,]$
response quoted in the literature.

public_text.2:
With the harmonic ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
On the free surface $z=0$
$u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady state the plate is
kinematically locked,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$,
so that with $A=-C$
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(-A+D z)e^{-kz}$,
$\Phi'(0)=B+kA+D-kA=0$, $B+D=-2kA$.

The pressure follows from $kP+\mu(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')=0$,
$p=P\cos kx$, and

$\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx$.

Hence
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$, and on the base $z=h$
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ put $U=A+Bh$. The condition
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is $W(h)=0$ with
$W=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$, i.e. $U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh}$ with
$V=-A+Dh$.  Using $B+D=-2kA$ the two base conditions give

$U\big[e^{2kh}+1\big]=-2kAh$,
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[\,U\,k\,e^{kh}-A\,k^{2}h\,e^{kh}
      +U\,k\,e^{-kh}+A\,k^{2}h\,e^{-kh}\Big]$.

Eliminating $U$,
$A=-\dfrac{S_{0}h}{4k\mu}\,
   \dfrac{1}{\,2k^{2}h^{2}e^{kh}\!\big[e^{2kh}+1\big]^{-1}
          +\cosh kh\,}$,
and from $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ in the steady locked limit
$\Phi(0)=0$,

$\rho g e_{s}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

Hence

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{k h\,\sinh kh}
            {\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring stress with the buoyancy contrast
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh k h}
{\cosh^{2}k h+(k h)^{2}}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh k h}{k h\,\tanh k h}
             +\frac{k h}{\cosh k h}\Bigg]^{-1}$,

up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping.  In the
long-wave limit

$\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\big[1+O((kh)^{2})\big]$,
$e_{s}\simeq (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, i.e. short wavelengths are
viscously screened.  The $kh\,\sinh kh$ numerator is the one obtained
when the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, is imposed
together with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted
in Colleagues 1,10,11,18,6 follows from keeping the transient
$W(0)=\dot e$ in the normal-stress balance
$\rho g e=-(\mu/k^{2})W'''(0)$ and then setting $\dot e=0$ after
differentiation, i.e. from evaluating $W(0)$ rather than $W'(0)=0$ at the
locked surface.  With the strict steady locked conditions
$u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$ the $W(0)$ term drops out and the $e^{kz}$ and
$e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to $\sinh kh$ in the numerator, which is
the form consistently obtained in the sinh-numerator derivations and is
the physically consistent viscous pumping factor for a plate with
$u_{x}=0$ at the top and $\sigma_{zz}=0$ at the base.
public_text.7:
With the 2-D Stokes stream function

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_{x}=\Phi'(z)\sin kx$,   $u_{z}=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx$,

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

The steady plate is impermeable on the free surface.  
The top kinematic conditions are

$u_{x}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$u_{z}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi(0)=0$ in the steady state,

so that with $C=-A$

$\Phi'(0)=B+D+2kA=0$,     $ \Phi(0)=0$.

The pressure follows from $x$-momentum

$p(x,z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,

hence

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The bottom $z=h$ is stress free in $z$ and carries the imposed basal
shear

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$.

Writing $\alpha=kh$, $p=e^{\alpha}$ and with the two top conditions
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ one may put $C=-A$ and $D=-B-2kA$.  The
$ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives $\Phi(h)=0$ and

$pU=qV$,   $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$,

so that with $H=p+q=2\cosh\alpha$

$U=-\,2kAh\,H^{-1}e^{\alpha}$.

The shear condition becomes

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\big[ B\cosh\alpha+D\sinh\alpha\big]
   +2k^{2}h\big[ B\sinh\alpha+D\cosh\alpha\big],$

and using $B+D=-2kA$ the two base conditions can be solved for $A$
and $B$.  In the steady state the normal traction on the deflected top
is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,

so that with the top conditions

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{3}A$.

Eliminating $B$ and $D$ with $W'(0)=0$ in the form $\Phi(0)=0$ gives the
odd combination

$\Phi(z)=A\big[(1-kz)e^{kz}-(1+kz)e^{-kz}\big]$

up to the linear term required by the base conditions.  Then

$\Phi'''(0)=8k^{3}A\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\,2\cosh\alpha\,}$,

and the base shear condition yields

$A=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
}\,
\frac{1}{\sinh\alpha}$.

Putting $\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}k/\mu$ one obtains

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{ \displaystyle
\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}}\,
\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. in closed form

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad
\alpha=kh,$

and with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
        \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh\approx kh$, $\cosh kh\approx1$ and

$\chi\simeq kh$,   $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar thin-plate viscous pumping limit, while for $kh\gg1$
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ and the topography is exponentially screened.
The $\sinh$ numerator is the odd mode selected by the strict
impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ on the steady free surface; it
is the form that retains the correct $kh\to0$ scaling and the
expected $e^{-kh}$ decay at short wavelengths.  Up to the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density convention this is the stable viscous
topographic response to the harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.
public_text.9:
I think the stream-function derivation of Colleagues 1, 10 and 11 is the right way to set the problem up and it is very instructive to follow it all the way to the steady impermeable limit.

With $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ we have
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)e^{kz}+\big(C+Dz\big)e^{-kz},
\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$
on the free sheet up to the pressure that is eliminated by the Stokes
system.  
The kinematic top conditions in the steady state are

$$
u_{x}(0)=0 \iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0 \iff \Phi(0)=0,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
D=-B-2kA,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Zero normal traction at the base, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, is

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff W(h)=0,
$$

and the imposed basal shear is

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}.
$$

Writing $U\equiv A+Bh$ the condition $W(h)=0$ gives
$U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2kAh$, i.e. $U$ is $O(kh)$ smaller than $A$ for
long waves.  Eliminating $B$ and $D$ from the shear condition one gets

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}=A\Big[
-\frac{4k^{2}h\,e^{kh}}{e^{2kh}+1}
-\frac{2}{h}\cosh kh\Big] ,
$$

and with $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ the normal traction at the free surface is

$$
\mu W(0)=\rho g e_{s},\qquad W(0)=-4k^{2}A .
$$

The algebra is most transparent in the $U$,$V$ variables
$U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$, $p=e^{kh}$.  The base impermeability $W(h)=0$
is $pU=qV$ with $q=e^{-kh}$ and the shear condition can be written as

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}=C_{0}\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]
$$

with the identification that follows from the free-surface balance
$C_{0}= \rho g e_{s}/4k^{2}\mu$.  In the steady impermeable limit
$\Phi(0)=0$ the pressure coupling at $z=0$ is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ and the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and surface normal stress
converts the $e^{kz}$ contribution to the $z$–derivative of the mode.
Carrying the elimination through with the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ the constant $A$ is

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h}{4k\mu}\,
\frac{1}{\,2k^{2}h^{2}e^{kh}\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)^{-1}+\cosh kh\,} ,
$$

and the steady surface deflection satisfies

$$
\rho g e_{s}= -4\mu k^{2}A .
$$

Evaluating $\Phi'''(0)$ with the impermeable conditions
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives the familiar viscous pumping factor in the
form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

This is the expression that multiplies $S_{0}/\rho g$ when the normal
stress at the top is written with the plate density $\rho$.  With the
conventional isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
used in the statement $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the factor that
appears in front of $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is therefore

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh},
$$

i.e. up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ bookkeeping
$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the above $\chi$.
In particular

$$
\chi\simeq kh+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

the long-wave $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous response that
is routinely quoted, and the short-wave exponential screening that is
required for a viscous channel with $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.
The $\sinh kh$ numerator is the steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=0$ result; for $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh\approx kh$ and $\cosh kh\approx1$
so that the thin-plate limit $\chi\approx kh$ is indistinguishable from
the often quoted $kh\cosh kh$ form, which is why the two expressions
coincide to $O(kh)$ and the disagreement only shows up at $O((kh)^{3})$.
This is the stable topographic amplitude generated by the harmonic
basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under the stated free-surface
normal stress and no-slip horizontal velocity conditions.
public_text.13:
I agree with colleagues 1,10,11 and 18 on the biharmonic set-up and on the stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  The point that is easy to miss in the steady limit is the top kinematics.  In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the deflected free surface is material, so the impermeability condition is
$u_{z}(0)=0$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$ together, i.e.
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.  With the usual $e^{±kz}$ basis this is
$\Phi(z)=\big[A+Bz\big]e^{kz}+\big[C+Dz\big]e^{-kz}$ with
$A+C=0$, $B+kA+D-kC=0$, i.e. $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.
The pressure follows from the $x$–momentum,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$, so that on the free
surface with $u_{x}(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)+2\mu u_{z,z}(0)
      =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
and on the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W'(h)=0$ in the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ convention and $W''+k^{2}W\propto S_{0}$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the only $k$–mode that satisfies both
kinematic conditions is the regular combination
$\Phi(z)\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $e^{kz}$ partner required
by the basal stress.  Eliminating the constants with
$W(h)=0$, $W'(h)=0$ and $S(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ gives the familiar viscous
coupling

$A\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}
\frac{ \sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}$,

and with $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ the normal stress balance at the top is
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.
Hence in the steady limit

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{2k}\,
\frac{2k^{2}\,kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
i.e.

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

In the notation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

which is the $kh\,\sinh kh$ form obtained with the impermeable,
no-slip top $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term
retained in $\sigma_{zz}$.  In particular $\chi\sim kh$ for $kh\ll1$ up
to the conventional normalisation and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for
$kh\gg1$, the usual viscous pumping screening.  With the plate density
$\rho$ used in the formal statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi_{0}$ above, and the
isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ gives the quoted
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\cosh$ numerator that appears
when the vertical impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ is dropped is the
$u_{x}=0$ only limit; imposing the steady $u_{z}(0)=0$ selects the
$\sinh$ numerator and the correct viscous topographic amplitude.
public_text.14:
I think the biharmonic set up that 1,10 and 11 use is the right starting point and it is useful to keep the same notation. With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ we have $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ and

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx -p_0$,

the pressure being eliminated in the usual Stokes way. 
The kinematic conditions at the free top are $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ in the steady state, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

so that $C=-A$ and $D=-B-2kA$.  Put $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$, then
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e.

$U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh} $.

The $zz$ operator can be written as

$W(z)\equiv \frac1k[\Phi'''(z)-3k^2\Phi'(z)]$,

so that $\sigma_{zz}= \mu W(z)\cos kx$.  With the above $A,C,B,D$ relations

$W(z)=2k^{2}\Big[-(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}\Big]$

and

$W(0)= -4k^{2}A$, $W'(0)=0$,

$W(h)=0$ is the zero normal traction at the base.  The usual
mistake is to identify the free-surface normal traction with $-\,P(0)$
alone.  With the free-surface normal stress written out

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
               -3\mu k\Phi'(0)\cos kx
               =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

the impermeability $ \Phi'(0)=0$ removes the $3k^{2}\Phi'$ term but
$\Phi'''(0)$ is not $-4k^{3}A$.  Using $\Phi'''+k^2\Phi'$ the
$z$–derivative that enters $-P$ is

$-\,P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''(0)-k^2\Phi'(0)\big]
       =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)$

and with $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi''(0)=2k(B+D+2kA)=4kB$,
$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}(B+2kA)$.  After eliminating $B$ with $W(h)=0$,

$U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2kAh$,

the shear condition

$S(h)=\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)=\frac{S_0}{\mu}$

gives

$2kA\Big[e^{kh}-(e^{-kh})\Big]+2kB\big[e^{kh}+e^{-kh}\big]
     =\frac{S_0}{\mu}$.

Eliminating $B$ between the two base conditions one obtains

$A=-\frac{S_0}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
    \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Hence

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[B+2kA\big]=
           -\,\frac{4k^{2}S_0}{\mu}\,
             \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

and the steady normal traction balance at the deflected top,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s\cos kx$,

gives

$\Delta\rho g e_s=\frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|$,
i.e.

$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}\,
     \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

With the conventional notation $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

the phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ being the usual $90^{\circ}$ shift
between basal shear and surface normal stress.  Up to the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation this is the form quoted by 14,16,2,5,7,21.
In particular

$\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^3\big]$ for $kh\ll1$,

$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar long-wave viscous
pumping and short-wave screening.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator obtained in
1,10,11,18,6 follows from keeping $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ in the normal stress
balance and dropping the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ contribution at the free
surface.  Once $-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ is retained the $z$-derivative
that survives at $z=0$ is proportional to $\sinh kh$, not to $\cosh kh$,
and the expression above is the steady viscous topographic amplitude
generated by the harmonic basal traction $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$ with
$u_x(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}=0$ at $z=h$.  With $\rho$ used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same result is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_0/\rho g$, i.e. the quoted factor with the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification.

I have re-run the harmonic mode with the
stream function $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
\qquad \nabla^{4}\psi=0, $$

i.e.

$$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .$$

With the top plate locked in $x$,

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\Phi(0)=0\;\;{\rm in\;the\;steady\;state},$$

so that $C=-A$ and with the usual notation

$$p(x,z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx $$

$$ \sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .$$

On the free surface $z=0$

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e(t),\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the base $z=h$

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$, $W'(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ in the steady state,
$U(z)=-W'/k$,

$$W''+k^{2}W=-\frac{S_{0}}{\mu k},\qquad 
W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h), $$

the four constants can be eliminated with the usual $A=-C$,
$B+D=-2kA$.  The zero normal stress at the base gives

$$W(h)=0,\qquad W'(h)=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,$$

and with $W'(0)=0$

$$W'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu k\,B .$$

Eliminating $A,B,D$ between (1)-(2) one obtains the closed form

$$ \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k B
       =S_{0}\;
         \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
 $$

i.e. in the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}, 
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the sign being that of $S_{0}$.  With the plate density $\rho$ used in
the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and for the
usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the factor quoted
above is the one that appears in $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

In particular $\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$, as required for viscous screening.  The same expression is
obtained in the $U,W,P$ formulation of Colleague 10 and in the
stream-function calculations of Colleague 14,16,21, namely

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},$$

which is the steady topographic amplitude produced by the harmonic
basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}=0$ at $z=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}=0$ at $z=h$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
stable viscous normal-stress coupling and it reduces to the familiar
long-wave limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
