With the harmonic stream function
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0 ,
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad 
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 .
$$

For the steady impermeable free surface

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
D=-B-2kA .
$$

On the $z$ -free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
         =\rho g e(t)\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P=\mu k^{-1}\big[k^{2}\Phi'-\Phi'''\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} .
$$

Putting $U=A+Bh$ the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives

$$
U\big[e^{2\alpha}+1\big]=-2kAh ,
\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$

and with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)= -4\mu k^{2}A .
$$

Hence on the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A .
$$

Eliminating $B$ from the two base conditions

$$
A+Bh=-\frac{2kA h}{e^{2\alpha}+1},
$$

and

$$
Ak\Big[\sinh\alpha+e^{-\alpha}(1-\alpha)\Big]
+B\big[\cosh\alpha+\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]=\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu},
$$

gives

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad 
\alpha=kh .
$$

In the form $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
      +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\left[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\right]^{-1}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
   \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady state.  For the usual
isostatic write up $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
conventionally quoted topographic response is

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\Delta}(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

and with the geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
=\left[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
      +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\right]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

so that in the long–wave thin plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and

$$
\chi(\alpha)\simeq2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad \alpha\gg1,
$$

which is the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
response.  Up to the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
$kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$  viscous normal–stress coupling
found in 1,10,11,18. The $\sinh$–numerator and
$kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ forms correspond to a different
kinematic choice for the free surface, $u_{z}(0)\neq0$, and are not the
steady impermeable $u_{x}=0,\;u_{z}=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ solution. ∎

I agree with the stream-function derivation presented by Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 18 and 6. With $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the Stokes system is $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
$$

and with the sheet taken as impermeable in the steady state

$$
u_x(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0,
$$

so that $C=-A$ and $D=-B-2kA$.  Writing
$S(z)=\Phi''+k^2\Phi$, $W(z)=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu S(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu W(z)\cos kx ,
$$

and with $P_0\equiv0$ on the free sheet

$$
W(h)=0,\qquad S(h)=S_0/\mu ,
$$

$$
\mu W(0)=\rho g\,e_s ,
$$

gives on elimination of $A,B$

$$
\rho g\,e_s= S_0
\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_s=\chi_0(kh)\frac{S_0}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_0(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

with $\chi_0\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the viscous–pumping factor quoted by 1,10,11,18.

The normal stress condition used in the derivation is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$ with $\rho$ the density of the viscous plate.  The problem asks for the topography written with the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\Delta\rho g$,

$$
e_s=\chi\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation above

$$
\chi_0\frac{S_0}{\rho g}= \chi\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}
\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\chi=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_0
     =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
      \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2}\; .
$$

In particular

$$
e_s=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2}\,
\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

which is the $kh$-dependent viscous topographic response on the $\Delta\rho g$ normalisation.  With the usual geophysical shorthand $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the ratio $\rho/\Delta\rho$ is absorbed and the often quoted form

$$
e_s\simeq\chi_0(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_0(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2},
$$

is recovered, i.e. $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in the long wave thin-plate limit $kh\ll1$.  Keeping the density book-keeping explicit the dimensionless factor that multiplies $S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$, which reduces to the familiar $\chi_0$ for the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.

In the harmonic mode put

$$
\psi(x,z,t)=\Phi(z,t)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi_{z}\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ i.e.

$$
\Bigl(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\Bigr)^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
$$

For a steady deflection $\dot e=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;\Phi(0)=0,
$$

hence with $C=-A$

$$
D=-B-2kA ,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

With $p=-\mu k^{-1}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Bigr]\cos kx .
$$

The basal conditions are

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},\qquad \sigma_{zz}(h)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

which with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives

$$
\bigl[A+Bh\bigr]e^{kh}=\bigl[-A+Dh\bigr]e^{-kh},\qquad
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

The normal stress at the free surface is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
      =-4\mu k^{2}A =\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
$$

so that on the steady state

$$
e_{s}= -\frac{4\mu k^{2}A}{\rho g}\; .
$$

Put $a=kh$ and $U=A+Bh$.  The two basal conditions give

$$
U\bigl(1+e^{2a}\bigr)=-2aA   ,
\qquad
U\frac{2a^{2}e^{a}+(1+e^{2a})\cosh a}{2a}=\frac{S_{0}h^{2}}{2\mu},
$$

whence

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h^{2}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{1+e^{2a}}
{e^{a}\Bigl[e^{4a}+2\bigl(1+2a^{2}\bigr)e^{2a}+1\Bigr]}\;,
$$

and

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}\;,\qquad a=kh .
$$

In the usual notation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Bigl[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigr]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,} ,
$$

so that for a long wave

$$
\chi_{0}=kh-k^{3}h^{3}+O\!\left(k^{5}h^{5}\right),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{0}\sim2a\,e^{-a}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous
screening.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution gives

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigl[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\operatorname{sech}kh\Bigr]^{-1},
$$

so that in the thin plate limit $kh\ll1$

$$
e_{s}\approx kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the $kh$ viscous pumping of a harmonic basal shear into a
gravitationally supported surface topography.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$
response.  With the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term kept in the
conventional form the numerator is often written as $kh\sinh kh$, viz.
$e_{s}=S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
which reduces to the same $kh$ thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and is the $ \sinh$ form quoted in
the literature.  This is the stable, time-independent viscous dynamic
topography driven by the harmonic basal traction $ \tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In the $k$ mode put

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\;, \qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla ^{4}\psi=0$ i.e.

$$
\Phi^{IV}-2k^{2}\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi^{'''} -k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi^{\prime}\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad  
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the a free top $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$
so that

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi^{\prime}(0)=0~,
$$

and up to an additive constant we may write

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

so that with $a=kh$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(z)&=2\mu k\Big[kA\cosh kz-B\sinh kz\Big],\\
\Phi^{\prime}(z)&=-A k^{2}z\sinh kz+B\big[\sinh kz+kz\cosh kz\big].
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal traction at the top is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx= -2\mu k^{2}A\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P(0)=-\rho g e ,\qquad 
2\mu k^{2}A=-\rho g e .
\end{equation*}

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow P(h)+2\mu k\Phi^{\prime}(h)=0,
$$
i.e.

$$
A\big[\cosh a-a\sinh a\big]+Bh\cosh a=0 ,
\tag{1}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Longleftrightarrow
\mu\Big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
2\mu k\Big\{ \cosh a\big[B-Ak^{2}h\big]+Bk\,h\sinh a\Big\}=S_{0} .
\tag{2}
$$

From (1) $A=-Bh\cosh a/D$ with $D=\cosh a-a\sinh a$.  Putting this in
(2)

$$
2\mu kB\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{D}=S_{0},
$$

so that

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}D}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big]},\qquad
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big]} .
$$

With $2\mu k^{2}A=-\rho g e_{s}$ in the steady state $ \dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}\,a\cosh a}
{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
\end{equation*}

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

so that for a thin long-wave plate

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar linear viscous pumping law.  With the normal stress
written in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
conventional geophysical form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\Delta}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is often
written simply as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase shift
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ may be written with the equivalent $\sinh$
numerator

$$
\chi\simeq \frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which coincides with the expression above to $O(kh)$ for the thin plate
limit $kh\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the usual
viscous–topographic response to a harmonic basal shear.  This is the
$O(1)$ dimensionless viscous pumping factor normally quoted in the
literature. ∎
public_text.6:
With the harmonic ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ 
$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the no slip top
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and, in the steady state, $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

the regular solution can be written

$$
\Phi(z)=\gamma\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+\delta z\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

The pressure is
$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$ so that
$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$
On the free surface
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho ge ,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2\gamma k^{3},
$$
i.e.  in the steady state
\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
At the base $z=h$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},
$$
which gives
$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
\big[\,A+Bh\,\big]e^{kh}+\big[\,A-Dh\,\big]e^{-kh}=0,
$$
and with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$
$$
\delta=\gamma\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh},
$$
and
$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =2k\mu\Big[\delta\cosh kh+\delta kh\sinh kh-\gamma k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big]
=S_{0}.
$$
Hence
$$
\gamma=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
        {2\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\;,
\qquad
\delta=\gamma\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}.
$$
From (1)
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\gamma
           =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$
i.e. with the plate density $\rho$ used in the normal stress balance
\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
so that
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,}\; .
$$
In particular
$$
\chi_{0}\simeq kh\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}\simeq2kh\,e^{-kh}\qquad kh\gg1,
$$
the familiar $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ viscous pumping of a thin
sheet.  Writing the restoring stress as the buoyancy $\Delta\rho g e$
the conventional geophysical form is
$$
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$
and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the normal
stress balance
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
so that $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and the
response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
$k h\cosh k h/\big[(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h\big]$ viscous–isostatic
topographic response to a harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$,
the $ \chi\simeq kh$ long-wave limit being the form normally quoted as
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the plate density kept in
the normal stress the factor in front of $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
$(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$.

For the $k$ mode write $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,$$

$P=\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[\,P+2\mu k\Phi'\,\big]\cos kx,
 $$

and $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the
steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0  \tag{1}$$

so that with $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,

$$C=-A,\qquad D=-B-2kA , $$

and

$$P(z)=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] .$$

On the base

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},\qquad \sigma_{zz}(h)=0,
$$

i.e.

$$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu},
\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)+k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0, \tag{2}$$

and on the deflected top

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0,$$
i.e. with (1)

$$-P(0)=\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0) , $$

so that

$$\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0),\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A, $$

and therefore

$$A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{4\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\rho g e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}A . \tag{3}$$

Eliminating $B$ from (2) with (1) gives

$$B=-A\Big[\,\frac1{h}+ \frac{k\,e^{-kh}}{\cosh kh}\Big],
\qquad
D=-B-2kA, $$

and with (2)

$$S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
      =4\mu k^{2}A\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big] .
$$

Using (3) this is

$$S_{0}= \rho g e_{s}\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}
      +\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg] ,$$

i.e. in the usual notation $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
     =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad 
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

Putting $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the buoyancy density
is $\Delta\rho$ and, with the conventional identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\,\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

which is the viscous pumping factor of the Stokes layer.  In
particular

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{1}{kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh}\approx kh+O(k^{3}h^{3}),
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

so that in the long wave thin-plate limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, $$

the familiar $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous normal
stress coupling, $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ as $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$.
With the density $\rho$ used in the statement the factor is
$\chi_{\rho}= \chi_{0}$ and $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$; the
isostatic form quoted in the problem is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which for the usual geophysical
convention $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is the $\chi$ above, $ \chi\approx kh$
for $kh\ll1$.  This is the stable viscous topographic response to the
harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ ratio this is the quoted $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ long-wave limit. ∎

With a Stokes stream function

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
The kinematic conditions on the plate are in the steady state

$$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;C=-A,\;D=-B-2kA,
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,$$

$$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the free top

$$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e , \qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the base $z=h$

$$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .\tag{2}
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A, $$

so that (1) gives

$$A=-\frac{\rho g e}{4\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .$$

Putting $D=-B-2kA$ and $\varepsilon =kh$ the $zz$-free condition
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ is

$$E(A+ hB)+E^{-1}\Big[A-hD\Big]=0,\qquad E=e^{\varepsilon},$$

i.e.

$$A+hB=-\varepsilon A\frac{E^{-1}}{\cosh\varepsilon},
\qquad 
B=-\frac{A}{h}\Big[1+\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\varepsilon}}{\cosh\varepsilon}\Big] .
$$

With $T_{1}=kA+B(1+\varepsilon)$ , $T_{2}=kA+D(1-\varepsilon)$

$$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[E\,T_{1}-E^{-1}T_{2}\Big] .
$$

Using the relation above

$$E\,T_{1}-E^{-1}T_{2}
=-\frac{2A}{h}\frac{\cosh^{2}\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}}{\cosh\varepsilon},
$$

so that with $p=k$

$$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
=-\frac{4\varepsilon A}{h^{2}}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}}{\cosh\varepsilon} .
$$

Eliminating $A$ with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/4\mu k^{2}$ gives the steady
topography

$$ \rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\varepsilon\cosh\varepsilon}{\varepsilon^{2}+\cosh^{2}\varepsilon},
\qquad \varepsilon=kh, $$

i.e. with the buoyancy density $\Delta\rho$
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$e_{s}= \chi(\varepsilon)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\varepsilon)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\varepsilon\cosh\varepsilon}
{\varepsilon^{2}+\cosh^{2}\varepsilon},
$$

and with the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$ \chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}  .
$$

In particular

$$\chi_{0}\simeq kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1, $$

so that on the long wave thin plate limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto k h S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio this is the
stated $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $kh$-dependent viscous
normal-stress coupling $\chi_{0}$ above, often written in the
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ form $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$.  The
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-topography
phase shift.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/[\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,]$
response quoted in the literature.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic mode is consistently written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.
Then
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
up to the usual $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ convention.
With the steady free surface $u_x(0)=0$, in the steady state $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$, so $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  In the $W(z)=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$ notation
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx$, $W(0)=-4k^2A$, $W(h)=0$.
Elimination of $B,D$ gives
$W(0)=-4k^2A$ and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_{h}=S_0$.
With $U=A+Bh$ the $W(h)=0$ condition is $U e^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and
$U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2kAh$.
Solving,
$A=-\dfrac{S_0h}{4\mu k}\dfrac{{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2}$,
and
$\mu W(0)=\dfrac{S_0kh\,{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2}$.

Hence with the normal stress written with the plate density $\rho$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho g e_{s}= \mu W(0)$,
$$e_{s}= \frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\,{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2}
 =\Big[\frac{{\rm cosh}kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{{\rm cosh}kh}\Big]^{-1}
 =\Big[\frac{{\rm cosh}kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},$$
the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  
$\chi_{0}=kh+O[(kh)^3]$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, i.e. the familiar long-wave viscous pumping $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$.

With the isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
$$e_s=\chi(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2},$$
so that in the thin-plate long wave limit
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

A minority strand in the round re-derives the strict impermeable $u_z(0)=0$ mode with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term kept explicitly in $\sigma_{zz}$ and obtains the formally equivalent $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2+(kh)^2]$ numerator, which coincides with the $kh\cosh kh$ form to $O(kh)$ and reduces to the same thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio is the only remaining bookkeeping difference between the $\rho g$ formulation in the statement and the $\Delta\rho g$ form requested.  The consensus thin-plate result used in the literature is therefore $e_s\approx kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the full $kh$-dependent regularisation $\chi_0$ above. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic mode can be written with a stream function 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
With the steady impermeable free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$,
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $C=-A$, $B+D+2kA=0$.
$x$-momentum gives $p=P(z)\cos kx$ with $P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.
Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$.
Top: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$, and in the steady state $\dot e=0$.

Eliminating $B,D$ with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the two base conditions gives
the usual viscous–pumping relation
$\rho g e_s=S_0\big[\cosh\alpha/\alpha+\alpha/\cosh\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$, i.e.

$\chi_0(\alpha)=\big[\cosh\alpha/\alpha+\alpha/\cosh\alpha\big]^{-1}
      =\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$,
$e_s=\chi_0(\alpha)S_0/\rho g$.

In particular
$\chi_0=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, $e_s\simeq\alpha S_0/\rho g$,
$\chi_0\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar
$kh$ thin-plate viscous coupling and exponential short-wave screening.

With the isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the same Stokes solution gives
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$e_s=\chi(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
          =\big[\cosh\alpha/\alpha+\alpha/\cosh\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$.

The current round repeats this result in Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,
21, etc. A minority derivation keeps the steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term in
$\sigma_{zz}$ in a different normalisation and obtains the equivalent
thin-plate form with a $\sinh\alpha$ numerator,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$,
which coincides with $\chi_0$ to $O(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}= \alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$,
and differs only at $O(\alpha^{3})$. The $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$
discrepancy is a normalisation/phase issue between using
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ vs $ \Phi'''(0)$ with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$
contribution and whether the steady $u_z(0)=0$ condition is imposed
before or after elimination of the pressure constant. The long-wave
limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and the
exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ are robust across all derivations.
The remaining $O(1)$ prefactor differences $1/2,1/4$ quoted by some
colleagues are attributable to the precise top shear/free-surface
normalisation; the functional form
$\chi\propto\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ and the
thin-plate limit $\chi\to kh$ are the stable result retained.
Density bookkeeping: formally $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$;
with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted $\chi$.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 2-D Stokes mode is written with
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$, i.e. $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
With the pressure $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

In the steady state the deflected top is material,
$u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, so $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.
On the base $z=h$
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$,
and on the top
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$.

With $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$ the normal stress balance gives
$\rho g e_s=-4\mu k^2 A$ and the two base conditions give
$\big[A+Bh\big]e^{kh}=\big[-A+Dh\big]e^{-kh}$ and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.  Eliminating $B,D$,
$S_0=\rho g e_s\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\big]$,
i.e. in the $\rho$-normalisation

$e_s=\chi_0(kh)S_0/\rho g$, 
$\chi_0(kh)=\Big[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}
 =\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$,
and the viscosity drops out of the steady response.
In particular
$\chi_0=kh+O((kh)^3)$, $kh\ll1$, 
$\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$, $kh\gg1$, so that
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$ in the thin–long wave limit, the usual
viscous pumping $e_s\propto kh S_0/\rho g$.

With the isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
same Stokes solution is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is quoted as
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]
 =\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\big]^{-1}$,
and $e_s\simeq khS_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh$, for $kh\ll1$.

The majority of colleagues 1,10,11,18,20 give this cosh–numerator
form.  A minority gets the equivalent $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2]$
form.  The discrepancy is the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ contribution in
$\sigma_{zz}$ at the free surface and the strict steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$.  To $O(kh)$ the two forms
coincide, $\sinh kh\simeq kh$, $\cosh kh\simeq1$, and both give the
familiar thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  The
density book-keeping $\rho/\Delta\rho$ is the only remaining
convention; with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the quoted dimensionless
factor is $\chi_0$ above.  The stable steady topographic amplitude is
therefore the $kh$-dependent viscous factor $\chi_0$, viscosity
cancelling, with the long-wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. The steady deflected top is
$u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$ in the steady state, i.e. 
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$. With $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

so that on the free surface with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,

and on the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the regular biharmonic is
$\Phi(z)=c_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+d\,z\sinh kz$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}=\rho g e$, 
$c_{0}=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  The base $zz$ condition gives
$c_{0}\cosh kh+h[d\cosh kh-kc_{0}\sinh kh]=0$,
$d=c_{0}[kh\tanh kh-1]/h$, and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
=-2\mu k c_{0}\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.

Hence

$c_{0}= -S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\,(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$,

and with $c_{0}=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

Thus on the $\rho$-normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0} S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{0}(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
 =[ \cosh kh/kh+kh/\cosh kh]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{0}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$,
the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.

With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
used in the statement $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the same solution
gives

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\Delta}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
the factor normally quoted is

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
        =[ \cosh kh/kh+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh]^{-1}$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

This is the $kh\cosh kh$ form obtained by the majority of the colleagues
in R0 and R1, e.g. Colleagues 1,10,11,18,6,15,20,21,3,4,8.  The
$kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ variant that appears in
Colleagues 13,14,16,2,5,7,17,9 is obtained when the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
term in $\sigma_{zz}$ is kept with a different sign convention or the
steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ is dropped/replaced by $W(0)=\dot e$.
In the strict steady locked limit $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the two forms
coincide to $O(kh)$: $\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, $\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$,
so both give the thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$, and the exponential screening $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The remaining notational issue is the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor.
The statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ but asks for
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Strictly $\chi=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$; with the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
absorption this is $\chi_{0}$ above.  Unresolved is whether the problem
wants the $\sinh$ numerator that follows from keeping $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}
u_{z}$ with the conventional sign, which is numerically identical to the
$\cosh$ form in the $kh\ll1$ thin-plate limit that is normally quoted.

19.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream function mode $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, gives $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

Steady impermeable free surface $u_x(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0\Rightarrow u_z(0)=0$ is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$. With $C=-A$,
$D=-B-2kA$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

Base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_0$.

Eliminating $B,D$ with $W(z)=k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$,
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$, $W(h)=0$, gives

$A=-\dfrac{\rho g e_s}{4\mu k^{2}}$,

and

$S_0=\rho g e_s\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]$.

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_0\frac{S_0}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_0(kh)=\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
      =\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

$\chi_0=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $kh\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$, $kh\gg1$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady response.  This is the viscous
pumping factor quoted by the majority, Colleagues 1,10,11,18,20,21 etc.,
and reproduces the familiar thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$.

With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
used in the statement $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\Delta}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_0$,
and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)$.

The same $kh$-dependence is often written with the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ as the $\sinh$ numerator form
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2]$, which coincides with
$\chi_0$ to $O(kh)$ for $kh\ll1$, i.e. the thin-plate limit
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is robust.  The disagreement in the
round is essentially the $ \cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator and the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping; the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
form with the $kh$ thin-plate limit is the consensus steady viscous
topographic response.  Unresolved is whether the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ should be kept explicitly, which moves the
numerator to $\sinh kh$ in some derivations, but the long-wave scaling
$\chi\approx kh$ and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable
across the derivations.

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic Stokes mode can be written with the stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the steady impermeable,
no-slip top the kinematic conditions are

$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

and the $x$–momentum gives $P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$
so that

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  The free–surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.

With $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, the odd mode can be put in the
regular form
$\Phi(z)=2A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+2\beta z\sinh kz$,
$\beta=B+kA$, whence $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A=\rho g e k/\mu$.
The two base conditions give

$Ak\big(a s_{a}-c_{a}\big)=\beta a c_{a}$,
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=4k\beta\frac{c_{a}-a s_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$,
$a=kh$, $s_{a}=\sinh a$, $c_{a}=\cosh a$,

so that

$\beta=\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu}\frac{c_{a}-a s_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$,
$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu}\frac{a c_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$.

Hence in the $ \rho g$ normalisation

$\rho g e_{s}= -4\mu k^{2}A
      =S_{0}\,\frac{a c_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$,

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

$\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\simeq2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
and
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady state; the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear–to–topography phase shift.

Writing the restoring stress in the geophysical form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution gives

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\equiv\chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}$.

With the usual convention $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

so that in the thin–plate long–wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Keeping the density
book–keeping explicit the factor that multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}$.  The $kh\sinh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+
(kh)^{2}\big]$ form that appears in several of the round-1 papers is the
same expression to $O(kh)$ and corresponds to retaining the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution in the usual way; it reduces to the $kh$ thin–plate limit
quoted above and is the conventional viscous pumping response to the
harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  Up to the
inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ ratio this is the $a\cosh a/( \cosh^{2}a+
a^{2})$ response, i.e. the familiar $e_{s}\propto kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
dynamic topography.

20.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes biharmonic mode is
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
The $x$-momentum gives $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$ and
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.
Top $u_x=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$. In the steady state the deflected plate is
material so $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, hence $C=-A$,
$D=-B-2kA$, and $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff \Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)=S_0/\mu$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ these give $U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh}$ with
$U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$ and the elimination $U(1+e^{2kh})=-2khA$.
The shear condition then yields

$A=-\dfrac{\rho g e_s}{4\mu k^2}$,
$\dfrac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$,

and
$S_0=\rho g e_s\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]$.

Hence on the $\rho$ normalisation
$e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\rho g$ with

$\chi_0(kh)=\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
 =\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$,

$\chi_0=kh+O((kh)^3)$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$,
viscosity cancels in the steady state. With the isostatic
normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the quoted form is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and with the conventional
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\operatorname{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

The current round reproduces this majority result in Colleagues 1,10,11,18,20,
6,8,15,19,21,3,4. A minority set 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9,21-argue for a
$\sinh$ numerator,
$\chi_{\sinh}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2]$, obtained when the
$2\mu\partial_z u_z$ contribution in $\sigma_{zz}$ is kept in the
form $-\!P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ and the steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=0$ is imposed before eliminating the pressure, i.e. a different
kinematic/stress bookkeeping for the free surface. The two forms coincide
to $O(kh)$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit $kh\ll1$, where both give
$\chi\simeq kh$ and $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and both give
exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. The disagreement is essentially the
$\sinh/\cosh$ numerator arising from whether the normal stress at the top
is written as $\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''$ alone or as $-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ with
the steady $u_z(0)=0$ condition applied after elimination of $P$, and the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio. The long-wave thin-plate
limit $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is robust across all derivations. ∎

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the steady impermeable, no-slip top
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, and

$p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

Writing $\Phi(z)=\alpha\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+\beta z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$ is automatic and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
          =\rho g e$,

so that in the steady state

$\alpha=- \rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.

The base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ are
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives

$\beta=-\alpha\Big[\frac1h-k\tanh kh\Big]$,

and

$S_{0}=2\mu k\,T$, $T=\beta c_{h}+k h\beta s_{h}-\alpha k^{2}h c_{h}$,
$c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$.
Eliminating $\beta$,
$T=-\alpha\,(c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2})/h c_{h}$ and

$S_{0}= -2\mu k\alpha\,(c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2})/h c_{h}$.

With $\alpha=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
and $\chi_{0}\simeq kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady response and the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the
usual shear-to-topography phase shift.

Writing the free-surface restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the $\rho g$ in the balance is
replaced by $\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$
book-keeping this is normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\,\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

so that in the thin-plate long-wave limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\;\chi\simeq kh$,

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Keeping the density
explicitly, $e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
i.e. $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$.  With the usual
geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the
$\chi_{0}$ quoted above.  The $kh\sinh kh$ numerator that appears in
several of the $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ derivations with the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term retained is $\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(kh)$ and
reduces to the same long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The disagreement in the literature is the $ \sinh$ vs $\cosh$ numerator
that comes from the precise treatment of the impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$
and of the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution to $\sigma_{zz}$ at the
locked top; the $kh\cosh kh$ form is the one obtained with the strict
steady conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ used by colleagues 1,10,11,18. ∎

18.text:
With the stream function $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0,
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the steady plate $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi^{\prime}(0)=0,\qquad 
C=-A,\qquad D=-B-2kA,
$$

and with $W=-k\Phi$

$$
W(0)=W'(0)=0,\qquad 
W(z)=\alpha\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+\beta z\sinh kz,
$$

$$
\alpha=\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},\qquad
W^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}\alpha .
$$

The free surface normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k^{2}}\big[-W'''(0)\big]
       =2\mu k\alpha =\rho g e_{s},
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow
W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

With $a=kh$

$$
W''+k^{2}W=2k\beta\cosh kz+2kz\big[-k^{2}\alpha\cosh kz
+k\beta\sinh kz\big],
$$

and $W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h)$ gives

$$
\beta=\alpha\Big(k\tanh a-\frac1h\Big),\qquad 
W''+k^{2}W\Big|_{h}= -\frac{2k\alpha}{h\cosh a}
\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big] .
$$

Hence

$$
-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}
\Longleftrightarrow
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \frac{2k\alpha}{h\cosh a}
\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big] .
$$

With $\alpha=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,}
          =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

and the viscosity cancels in the steady state.  On the usual
isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the thin–plate long wave limit

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the harmless
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor this is the $a\cosh a/[ \cosh^{2}a+a^{2}]$
viscous pumping response, often written in the $90^{\circ}$ phase form
$e_{s}\simeq S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+
(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with the above to $O(kh)$ and gives the
familiar $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ thin–plate limit.  With
the density $\rho$ kept in the statement the factor is
$\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ and
$e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$. ∎

reflection_text.4:
The harmonic mode is consistently written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.
Then
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
up to the usual $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ convention.
With the steady free surface $u_x(0)=0$, in the steady state $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$, so $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  In the $W(z)=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$ notation
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx$, $W(0)=-4k^2A$, $W(h)=0$.
Elimination of $B,D$ gives
$W(0)=-4k^2A$ and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_{h}=S_0$.
With $U=A+Bh$ the $W(h)=0$ condition is $U e^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and
$U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2kAh$.
Solving,
$A=-\dfrac{S_0h}{4\mu k}\dfrac{{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2}$,
and
$\mu W(0)=\dfrac{S_0kh\,{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2}$.

Hence with the normal stress written with the plate density $\rho$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho g e_{s}= \mu W(0)$,
$$e_{s}= \frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\,{\rm cosh}kh}{{\rm cosh}^{2}kh+(kh)^2}
 =\Big[\frac{{\rm cosh}kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{{\rm cosh}kh}\Big]^{-1}
 =\Big[\frac{{\rm cosh}kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},$$

reflection_text.10:
The harmonic mode can be taken as $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

Steady top: $u_{x}(0)=0\Rightarrow\Phi'(0)=0$, and for a stationary deflection $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\Rightarrow\Phi(0)=0$.  With $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$,
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

Base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e. $(A+Bh)e^{kh}=(C+Dh)e^{-kh}$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Free surface:
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e(t)$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.
In the steady state $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and $\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

Eliminating $B,D$ with $W(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives
$A=-S_{0}Ch/[4\mu k\,(k^{2}h^{2}+C^{2})]$ with $C=\cosh kh$, and

$\rho g e_{s}= -4\mu k^{2}A=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

In particular $\chi_{0}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $kh\ll1$, 
$\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$, $kh\gg1$, so the long–wave thin-plate limit is
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventionally quoted amplitude is

$e_{s}= \chi_{\Delta}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi_{\Delta}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{0}(kh)$,

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}\approx kh$,

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

The current round shows a split in notation. A majority 1,10,11,18,20,21, etc. obtain the $\cosh$ numerator above. A minority keeps the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term in $\sigma_{zz}$ together with the strict impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and reports the equivalent viscous-pumping form
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
which coincides with the $\cosh$ form to $O(kh)$: $\sinh kh=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$. The difference is only a $O[(kh)^{3}]$ normalisation and the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio. The viscosity cancels in the steady state. The $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and surface normal stress is the standard result.

Unresolved: whether the problem statement intends the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ or the transient kinematic $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term kept in $\sigma_{zz}$. Both reduce to the quoted $kh$ thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, with the full $kh$-dependent regularisation $\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ being the form most often quoted.

reflection_text.11:
The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. The steady deflected top is
$u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$ in the steady state, i.e. 
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$. With $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

so that on the free surface with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,

and on the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the regular biharmonic is
$\Phi(z)=c_{0}[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+d\,z\sinh kz$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}=\rho g e$, 
$c_{0}=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  The base $zz$ condition gives
$c_{0}\cosh kh+h[d\cosh kh-kc_{0}\sinh kh]=0$,
$d=c_{0}[kh\tanh kh-1]/h$, and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
=-2\mu k c_{0}\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.

Hence

$c_{0}= -S_{0}h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\,(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$,

and with $c_{0}=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

Thus on the $\rho$-normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0} S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{0}(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
 =[ \cosh kh/kh+kh/\cosh kh]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{0}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$,
the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.

With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
used in the statement $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the same solution
gives

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\Delta}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
the factor normally quoted is

$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
        =[ \cosh kh/kh+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh]^{-1}$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

This is the $kh\cosh kh$ form obtained by the majority of the colleagues
in R0 and R1, e.g. Colleagues 1,10,11,18,6,15,20,21,3,4,8.  The
$kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ variant that appears in
Colleagues 13,14,16,2,5,7,17,9 is obtained when the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
term in $\sigma_{zz}$ is kept with a different sign convention or the
steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ is dropped/replaced by $W(0)=\dot e$.
In the strict steady locked limit $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the two forms
coincide to $O(kh)$: $\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, $\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$,
so both give the thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$, and the exponential screening $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The remaining notational issue is the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor.
The statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ but asks for
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Strictly $\chi=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$; with the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
absorption this is $\chi_{0}$ above.  Unresolved is whether the problem
wants the $\sinh$ numerator that follows from keeping $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}
u_{z}$ with the conventional sign, which is numerically identical to the
$\cosh$ form in the $kh\ll1$ thin-plate limit that is normally quoted.
reflection_text.19:
The stream function mode $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, gives $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

Steady impermeable free surface $u_x(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0\Rightarrow u_z(0)=0$ is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$. With $C=-A$,
$D=-B-2kA$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

Base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_0$.

Eliminating $B,D$ with $W(z)=k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$,
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$, $W(h)=0$, gives

$A=-\dfrac{\rho g e_s}{4\mu k^{2}}$,

and

$S_0=\rho g e_s\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]$.

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_0\frac{S_0}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_0(kh)=\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
      =\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

$\chi_0=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $kh\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$, $kh\gg1$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady response.  This is the viscous
pumping factor quoted by the majority, Colleagues 1,10,11,18,20,21 etc.,
and reproduces the familiar thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$.

With the isostatic normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
used in the statement $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\Delta}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_0$,
and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)$.

The same $kh$-dependence is often written with the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ as the $\sinh$ numerator form
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2]$, which coincides with
$\chi_0$ to $O(kh)$ for $kh\ll1$, i.e. the thin-plate limit
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is robust.  The disagreement in the
round is essentially the $ \cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator and the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping; the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
form with the $kh$ thin-plate limit is the consensus steady viscous
topographic response.  Unresolved is whether the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ should be kept explicitly, which moves the
numerator to $\sinh kh$ in some derivations, but the long-wave scaling
$\chi\approx kh$ and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable
across the derivations.
