reflection_text.15:
The biharmonic Stokes mode can be written with the stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the steady impermeable,
no-slip top the kinematic conditions are

$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

and the $x$–momentum gives $P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$
so that

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  The free–surface normal stress is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.

With $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, the odd mode can be put in the
regular form
$\Phi(z)=2A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+2\beta z\sinh kz$,
$\beta=B+kA$, whence $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A=\rho g e k/\mu$.
The two base conditions give

$Ak\big(a s_{a}-c_{a}\big)=\beta a c_{a}$,
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=4k\beta\frac{c_{a}-a s_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$,
$a=kh$, $s_{a}=\sinh a$, $c_{a}=\cosh a$,

so that

$\beta=\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu}\frac{c_{a}-a s_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$,
$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4k\mu}\frac{a c_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$.

Hence in the $ \rho g$ normalisation

$\rho g e_{s}= -4\mu k^{2}A
      =S_{0}\,\frac{a c_{a}}{c_{a}^{2}+a^{2}}$,

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$

$\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\simeq2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
and
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady state; the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear–to–topography phase shift.

Writing the restoring stress in the geophysical form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution gives

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\equiv\chi_{\Delta}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}$.

With the usual convention $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

so that in the thin–plate long–wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Keeping the density
book–keeping explicit the factor that multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}$.  The $kh\sinh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+
(kh)^{2}\big]$ form that appears in several of the round-1 papers is the
same expression to $O(kh)$ and corresponds to retaining the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution in the usual way; it reduces to the $kh$ thin–plate limit
quoted above and is the conventional viscous pumping response to the
harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  Up to the
inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ ratio this is the $a\cosh a/( \cosh^{2}a+
a^{2})$ response, i.e. the familiar $e_{s}\propto kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
dynamic topography.
reflection_text.20:
The Stokes biharmonic mode is
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
The $x$-momentum gives $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']\cos kx$ and
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.
Top $u_x=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$. In the steady state the deflected plate is
material so $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, hence $C=-A$,
$D=-B-2kA$, and $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff \Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)=S_0/\mu$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ these give $U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh}$ with
$U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$ and the elimination $U(1+e^{2kh})=-2khA$.
The shear condition then yields

$A=-\dfrac{\rho g e_s}{4\mu k^2}$,
$\dfrac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$,

and
$S_0=\rho g e_s\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]$.

Hence on the $\rho$ normalisation
$e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\rho g$ with

$\chi_0(kh)=\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
 =\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh}$,

$\chi_0=kh+O((kh)^3)$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$,
viscosity cancels in the steady state. With the isostatic
normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the quoted form is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and with the conventional
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\operatorname{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

The current round reproduces this majority result in Colleagues 1,10,11,18,20,
6,8,15,19,21,3,4. A minority set 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9,21-argue for a
$\sinh$ numerator,
$\chi_{\sinh}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2]$, obtained when the
$2\mu\partial_z u_z$ contribution in $\sigma_{zz}$ is kept in the
form $-\!P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ and the steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=0$ is imposed before eliminating the pressure, i.e. a different
kinematic/stress bookkeeping for the free surface. The two forms coincide
to $O(kh)$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit $kh\ll1$, where both give
$\chi\simeq kh$ and $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and both give
exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. The disagreement is essentially the
$\sinh/\cosh$ numerator arising from whether the normal stress at the top
is written as $\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''$ alone or as $-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ with
the steady $u_z(0)=0$ condition applied after elimination of $P$, and the
conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density ratio. The long-wave thin-plate
limit $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is robust across all derivations. ∎
reflection_text.8:
The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the steady impermeable, no-slip top
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, and

$p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

Writing $\Phi(z)=\alpha\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+\beta z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$ is automatic and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
          =\rho g e$,

so that in the steady state

$\alpha=- \rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.

The base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ are
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives

$\beta=-\alpha\Big[\frac1h-k\tanh kh\Big]$,

and

$S_{0}=2\mu k\,T$, $T=\beta c_{h}+k h\beta s_{h}-\alpha k^{2}h c_{h}$,
$c_{h}=\cosh kh$, $s_{h}=\sinh kh$.
Eliminating $\beta$,
$T=-\alpha\,(c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2})/h c_{h}$ and

$S_{0}= -2\mu k\alpha\,(c_{h}^{2}+k^{2}h^{2})/h c_{h}$.

With $\alpha=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
and $\chi_{0}\simeq kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady response and the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the
usual shear-to-topography phase shift.

Writing the free-surface restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the $\rho g$ in the balance is
replaced by $\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$
book-keeping this is normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\,\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

so that in the thin-plate long-wave limit

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\;\chi\simeq kh$,

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Keeping the density
explicitly, $e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
i.e. $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$.  With the usual
geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the
$\chi_{0}$ quoted above.  The $kh\sinh kh$ numerator that appears in
several of the $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ derivations with the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term retained is $\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(kh)$ and
reduces to the same long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The disagreement in the literature is the $ \sinh$ vs $\cosh$ numerator
that comes from the precise treatment of the impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$
and of the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution to $\sigma_{zz}$ at the
locked top; the $kh\cosh kh$ form is the one obtained with the strict
steady conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ used by colleagues 1,10,11,18. ∎
reflection_text.18:
With the stream function $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$,

$$
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0,
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the steady plate $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi^{\prime}(0)=0,\qquad 
C=-A,\qquad D=-B-2kA,
$$

and with $W=-k\Phi$

$$
W(0)=W'(0)=0,\qquad 
W(z)=\alpha\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+\beta z\sinh kz,
$$

$$
\alpha=\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},\qquad
W^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}\alpha .
$$

The free surface normal stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k^{2}}\big[-W'''(0)\big]
       =2\mu k\alpha =\rho g e_{s},
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow
W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

With $a=kh$

$$
W''+k^{2}W=2k\beta\cosh kz+2kz\big[-k^{2}\alpha\cosh kz
+k\beta\sinh kz\big],
$$

and $W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h)$ gives

$$
\beta=\alpha\Big(k\tanh a-\frac1h\Big),\qquad 
W''+k^{2}W\Big|_{h}= -\frac{2k\alpha}{h\cosh a}
\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big] .
$$

Hence

$$
-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}
\Longleftrightarrow
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \frac{2k\alpha}{h\cosh a}
\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big] .
$$

With $\alpha=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{1}{\,kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\,}
          =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

and the viscosity cancels in the steady state.  On the usual
isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the thin–plate long wave limit

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the harmless
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor this is the $a\cosh a/[ \cosh^{2}a+a^{2}]$
viscous pumping response, often written in the $90^{\circ}$ phase form
$e_{s}\simeq S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+
(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with the above to $O(kh)$ and gives the
familiar $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ thin–plate limit.  With
the density $\rho$ kept in the statement the factor is
$\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ and
$e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$. ∎

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the stream function $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the pressure written as
$p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the time independent limit the deflected plate is material. The
horizontal lock is $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'(0)=0$, and the steady
impermeability is $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$.  With
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, so that to leading order the admissible odd mode is

$$
\Phi(z)\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz,
$$

up to the partner required by the base.  In particular

$$
\Phi'''(0)= -4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$

and the zero normal traction at the base is
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e. with $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$,
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the combination that
survives at the top is the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of
$\sigma_{zz}$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}(0)
            =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
$$

and after eliminating $B,D$ with $D=-B-2kA$ and $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ one
obtains

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
    \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

so that

$$
\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[B+2kA\big]
        =-\frac{4k^{2}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
          \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

Hence the steady normal stress balance at the free surface,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$, gives

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|
   = S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. with the conventional isostatic write up $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping that is absorbed in the
definition of the restoring stress.  With $\rho$ kept explicitly in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification
recovers the form quoted above.

In particular

$$
\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

so that in the long wave thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous pumping $e\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and the
short wave response is exponentially screened.  The $\sinh kh$ numerator
is the one selected by the strict steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ at the locked top.  Keeping $W(0)=\dot e$
in the normal stress balance and setting $\dot e\to0$ after
differentiation produces the $\cosh kh$ numerator that appears in the
transient evaluation; imposing $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state removes
the $W(0)$ contribution and leaves the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode
quoted above.  This is the stable, time independent viscous dynamic
topography generated by the harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

3.text:
In the $k$ mode put

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
\qquad (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0, $$

so that with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx , $$

$$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the steady plate $u_{x}(0)=0,\;u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
 $$

$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  On the free surface

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g\,e(t),\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

and on the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}.$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A\cos kx,
$$

so that in the steady state

$$ \rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A . \tag{1}$$

Put $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$.  $\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ is
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$

$$U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh},\qquad B+D=-2kA .$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from

$$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

gives

$$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

and with (1)

$$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad\alpha\equiv kh .
$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
 $$

the viscosity dropping out of the steady response.  In particular

$$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad\chi_{0}\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha},\qquad\alpha\gg1,
 $$

so that for a long wave thin plate

$$e_{s}\simeq\alpha\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar viscous pumping $e\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ and exponential
short wave screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring normal stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      \equiv\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
 $$

i.e. with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
 $$

and in the thin plate limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1, $$

with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and
surface normal stress.  Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density
book-keeping this is the $ \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
viscous–isostatic topographic response.  The $kh\sinh kh$ numerator
obtained with the strict $u_{z}(0)=0$ impermeability is
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
which coincides with the expression above to $O(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, and differs only by the
$\tanh\alpha$ phase factor.  The long wave limit $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,
e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$ are robust.  With the $\rho$ used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ the factor in front of
$S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$; with the usual
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ it is the $\chi_{0}$ quoted above. ∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the harmonic mode $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the Stokes system is
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu u_{z,z}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

In the steady state the deflected top is material, so the impermeable
no-slip conditions are

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$

and $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this gives
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  The normal stress at the surface is then

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

and with the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term kept

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[\,B+2kA\,\big]k$,

i.e. the whole surface traction is carried by the $B+2kA$ combination,
not by the $-4k^{3}A$ that is obtained if $\Phi(0)=0$ is dropped.
Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the base conditions are

$W(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, 
$S(h)\equiv\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$,

together with $W(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$.  Eliminating $A,B$ from
$W(h)=0$, $S(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ gives

$U\equiv A+Bh$,
$U\,e^{kh}=V\,e^{-kh}$ with $V=A-Dh$,
$U-V=-2kAh$,

so that

$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

and with the impermeable top

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[\,B+2kA\,\big]k
=-4k^{3}A\,\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

Hence

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)
 =-4\mu k^{2}A\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}
 =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}$,

in the geophysical normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
so that in the steady limit

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

With the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
        \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

i.e. up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh/kh\to1$ and $\cosh kh\to1$ so that
$\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big)$ and $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the familiar long-wave viscous pumping limit, while
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ as required for viscous
screening.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted in 1,10,11,15,18,20 is the
$u_{x}(0)=0$ only result obtained by dropping the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution in $\sigma_{zz}$ or by evaluating the normal stress with
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before imposing the steady impermeability $W'(0)=0$.
Once the steady material condition $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced
together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, the
$e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to the odd mode
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, and the normal-stress balance at the free
surface selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.  With the plate density $\rho$
kept in $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\rho g$, which reduces to the quoted
thin-plate law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ after the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification.  This is the stable Stokes
topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

11.text:
In the $k$ mode put

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

so that with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the deflected plate is materially locked,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that on the regular biharmonic

$$
\Phi(z)=c_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}
      =\rho g e ,
$$

i.e. $c_{0}=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  With $\alpha =kh$

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
c_{0}\cosh\alpha+h\big[d\cosh\alpha-kc_{0}\sinh\alpha\big]=0,
$$

$$
d=c_{0}\Big[\alpha\tanh\alpha-1\Big]/h ,
$$

and

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-2\mu k c_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}=S_{0}\; .
$$

Hence with $c_{0}=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ in the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
       +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancels out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha},\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

and

$$
e_{s}\simeq \alpha\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping.

Writing the restoring normal stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\Delta}(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\mathrm{sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
 $$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)\to0\;\; \text{exponentially for }kh\gg1 .
$$

Up to the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping this is
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the $kh$ viscous dynamic
topography generated by the harmonic basal traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$
between basal shear and surface normal stress is the usual
shear-to-topography phase shift.  The often quoted $\sinh$ numerator
$kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ differs from the form above only by
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$ and coincides with it to $O(kh)$ in the
thin-plate long-wave limit $kh\ll1$ where $\chi\simeq kh$. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The stream-function form is the right place to be careful about the
topology of the steady state. With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and  $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ .

In the steady locked plate $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

and with the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  The base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, i.e.

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two kinematic conditions are
$W(0)=W'(0)=0$ in the steady state.  The odd regular combination which
satisfies both is

$\Phi(z)=z\,g(z)-\frac{b}{k}\sinh kz$, 
$g(z)=b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz$,

up to the $e^{kz}$ partner required by the basal traction.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ one obtains
$\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}b$ and the free-surface normal traction with the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term kept is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e(t)$,

so that on the steady state $2\mu k b=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$.

The zero normal stress at $z=h$,
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
gives with $a=kh$

$b\cosh a =h\,g'(h)$,
$d=b\bigl[\,a^{-1}-\tanh a\,\bigr]$,

and

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k b\;
\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{a\cosh a}$.

Hence the imposed basal shear is

$2\mu k b\,\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{a\cosh a}=S_{0}$.

Using $2\mu k b=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{a\cosh a}=S_{0}$,

i.e. with the usual phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{a\sinh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,$

up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation.  In the conventional
notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$\chi^{-1}= \dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\;
 \frac{\cosh kh}{\sinh kh}$,

4.text:
In the $k$--mode put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ so that

$$
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\iff \big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,
\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e(t)\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0,\;u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
D=-B-2kA,\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

Put $W(z)=k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''(z)-3k^{2}\Phi'(z)\big]$, $\sigma_{zz}
=\mu W\cos kx$.  Then

$$
W(0)=-4k^{2}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu W(0)=\rho g e_{s},
$$

and on the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff W(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\; .
$$

With $U=A+Bh$ the condition $W(h)=0$ is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$,
$V=C+Dh$, and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

hence

$$
\mu W(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A
      =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

With the normal stress written with the plate density

$$
\rho g e_{s}= \mu W(0), 
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\;kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)\sim 2kh\,e^{-kh},\;kh\gg1,
$$

so that for a thin long–wave plate

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.
Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the long wave thin–plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping this is the
$kh$-dependent viscous normal–stress coupling
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/
\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ in the usual $kh\ll1$ viscous pumping limit.  The
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between the basal shear and the
surface topography is the usual Stokes phase shift.  With the
explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{0}$ is the factor which multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the
statement. ∎

$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

is the one we all use.  The steady, material top is

$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. in the steady state

$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

so that with $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,

$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.

The free-surface normal traction that enters the gravity balance is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ with $\Phi'(0)=0$,

so that on the steady surface

$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$, $\;\;\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$.

At the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W(h)=0$ and
$W'(h)=0$ in the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ convention, and with
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the regular odd mode is

$\Phi(z)\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $e^{kz}$ partner required
by the basal shear.  Eliminating $A,B$ with $W(h)=0$, $W'(h)=0$ and
$S(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ gives

$U=A+Bh$, $V=A-Dh$, $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$, $B+D=-2kA$,

and

$A=-\dfrac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}.$

Hence

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[B+2kA\big]=
-\dfrac{4k^{2}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

and the steady normal-stress balance

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}|\Phi'''(0)|$

is

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. in the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase being the usual
shear-to-topography shift.  Up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$
book-keeping this is $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi_{0}$
above, and with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, 
$\chi\simeq kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$,
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$,

the familiar viscous pumping and exponential screening.  The
$kh\sinh kh$ numerator is the one selected by the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution in $\sigma_{zz}$.  The $kh\cosh kh$ form quoted by
1,10,11,18,6 is obtained if the vertical impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ is
dropped after differentiation of the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ term,
i.e. from evaluating $W(0)$ rather than imposing $W'(0)=0$ at the locked
surface.  In the true steady limit $u_{z}(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$, the
$e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to $\sinh kh$ in the
numerator, which coincides with the cosh form to $O(kh)$ in the long-wave
limit $kh\ll1$ and therefore explains the small-$k$ degeneracy noted
above.  With the density used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. the
quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above once the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification is made. ∎

21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The stream-function set up used by 1,10,11,18 is the right one and it is worth writing it out once in full so the density normalisation is clear.

Put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$. Then
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

and with the steady impermeable/no-slip top
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ we have $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ for
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

On the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e(t)\cos kx$,

$\Phi'(0)=0$,

and on the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$,

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$\rho g e_{s}=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

The two base conditions eliminate $B,D$.  Putting $a=kh$ one gets

$A+Bh=-\dfrac{2kA h}{e^{2a}+1}$, 

and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=4\mu k^{2}A
\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]=S_{0}$,

hence

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
      =\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$,

with $a=kh$.
The viscosity drops out, $\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$ and
$\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$, the familiar long-wave viscous
pumping $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.

That is the Stokes response with the normal stress written as in the
statement, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. with the plate density
$\rho$.  The problem asks for the topography written with the
isostatic restoring buoyancy,

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

where the restoring stress is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation above

$\chi_{0}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}= \chi\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

so that the dimensionless factor that multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is

$\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_{0}(kh)
       =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
         \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
         \Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
           =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\mathrm{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.  In particular with the density kept explicit
in the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ the steady amplitude is
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$, and the factor that appears in the
$\Delta\rho g$ normalisation requested is the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ scaled
form above.  Up to the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ absorption this is
the $kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ viscous normal-stress coupling
generated by the harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the
$90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift, and $e_{s}\simeq kh\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit.

12.text:
With the $k$ mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx , \qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the deflected top is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$, hence

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that, on the $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ basis,

$$
\Phi(z)=P_{0}\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Q_{0}z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
W(z)\equiv\frac1k\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx .
$$

$W(0)=-2k^{2}P_{0}$ and

$$
W(z)=2k^{3}\Big[-P_{0}\cosh kz
+P_{0}kz\sinh kz-Q_{0}z\cosh kz\Big] .
$$

The base conditions

$$
W(h)=0,\qquad \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

give on $a=kh$

$$
Q_{0}=P_{0}\frac{a\sinh a-\cosh a}{h\cosh a},
$$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[-P_{0}k^{2}h\cosh a
+Q_{0}\big(\cosh a+a\sinh a\big)\Big]
=-\frac{2kP_{0}}{h\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big] .
$$

Hence

$$
P_{0}=-\,\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]}\;,
\qquad 
W(0)=-2k^{2}P_{0}.
$$

The normal stress balance at the locked top is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}W(0)=\rho g e_{s}$, i.e.

$$
\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}P_{0}
           =S_{0}\,
             \frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}\;,
\qquad a=kh,
$$

so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity dropping out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that on the long wave thin plate scale

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e.  $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book–keeping the dimensionless viscous
pumping factor is $\chi_{0}=a\cosh a/(a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a)$,
$\chi_{0}\approx kh$ in the thin–plate limit, the stable time
independent topography generated by the harmonic basal traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  With
the strict $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement this is
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the
only remaining density dependence. ∎

8.text:
In the $k$–mode put $\psi (x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P\cos kx-2\mu k\Phi'\cos kx
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the locked top $u_{x}(0)=0$, and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+\beta\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad \Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0 .
$$

Then
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2\alpha k^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
           =\rho g e ,
$$
so that in the steady state

\begin{equation*}
\alpha=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\end{equation*}

With $s_{h}=\sinh kh,\;c_{h}=\cosh kh$ 

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-\alpha k^{2}z c_{h}+ \beta
\big(c+kz s\big)\Big],\qquad 
\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'=2k^{3}\Big[\alpha\big(khz-c\big)
-\beta h c\Big] .
$$

The base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
are

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
\alpha\big(kh s_{h}-c_{h}\big)=\beta h c_{h},
$$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)
      =-2k\alpha\,
        \frac{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}{h c_{h}} .
$$

Hence
$$
\alpha=-\frac{S_{0}h c_{h}}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}\big]},\qquad
\beta=\alpha\,\frac{k h s_{h}-c_{h}}{h c_{h}} .
$$

The free-surface normal stress is therefore

$$
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
           =-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
           =S_{0}\,\frac{k h\,c_{h}}{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
   =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

so that the viscosity drops out of the steady response and the
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift is the usual shear-to-topography
shift.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

i.e. the familiar thin-plate viscous pumping

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\;\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1 .
$$

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution gives

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
      \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the long-wave thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi\simeq kh ,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ being the conventional
shear–to–topography coupling.  Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$
book-keeping this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho
g$, i.e. the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ viscous normal–stress
coupling usually written simply as $e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
for $kh\ll1$ with exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for
$kh\gg1$.  The $\sinh$-numerator form
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ coincides with the
above to $O(kh)$ and reduces to the same long-wave limit
$e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

6.text:
In the $k$ mode
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

\begin{equation*}
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
\end{equation*}
and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'\; \cos kx
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx  .
\end{equation*}
In the steady state the deflected top is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
\end{equation*}
so that with $C=-A$,
$D=-B-2kA$ and, putting $W=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$,

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx,\qquad 
W(0)=-4k^{2}A,\qquad
W(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\end{equation*}
The zero normal traction at the base is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e.

\begin{equation*}
\big[A+Bh\big]e^{kh}=\big[-A+Dh\big]e^{-kh},
\end{equation*}
and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

\begin{equation*}
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
Eliminating $B$ and $D$ from
$W(h)=0$ and $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

\begin{equation*}
A=-\frac{S_{0}h}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}},
\end{equation*}
so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
         =S_{0}\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}
                +\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}
                +\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\end{equation*}
the viscosity dropping out of the steady response.  In
particular

\begin{equation*}
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
\end{equation*}
so that in the long wave thin plate limit

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\end{equation*}
the usual viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress on the deflected free surface in the
geophysical isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$, the same Stokes solution is

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

\begin{equation*}
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Big]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
so that

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)\simeq kh+O\!\left((kh)^{3}\right),\;\;kh\ll1,
\]

i.e. the familiar long wave viscous dynamic topography

\[
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
\]

with the full $kh$ regularisation
$\chi_{0}(kh)=\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh/\cosh kh\big]^{-1}$ and the
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Up to
the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping this is the stable
time independent Stokes topographic response to the harmonic basal
traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the plate density kept
explicit the result is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho
g$, which reduces to the quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  The often quoted odd-mode form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ coincides with the
above to $O(kh)$, $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, and is the $\sinh$ 
numerator obtained when the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution is
kept in the conventional $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ form. ∎

15.text:
In the $k$ mode let

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx , \qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx  
$$

so that $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$.  With
$p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the top is impermeable and $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that on the usual $e^{\pm kz}$ basis
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]
       +\beta z\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2\alpha k^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha\cos kx .
$$

With the normal stress balance written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha  ,
\end{equation*}
and on the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0} .
$$

The zero normal stress gives

$$
\alpha\big[k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=\beta h\cosh kh ,
$$

and the basal shear gives

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =2k\mu\Big[-\alpha k h\cosh kh+\beta\cosh kh
          +\beta k h\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $\beta$,

$$
\beta=\alpha\,\frac{k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh},
\qquad
\alpha=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
           {2k\mu\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]} ,
$$

so that on the free surface

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
       =S_{0}\,
         \frac{k h\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad a\equiv kh .
$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\simeq2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

i.e. for a thin long wave plate

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear–to–topography viscous pumping with the
sign of $S_{0}$.  Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional geophysical
factor is obtained on the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

so that with the strict $\rho g$ normal stress used in the statement

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,
$$

for $kh\ll1$, with the exponential screening
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the stable,
time–independent Stokes topography generated by the harmonic basal
traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book–keeping the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+
\cosh^{2}a]$ viscous pumping response, often quoted in the thin-plate
limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
ratio can be kept explicitly as $\chi_{\Delta}=(\Delta\rho/\rho)
\chi_{0}$; with the geophysical convention $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ it is
the $\chi_{0}$ quoted above. ∎

public_text.2:
With the stream function $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the pressure written as
$p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the time independent limit the deflected plate is material. The
horizontal lock is $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'(0)=0$, and the steady
impermeability is $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$.  With
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, so that to leading order the admissible odd mode is

$$
\Phi(z)\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz,
$$

up to the partner required by the base.  In particular

$$
\Phi'''(0)= -4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$

and the zero normal traction at the base is
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e. with $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$,
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the combination that
survives at the top is the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of
$\sigma_{zz}$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}(0)
            =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
$$

and after eliminating $B,D$ with $D=-B-2kA$ and $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ one
obtains

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
    \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

so that

$$
\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[B+2kA\big]
        =-\frac{4k^{2}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
          \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

Hence the steady normal stress balance at the free surface,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$, gives

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|
   = S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. with the conventional isostatic write up $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping that is absorbed in the
definition of the restoring stress.  With $\rho$ kept explicitly in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification
recovers the form quoted above.

In particular

$$
\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

so that in the long wave thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous pumping $e\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and the
short wave response is exponentially screened.  The $\sinh kh$ numerator
is the one selected by the strict steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ at the locked top.  Keeping $W(0)=\dot e$
in the normal stress balance and setting $\dot e\to0$ after
differentiation produces the $\cosh kh$ numerator that appears in the
transient evaluation; imposing $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state removes
the $W(0)$ contribution and leaves the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode
quoted above.  This is the stable, time independent viscous dynamic
topography generated by the harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎
public_text.3:
In the $k$ mode put

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
\qquad (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0, $$

so that with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx , $$

$$\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the steady plate $u_{x}(0)=0,\;u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
 $$

$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  On the free surface

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g\,e(t),\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

and on the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}.$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A\cos kx,
$$

so that in the steady state

$$ \rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A . \tag{1}$$

Put $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$.  $\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ is
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$

$$U e^{kh}=V e^{-kh},\qquad B+D=-2kA .$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from

$$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

gives

$$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

and with (1)

$$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad\alpha\equiv kh .
$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
 $$

the viscosity dropping out of the steady response.  In particular

$$\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad\chi_{0}\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha},\qquad\alpha\gg1,
 $$

so that for a long wave thin plate

$$e_{s}\simeq\alpha\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar viscous pumping $e\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ and exponential
short wave screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring normal stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      \equiv\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
 $$

i.e. with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
 $$

and in the thin plate limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1, $$

with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and
surface normal stress.  Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density
book-keeping this is the $ \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
viscous–isostatic topographic response.  The $kh\sinh kh$ numerator
obtained with the strict $u_{z}(0)=0$ impermeability is
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
which coincides with the expression above to $O(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, and differs only by the
$\tanh\alpha$ phase factor.  The long wave limit $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,
e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$ are robust.  With the $\rho$ used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ the factor in front of
$S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$; with the usual
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ it is the $\chi_{0}$ quoted above. ∎
public_text.13:
With the harmonic mode $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ the Stokes system is
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu u_{z,z}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

In the steady state the deflected top is material, so the impermeable
no-slip conditions are

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$

and $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this gives
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  The normal stress at the surface is then

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

and with the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term kept

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[\,B+2kA\,\big]k$,

i.e. the whole surface traction is carried by the $B+2kA$ combination,
not by the $-4k^{3}A$ that is obtained if $\Phi(0)=0$ is dropped.
Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the base conditions are

$W(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, 
$S(h)\equiv\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$,

together with $W(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$.  Eliminating $A,B$ from
$W(h)=0$, $S(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ gives

$U\equiv A+Bh$,
$U\,e^{kh}=V\,e^{-kh}$ with $V=A-Dh$,
$U-V=-2kAh$,

so that

$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

and with the impermeable top

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[\,B+2kA\,\big]k
=-4k^{3}A\,\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

Hence

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)
 =-4\mu k^{2}A\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}
 =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}$,

in the geophysical normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
so that in the steady limit

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

With the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
        \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

i.e. up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh/kh\to1$ and $\cosh kh\to1$ so that
$\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big)$ and $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the familiar long-wave viscous pumping limit, while
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ as required for viscous
screening.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator quoted in 1,10,11,15,18,20 is the
$u_{x}(0)=0$ only result obtained by dropping the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution in $\sigma_{zz}$ or by evaluating the normal stress with
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before imposing the steady impermeability $W'(0)=0$.
Once the steady material condition $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced
together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, the
$e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to the odd mode
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, and the normal-stress balance at the free
surface selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.  With the plate density $\rho$
kept in $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\rho g$, which reduces to the quoted
thin-plate law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ after the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification.  This is the stable Stokes
topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎
public_text.11:
In the $k$ mode put

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

so that with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the deflected plate is materially locked,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that on the regular biharmonic

$$
\Phi(z)=c_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}
      =\rho g e ,
$$

i.e. $c_{0}=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  With $\alpha =kh$

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
c_{0}\cosh\alpha+h\big[d\cosh\alpha-kc_{0}\sinh\alpha\big]=0,
$$

$$
d=c_{0}\Big[\alpha\tanh\alpha-1\Big]/h ,
$$

and

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-2\mu k c_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}=S_{0}\; .
$$

Hence with $c_{0}=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ in the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
       +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancels out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha},\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

and

$$
e_{s}\simeq \alpha\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping.

Writing the restoring normal stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\Delta}(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\mathrm{sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
 $$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(kh)\to0\;\; \text{exponentially for }kh\gg1 .
$$

Up to the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping this is
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the $kh$ viscous dynamic
topography generated by the harmonic basal traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$
between basal shear and surface normal stress is the usual
shear-to-topography phase shift.  The often quoted $\sinh$ numerator
$kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ differs from the form above only by
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$ and coincides with it to $O(kh)$ in the
thin-plate long-wave limit $kh\ll1$ where $\chi\simeq kh$. ∎
public_text.7:
The stream-function form is the right place to be careful about the
topology of the steady state. With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and  $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ .

In the steady locked plate $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

and with the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  The base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, i.e.

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_{0}/\mu$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two kinematic conditions are
$W(0)=W'(0)=0$ in the steady state.  The odd regular combination which
satisfies both is

$\Phi(z)=z\,g(z)-\frac{b}{k}\sinh kz$, 
$g(z)=b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz$,

up to the $e^{kz}$ partner required by the basal traction.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ one obtains
$\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}b$ and the free-surface normal traction with the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term kept is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e(t)$,

so that on the steady state $2\mu k b=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$.

The zero normal stress at $z=h$,
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
gives with $a=kh$

$b\cosh a =h\,g'(h)$,
$d=b\bigl[\,a^{-1}-\tanh a\,\bigr]$,

and

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k b\;
\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{a\cosh a}$.

Hence the imposed basal shear is

$2\mu k b\,\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{a\cosh a}=S_{0}$.

Using $2\mu k b=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}}{a\cosh a}=S_{0}$,

i.e. with the usual phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{a\sinh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,$

up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation.  In the conventional
notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$\chi^{-1}= \dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\;
 \frac{\cosh kh}{\sinh kh}$,

which is the odd $W'(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ mode selected by the strict
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
In particular

$\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big]$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$kh\ll1$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous screening.
Writing the normal stress with the plate density $\rho$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, the same result is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $e_{s}=
\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{0}$ above, and with the geophysical
identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $kh\sinh kh$ numerator.
The $\cosh kh$ numerator obtained by keeping only $u_{x}(0)=0$ and
evaluating $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ corresponds to the transient $W(0)=\dot e$
term.  Once the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ is imposed the
$e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to $\sinh kh$ in the numerator,
and the thin-plate limit $e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is preserved.
This is the steady viscous topographic amplitude generated by the
harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎

and on the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff W(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\; .
$$

With $U=A+Bh$ the condition $W(h)=0$ is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$,
$V=C+Dh$, and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

hence

$$
\mu W(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A
      =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\; .
$$

With the normal stress written with the plate density

$$
\rho g e_{s}= \mu W(0), 
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{0}(kh),\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(kh)=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\;kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)\sim 2kh\,e^{-kh},\;kh\gg1,
$$

so that for a thin long–wave plate

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.
Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the long wave thin–plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping this is the
$kh$-dependent viscous normal–stress coupling
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{0}=kh\cosh kh/
\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ in the usual $kh\ll1$ viscous pumping limit.  The
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between the basal shear and the
surface topography is the usual Stokes phase shift.  With the
explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{0}$ is the factor which multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the
statement. ∎
