Following the harmonic stream-function set-up of Colleagues 1,10,11,18 the mode can be written

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

In the steady state the deflected material top is impermeable and has
no slip

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,$

so that with $C=-A$

$D=-B-2kA$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ up to the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of
$\sigma_{zz}$.  On the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx$,

and on the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Put $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and with
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$U-V=-2kAh$.

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W(h)=0$,
$W'(h)=0$ in the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ convention and
$S(h)=S_{0}/\mu$ with $S=\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi$.  Elimination of $B,D$ with
$D=-B-2kA$ gives

$U\,[\,e^{2kh}+1\,]=-2khA$,

and

$\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=4\mu k^{2}A\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\cosh kh}
+4\mu kB\,\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

With $W(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$ the regular odd combination which satisfies the
steady impermeability is the $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  The
$z$-derivative that enters the free-surface normal stress is then the
one proportional to $\sinh kh$ and not to $\cosh kh$.  After elimination

$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

and with $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$

$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)= \frac{S_{0}\,kh\,\sinh kh}
{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Hence on the steady state

$\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}\,kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

With the isostatic restoring stress written as in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the usual geophysical
normalisation is

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
        \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

In particular

$\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,$
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$,

the familiar viscous pumping screening.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping this is
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
$\chi_{0}$ normally quoted as $kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
the two forms being identical to $O(kh)$ in the thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and differing only by the
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh$ phase factor that is generated by the strict
steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the retention of the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term in $\sigma_{zz}(0)$.  This is the
stable time-independent topography generated by the harmonic basal
traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎
public_text.5:
With $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx $ the Stokes system is
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$
In the steady state the deflected top is a material surface,
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$.  Hence
$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$
i.e. $C=-A$ and $B+D=-2kA$.  The pressure that enters the normal
traction is therefore
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,
$$
so that on the steady state
$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0 .
\tag{1}
$$
At the base $z=h$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$
Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W(h)=0$ and
$W''(h)+k^{2}W(h)=-S_{0}/\mu k$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the
regular odd mode can be written as
$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[e^{kz}-e^{-kz}\big]+zB\big[e^{kz}+e^{-kz}\big],
$$
so that
$$
\Phi'''(0)=4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\Phi'(h)=2kA\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]
        +2B\big[\sinh kh+kh\cosh kh\big],
$$
$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=4k^{2}A\cosh kh+4kB\sinh kh .
$$
The $zz$-free condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$$
\big[A+Bh\big]e^{kh}=\big[-A+Dh\big]e^{-kh},
\qquad D=-B-2kA,
$$
i.e. with $U=A+Bh$
$$
U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2kAh .
\tag{3}
$$
Eliminating $B$ between (2) and (3) one obtains
$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=4k^{2}A\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh kh} .
$$
In particular
$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
   \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\tag{4}
$$
and with (1)
$$
\Phi'''(0)=4k^{3}A=
-\frac{4k^{3}S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}
   \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$
so that in the steady limit $\dot e=0$
$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|
     =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$
Hence with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh},
$$
i.e.
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}  ,
$$
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ being the usual
shear-to-normal stress shift.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\sinh kh=kh+O((kh)^{3})$ and $\cosh kh=1+O((kh)^{2})$, so that
$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O((kh)^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar long-wave viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
For $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, the expected viscous screening.

This is the $W(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$ impermeable, no-slip top result.
The $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term is retained in
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$; with $\Phi'(0)=0$ it is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ and the steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=0$ selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.  The $\cosh kh$ numerator
quoted in 1,10,11,18 is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only limit, i.e. the
$W(0)\neq0$ transient form. Once the steady material condition
$u_{z}(0)=0$ is imposed the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine
to $\sinh kh$, and the viscous normal-stress coupling is the
$kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ factor above.  With the plate
density $\rho$ used in the formal statement
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which reduces to the
usual geophysical form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ on the
conventional identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  Up to the harmless
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping this is the stable time independent
dynamic topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with a
kinematically locked, impermeable free surface. ∎
public_text.16:
With the harmonic mode put $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx , $$

so that $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  In the $k$ mode
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ and with the Stokes relations

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,$$
$$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
        =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,$$

the pressure term and the viscous normal strain have to be kept
together at the free surface.

In the steady state the deflected top is material.  The stated
conditions are $u_{x}(0)=0$ and a steady plate, i.e. impermeability,
$u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0, $$

which is the regular odd mode.  With $C=-A$

$$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(-A+D z)e^{-kz},\qquad B+D=-2kA, $$

and the impermeable mode can be written as

$$\Phi(z)=z\big[\,a\sinh kz+b\big(kz\cosh kz-\sinh kz\big)\big],$$

so that the only $k$–dependence that survives at $z=0$ is the odd
combination $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  Then

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
              =\Delta\rho\,g\,e(t)\cos kx , $$

with the usual geophysical restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$, and in the steady limit $\dot e=0$

$$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}, $$

while at the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the two base conditions are $W(h)=0$ and
$W'(h)=0$ in the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ convention and

$$S(h)=\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}.$$

Eliminating $A,B,D$ with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives the regular
combination

$$\Phi'''(0)=-\frac{4k^{3}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} $$

and hence, with $a=kh$,

$$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|
       =S_{0}\,
\frac{a\,\sinh a}{\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}} .$$

In the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh} ,$$

i.e.

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;\;{\rm sign}\,S_{0}.$$

With the plate density $\rho$ used in the formal statement
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping.
For $kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$ and

$$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, $$

the thin-plate viscous pumping limit, while $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$
for $kh\gg1$, the expected viscous screening.  

The $\cosh kh$ numerator obtained when the vertical impermeability
$\Phi(0)=0$ is dropped, i.e. when $u_{z}(0)=\dot e\neq0$ is retained in
the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ balance, corresponds to the $u_{x}=0$ only
limit.  The steady material top requires both $\Phi(0)=0$ and
$\Phi'(0)=0$, which selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and
changes the $z$–derivative that enters $\sigma_{zz}(0)$ from a
$\cosh$ to a $\sinh$ combination.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation this is the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
stable viscous topographic response to the harmonic basal traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and surface normal stress. ∎

I agree with the stream-function set up used by 1,10,11,18 and the biharmonic
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ with

$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

The steady deflected plate is material.  The problem states $u_{x}(0)=0$
and the normal stress balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ at $z=0$.
In the steady limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is impermeable, so that in
addition to $u_{x}(0)=0$

$\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$,

and with the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.

With $u_{x}(0)=0$ the $3k^{2}\Phi'$ term drops from $\sigma_{zz}(0)$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx$,

so that in the steady state

$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}$.

$\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx$, the base conditions are

$W(h)=0$, $\;S(h)=\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=S_{0}/\mu$,

with $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ on $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.

i.e. the regular odd mode that satisfies both $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$
is the combination $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  Using $U=A+Bh$ the two base
conditions give

$U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$,

and

$S(h)=2k\big[U e^{kh}+U e^{-kh}\big]+2k^{2}h\big[U e^{kh}-U e^{-kh}\big]$.

Eliminating $U$ one finds

$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

and with $\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}(B+2kA)$ the impermeability $W(0)=0$ is
replaced by the full normal stress

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.

Hence

$\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|
           =\frac{S_{0}\,kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

in the steady locked limit.  On the conventional isostatic normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\,,$

definition of the buoyancy stress.  In particular

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $kh\ll1$,  $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

normal stress at the free surface is the $u_{x}=0$ only limit in which
the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution to $\sigma_{zz}$ is dropped.

this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which reduces
to the quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ on the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification.

$kh\sinh kh$ numerator is the one selected by the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution in $\sigma_{zz}$.  The $kh\cosh kh$ form quoted by
1,10,11,18,6 is obtained if the vertical impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ is
dropped after differentiation of the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ term,
i.e. from evaluating $W(0)$ rather than imposing $W'(0)=0$ at the locked
surface.  In the true steady limit $u_{z}(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$, the
$e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to $\sinh kh$ in the
numerator, which coincides with the cosh form to $O(kh)$ in the long-wave
limit $kh\ll1$ and therefore explains the small-$k$ degeneracy noted
above.  With the density used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. the
quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above once the
conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification is made. ∎
public_text.21:
The stream-function set up used by 1,10,11,18 is the right one and it is worth writing it out once in full so the density normalisation is clear.

Put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$. Then
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

and with the steady impermeable/no-slip top
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ we have $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ for
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

On the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e(t)\cos kx$,

$\Phi'(0)=0$,

and on the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$,

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$\rho g e_{s}=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

The two base conditions eliminate $B,D$.  Putting $a=kh$ one gets

$A+Bh=-\dfrac{2kA h}{e^{2a}+1}$, 

and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=4\mu k^{2}A
\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]=S_{0}$,

hence

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
      =\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$,

with $a=kh$.
The viscosity drops out, $\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$ and
$\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$, the familiar long-wave viscous
pumping $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.

That is the Stokes response with the normal stress written as in the
statement, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. with the plate density
$\rho$.  The problem asks for the topography written with the
isostatic restoring buoyancy,

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

where the restoring stress is $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation above

$\chi_{0}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}= \chi\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

so that the dimensionless factor that multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is

$\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_{0}(kh)
       =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
         \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
         \Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
           =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\mathrm{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.  In particular with the density kept explicit
in the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ the steady amplitude is
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$, and the factor that appears in the
$\Delta\rho g$ normalisation requested is the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ scaled
form above.  Up to the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ absorption this is
the $kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ viscous normal-stress coupling
generated by the harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the
$90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift, and $e_{s}\simeq kh\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit.
public_text.12:
With the $k$ mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx , \qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the deflected top is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$, hence

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that, on the $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ basis,

$$
\Phi(z)=P_{0}\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Q_{0}z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
W(z)\equiv\frac1k\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx .
$$

$W(0)=-2k^{2}P_{0}$ and

$$
W(z)=2k^{3}\Big[-P_{0}\cosh kz
+P_{0}kz\sinh kz-Q_{0}z\cosh kz\Big] .
$$

The base conditions

$$
W(h)=0,\qquad \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

give on $a=kh$

$$
Q_{0}=P_{0}\frac{a\sinh a-\cosh a}{h\cosh a},
$$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[-P_{0}k^{2}h\cosh a
+Q_{0}\big(\cosh a+a\sinh a\big)\Big]
=-\frac{2kP_{0}}{h\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big] .
$$

Hence

$$
P_{0}=-\,\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]}\;,
\qquad 
W(0)=-2k^{2}P_{0}.
$$

The normal stress balance at the locked top is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}W(0)=\rho g e_{s}$, i.e.

$$
\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}P_{0}
           =S_{0}\,
             \frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}\;,
\qquad a=kh,
$$

so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity dropping out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that on the long wave thin plate scale

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e.  $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book–keeping the dimensionless viscous
pumping factor is $\chi_{0}=a\cosh a/(a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a)$,
$\chi_{0}\approx kh$ in the thin–plate limit, the stable time
independent topography generated by the harmonic basal traction
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  With
the strict $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement this is
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the
only remaining density dependence. ∎
public_text.8:
In the $k$–mode put $\psi (x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P\cos kx-2\mu k\Phi'\cos kx
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the locked top $u_{x}(0)=0$, and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+\beta\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad \Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0 .
$$

Then
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2\alpha k^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
           =\rho g e ,
$$
so that in the steady state

\begin{equation*}
\alpha=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\end{equation*}

With $s_{h}=\sinh kh,\;c_{h}=\cosh kh$ 

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-\alpha k^{2}z c_{h}+ \beta
\big(c+kz s\big)\Big],\qquad 
\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'=2k^{3}\Big[\alpha\big(khz-c\big)
-\beta h c\Big] .
$$

The base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
are

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
\alpha\big(kh s_{h}-c_{h}\big)=\beta h c_{h},
$$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)
      =-2k\alpha\,
        \frac{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}{h c_{h}} .
$$

Hence
$$
\alpha=-\frac{S_{0}h c_{h}}{2\mu k\big[k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}\big]},\qquad
\beta=\alpha\,\frac{k h s_{h}-c_{h}}{h c_{h}} .
$$

The free-surface normal stress is therefore

$$
\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
           =-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
           =S_{0}\,\frac{k h\,c_{h}}{k^{2}h^{2}+c_{h}^{2}} ,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
   =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

so that the viscosity drops out of the steady response and the
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift is the usual shear-to-topography
shift.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

i.e. the familiar thin-plate viscous pumping

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\;\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1 .
$$

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution gives

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
      \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the long-wave thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi\simeq kh ,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$ being the conventional
shear–to–topography coupling.  Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$
book-keeping this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho
g$, i.e. the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ viscous normal–stress
coupling usually written simply as $e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
for $kh\ll1$ with exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for
$kh\gg1$.  The $\sinh$-numerator form
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ coincides with the
above to $O(kh)$ and reduces to the same long-wave limit
$e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎
public_text.6:
In the $k$ mode
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

\begin{equation*}
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
\end{equation*}
and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'\; \cos kx
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx  .
\end{equation*}
In the steady state the deflected top is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
\end{equation*}
so that with $C=-A$,
$D=-B-2kA$ and, putting $W=-3k\Phi'+\Phi'''/k$,

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx,\qquad 
W(0)=-4k^{2}A,\qquad
W(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\end{equation*}
The zero normal traction at the base is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e.

\begin{equation*}
\big[A+Bh\big]e^{kh}=\big[-A+Dh\big]e^{-kh},
\end{equation*}
and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

\begin{equation*}
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
Eliminating $B$ and $D$ from
$W(h)=0$ and $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

\begin{equation*}
A=-\frac{S_{0}h}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}},
\end{equation*}
so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
         =S_{0}\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}
                +\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}
                +\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\end{equation*}
the viscosity dropping out of the steady response.  In
particular

\begin{equation*}
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
\end{equation*}
so that in the long wave thin plate limit

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\end{equation*}
the usual viscous pumping $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the
$90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress on the deflected free surface in the
geophysical isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$, the same Stokes solution is

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

\begin{equation*}
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Big]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
so that

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)\simeq kh+O\!\left((kh)^{3}\right),\;\;kh\ll1,
\]

i.e. the familiar long wave viscous dynamic topography

\[
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
\]

with the full $kh$ regularisation
$\chi_{0}(kh)=\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh/\cosh kh\big]^{-1}$ and the
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Up to
the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping this is the stable
time independent Stokes topographic response to the harmonic basal
traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With the plate density kept
explicit the result is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho
g$, which reduces to the quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  The often quoted odd-mode form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ coincides with the
above to $O(kh)$, $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, and is the $\sinh$ 
numerator obtained when the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution is
kept in the conventional $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ form. ∎
public_text.15:
In the $k$ mode let

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx , \qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx  
$$

so that $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$.  With
$p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the top is impermeable and $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that on the usual $e^{\pm kz}$ basis
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]
       +\beta z\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2\alpha k^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha\cos kx .
$$

With the normal stress balance written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha  ,
\end{equation*}
and on the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0} .
$$

The zero normal stress gives

$$
\alpha\big[k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=\beta h\cosh kh ,
$$

and the basal shear gives

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =2k\mu\Big[-\alpha k h\cosh kh+\beta\cosh kh
          +\beta k h\sinh kh\Big]=S_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $\beta$,

$$
\beta=\alpha\,\frac{k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh},
\qquad
\alpha=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
           {2k\mu\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]} ,
$$

so that on the free surface

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}\alpha
       =S_{0}\,
         \frac{k h\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad a\equiv kh .
$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\simeq2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

i.e. for a thin long wave plate

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear–to–topography viscous pumping with the
sign of $S_{0}$.  Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional geophysical
factor is obtained on the usual identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

so that with the strict $\rho g$ normal stress used in the statement

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,
$$

for $kh\ll1$, with the exponential screening
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the stable,
time–independent Stokes topography generated by the harmonic basal
traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book–keeping the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+
\cosh^{2}a]$ viscous pumping response, often quoted in the thin-plate
limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
ratio can be kept explicitly as $\chi_{\Delta}=(\Delta\rho/\rho)
\chi_{0}$; with the geophysical convention $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ it is
the $\chi_{0}$ quoted above. ∎

20.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes biharmonic in the k-mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$. With $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
In the steady material limit the top is locked, $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, so $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$.  The base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.

The majority derivation 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,21,3,4 gives after elimination
$\rho g e_s=-4\mu k^{2}A=S_{0}\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, viscosity cancels, and with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_s=\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$, $\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}$,
and with the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Long wave $kh\ll1$: $\chi_{0}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; short wave $\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the shear-to-normal stress shift.

A minority set 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9 argues for the strict steady impermeable/no-slip odd mode $\Phi\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ retained at the locked surface.  That gives the $\sinh$ numerator

$\chi_{\sinh}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

$e_s=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,

which coincides with the cosh form to $O(kh)$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit, $\chi_{\sinh}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$, and has the same exponential screening $ \sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The difference is the $\sinh kh/\cosh kh$ factor coming from whether the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term is kept together with $W(0)=\dot e$ before imposing the steady $u_{z}(0)=0$.

The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping is inessential: the statement uses $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$, the geophysical form uses $\Delta\rho g$.  Up to $\rho/\Delta\rho$, $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and with the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the factor normally quoted is $\chi_{0}$ above, i.e. $e_s\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

Unresolved nuance remains the sinh vs cosh numerator, i.e. whether the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ is enforced before or after eliminating the pressure in $\sigma_{zz}$; both give the same thin-plate limit $e_s\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which is the robust physical result.

 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}$.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$.
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

Steady material top $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$ gives in the steady limit
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. The regular biharmonic with these two conditions is
$\Phi=c_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+d\,z\sinh kz$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_0$
and with the statement normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$c_0=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base $z=h$ : $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_h=S_0$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives
$c_0\cosh kh+h[d\cosh kh-kc_0\sinh kh]=0$,
$d=c_0[\,kh\tanh kh-1\,]/h$ and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_h
=-2\mu k c_0\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.

Hence
$c_0=-S_0h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\,(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$
and with $c_0=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

Thus on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_0(kh) S_0/\rho g$,

$\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
          =\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh\big]^{-1}
          =\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh/\cosh kh\big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady response.  Long wave:
$\chi_0=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$;
short wave $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$, $kh\gg1$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-normal coupling.

The problem writes the restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
but asks for $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  Hence strictly

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

i.e. the factor that multiplies $S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is
$\chi_\Delta=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as $e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\simeq kh$.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 13,14,16,2,5,7,17,9 obtain the
strictly impermeable, $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ retained form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, i.e.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=\chi_0\tanh kh$.  The two forms coincide to $O(kh)$,
$\sinh kh/kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$, $\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$, so the thin-plate
limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential screening
are common to all derivations.  The $\cosh$ numerator is the $u_x(0)=0$
only, $W(0)$-evaluated form; the $\sinh$ numerator is the
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ steady-material form with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

No new evidence in round 2 changes the core result.  The remaining
unresolved bookkeeping is the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor and
the $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator which is $O[(kh)^2]$ in the thin-plate
limit that is normally quoted.  The stable thin-plate answer quoted
by the majority is $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $\chi\simeq kh$,
with the exact regularised factor $\chi_0=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+
\cosh^{2}kh]$, up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ identification.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $k$–mode $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ is the common set-up.  
With $p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$,

and $\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.  
In the steady material limit the deflected top is $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$,
i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, so $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A\cos kx$.

Base $z=h$:

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Writing $W(z)=k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu W\cos kx$,

$U=A+Bh$, $U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$,
and

$S_{0}= -2\mu k p\big[e^{-1}+k^{2}h^{2}e^{-1}\big]$,
$p=A$.

$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
      =S_{0}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

so that

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,

           =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
           =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

the viscosity cancelling in the steady state.  
$\chi_{0}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
The $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-normal
stress shift.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the same Stokes solution is quoted as

$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

i.e. the familiar thin-plate viscous pumping $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the form obtained by Colleagues 1,10,11,18,19,20,21 and is the

A persistent minority strand keeps the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term in
$\sigma_{zz}$ with the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
enforced after differentiation.  In that book-keeping the odd mode
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ is selected and the free-surface coupling becomes

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.
To $O(kh)$ $\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, so
$\chi_{\rm odd}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ and the thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$,
is identical to the $\cosh$ form.  The $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ difference is
therefore an $O[(kh)^{2}]$ book-keeping of the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term
and the transient $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ condition; it does not change the
robust long-wave result $\chi\simeq kh$ and the viscosity-free steady
response.

Unresolved book-keeping: the statement uses $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$
with plate density $\rho$ but asks for $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$.  Hence the factor quoted in the

one has $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\Big[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}

 =\Big[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the same Stokes solution is normally quoted as
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}(\alpha) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

kh$ for $kh\ll1$.

12,15,18,19,20,21,3,4,6,8 etc.  A persistent minority keeps the strict

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $p=P\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$.
In the steady state the material top is locked,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$.  The impermeable steady limit is
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$ on
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and with the full normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,
$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives the regular odd mode
$\Phi\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $e^{\pm kz}$ partner
required by the basal traction.  Eliminating $B,D$,
$U=A+Bh$, $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$,
$U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$,

$\displaystyle 
S_{0}= -2\mu k p\,
\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{h}+k^{2}h\,\frac1{\cosh kh}\Big]
       =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h\cosh kh}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]$,
with $p$ the amplitude of the odd mode,
$ \sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p=\rho g e_{s}$.
Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

$\mu$ drops out of the steady response and the phase is
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.  In particular
$\chi_{0}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$,
so that in the thin–plate long wave limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.
Up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping the
dimensionless viscous pumping factor is $\chi_{0}$ above.

Debate noted in the round: the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
numerator is obtained if the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution to
$\sigma_{zz}$ is kept with the transient kinematic condition
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ and the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
is imposed after differentiation.  This $\sinh$ form coincides with the
$\cosh$ form to $O(kh)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,21,3,4,6,8
give the $\cosh$ numerator $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
with the strict steady conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, which is the form used in
the persistent memory.  The minority $\sinh$ forms of 13,14,16,17,5,2,7,9
differ only by the $\sinh kh/\cosh kh$ phase factor and reduce to the
same $kh$ long-wave limit.  Unresolved is the exact $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor: with the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$ the steady
amplitude is $\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$, i.e. $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{0}$ in the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normalisation, which
reduces to the quoted $\chi$ on the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$  

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
The $k$–mode is $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.  
In the steady material limit the deflected top is locked and impermeable,

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$,
so that $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, 
$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

The base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $U=A+Bh$ the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$,
$V=C+Dh$, whence $U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$.

Eliminating $B,D$ gives
$A=-\,S_{0}h\cosh kh\big/[4\mu k\big((kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big)]$
and  

$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
     =S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\,,$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

so that $\mu$ drops out of the steady response. 
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
and the familiar long-wave viscous pumping is
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\big[ \cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

The $kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form that appears in a
minority of the round-2 derivations is the strict $W(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$
odd-mode result obtained by retaining the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ 
and imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ before the steady limit. It coincides
with the $\cosh$ form to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{\sinh}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same exponential screening
$\sim2kh e^{-kh}$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping is the only
remaining density dependence; with the statement’s $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$
the factor in front of $S_{0}/\rho g$ is $\chi_{0}$ above, and the factor
in front of $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$, which
reduces to $\chi_{0}$ on the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification.  The viscosity cancels in the steady state and the
phase shift $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-topography shift.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains centred on the Stokes stream function 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx =-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.
In the steady state the top is $u_x(0)=0$ and materially locked, so the
usual regularisation used in the majority of the rounds is 
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and under the stated normal stress 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho g e_s =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.
Basal conditions $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e.
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, $\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_0/\mu$, give
$[A+Bh]e^{kh}=[C+Dh]e^{-kh}$ and, with $U=A+Bh$, $U(1+e^{2kh})=-2khA$.
Eliminating $B,D$,
$A=-\dfrac{S_0 h\cosh kh}{4\mu k\big[(kh)^2+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,
whence on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$e_s=\chi_0(kh)S_0/\rho g$ with
$\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}\,a\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular
$\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
so the thin long-wave viscous pumping limit is
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$, the familiar $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
form obtained by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,21, etc.

Writing the restoring stress on the deflected free surface in the
isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same solution
is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this
is quoted as
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^2+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.
The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is the only remaining density
book-keeping; with the $\rho g$ normal stress used in the statement the
bare factor is $\chi_0$.

A minority stream, Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7, keeps the full

impermeability $u_z(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, and obtains the odd
mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  The free-surface coupling then becomes
$\sigma_{zz}(0)\propto\Phi'''(0)$ with the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$
contributions combining to a $\sinh kh$ numerator,
$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$,
i.e. $e_s=S_0/\Delta\rho g\;a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$.
To $O(a)$ $\sinh a=a+O(a^{3})$, $\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$ so
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and the thin-plate limit
$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is unchanged.  The $\cosh$ and $\sinh$
forms differ only by the factor $\tanh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$ and coincide
to leading order in the long-wave limit; the degeneracy explains the
persistent $kh\cosh$ vs $kh\sinh$ split in the discussion.

Unresolved points carried forward: the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor in $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ versus the statement's
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$; whether the steady impermeability
$u_z(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, should be imposed in addition to $u_x(0)=0$,
i.e. whether the quoted numerator is strictly $\cosh kh$ or the
impermeable odd-mode $\sinh kh$; and sign conventions.  The thin-plate
limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and the
exponential viscous screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable across both
families.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady mode can be written with the biharmonic stream
function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

the usual $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ normal stress.  In the steady,
material limit the locked free surface is

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e =0\iff 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e. the regular odd biharmonic
$\Phi=a\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+b\,z\sinh kz$.  
With $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ on the $(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ basis this
is $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
               =-4\mu k^{2}A\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.
The base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e. $\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ i.e. $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Writing $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$ the zero $zz$ condition at $h$ is
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with $U+V=-2khA$, so that

$$
U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ one obtains on the odd basis

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
=-\frac{2kA}{h\cosh kh}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big] ,
$$

hence

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kA}{h\cosh kh}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big] ,
$$

and with $\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,\qquad a=kh .
$$

The viscosity cancels out of the steady response.  On the $\rho g$
normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\;kh\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\;kh\gg1,
$$

so that $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ in the thin long-wave limit,
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}
       \simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form quoted by a minority of colleagues is the
same expression to $O(kh)$,
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, and is obtained when the transient
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ term is kept in the normal stress balance before
the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ is imposed.  Once the strict
steady material condition $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together
with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode is selected and the $kh\cosh kh/
[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ viscous-isostatic factor above is the stable
time-independent topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  This
is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ response, often quoted in
the thin-plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, viscosity
cancelling out of the steady state. ∎

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $k$ mode can be written with the stream function
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, 

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\iff (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}\; .
$$

In the steady material limit the deflected top is locked and
impermeable,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\iff 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

and the regular biharmonic can be written as

$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,
$$

i.e. on the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  On the steady free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p ,
$$

and the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  The base
conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

which with $a=kh$ give

$$
q=p\,\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-2\mu p k\frac{\cosh a}{h}\Big[1+a^{2}{\rm sech}^{2}a\Big]=S_{0},
$$

so that

$$
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big]},\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p .
$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},\qquad a=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping, with
exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $\chi\simeq kh$ for the
thin long-wave plate $kh\ll1$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form that appears in several
derivations is the odd-mode expression obtained when the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is retained in the
transient $W(0)=\dot e$ book-keeping.  With the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ imposed, $\sinh a/\cosh a=
1+O(a^{2})$ and the two expressions coincide to $O(a)$,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=a+O(a^{3})$, i.e. the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift and
the exponential short-wave screening being robust.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
density ratio is the only remaining book-keeping difference between the
$\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement and the usual
$\Delta\rho g$ isostatic normalisation. ∎

reflection_text.11:
The harmonic Stokes mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$.
With $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

Steady material top $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$ gives in the steady limit
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. The regular biharmonic with these two conditions is
$\Phi=c_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+d\,z\sinh kz$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_0$
and with the statement normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$c_0=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base $z=h$ : $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_h=S_0$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives
$c_0\cosh kh+h[d\cosh kh-kc_0\sinh kh]=0$,
$d=c_0[\,kh\tanh kh-1\,]/h$ and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_h
=-2\mu k c_0\,[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.

Hence
$c_0=-S_0h\cosh kh/[2\mu k\,(k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh)]$
and with $c_0=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.

Thus on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_0(kh) S_0/\rho g$,

$\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
          =\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh\big]^{-1}
          =\big[\cosh kh/kh+kh/\cosh kh\big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady response.  Long wave:
$\chi_0=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$;
short wave $\chi_0\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$, $kh\gg1$.  The $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-normal coupling.

The problem writes the restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
but asks for $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  Hence strictly

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

i.e. the factor that multiplies $S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is
$\chi_\Delta=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as $e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\simeq kh$.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 13,14,16,2,5,7,17,9 obtain the
strictly impermeable, $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ retained form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, i.e.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=\chi_0\tanh kh$.  The two forms coincide to $O(kh)$,
$\sinh kh/kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$, $\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$, so the thin-plate
limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential screening
are common to all derivations.  The $\cosh$ numerator is the $u_x(0)=0$
only, $W(0)$-evaluated form; the $\sinh$ numerator is the
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ steady-material form with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

No new evidence in round 2 changes the core result.  The remaining
unresolved bookkeeping is the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor and
the $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator which is $O[(kh)^2]$ in the thin-plate
limit that is normally quoted.  The stable thin-plate answer quoted
by the majority is $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $\chi\simeq kh$,
with the exact regularised factor $\chi_0=kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+
\cosh^{2}kh]$, up to the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ identification.
reflection_text.4:
The $k$–mode $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ is the common set-up.

          =-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$,

and $\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

      =S_{0}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

           =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
           =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

reflection_text.15:
The steady harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$  

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
The $k$–mode is $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.  
In the steady material limit the deflected top is locked and impermeable,

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$,
so that $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, 
$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.

The base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $U=A+Bh$ the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$,
$V=C+Dh$, whence $U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$.

Eliminating $B,D$ gives
$A=-\,S_{0}h\cosh kh\big/[4\mu k\big((kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big)]$
and  

$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
     =S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\,,$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

so that $\mu$ drops out of the steady response. 
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
and the familiar long-wave viscous pumping is
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\big[ \cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

The $kh\sinh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form that appears in a
minority of the round-2 derivations is the strict $W(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$
odd-mode result obtained by retaining the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ 
and imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ before the steady limit. It coincides
with the $\cosh$ form to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{\sinh}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same exponential screening
$\sim2kh e^{-kh}$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping is the only
remaining density dependence; with the statement’s $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$
the factor in front of $S_{0}/\rho g$ is $\chi_{0}$ above, and the factor
in front of $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$, which
reduces to $\chi_{0}$ on the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification.  The viscosity cancels in the steady state and the
phase shift $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-topography shift.
reflection_text.12:
The deliberation remains centred on the Stokes stream function 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx =-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.
In the steady state the top is $u_x(0)=0$ and materially locked, so the
usual regularisation used in the majority of the rounds is 
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and under the stated normal stress 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho g e_s =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A$.
Basal conditions $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e.
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$, $\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=S_0/\mu$, give
$[A+Bh]e^{kh}=[C+Dh]e^{-kh}$ and, with $U=A+Bh$, $U(1+e^{2kh})=-2khA$.
Eliminating $B,D$,
$A=-\dfrac{S_0 h\cosh kh}{4\mu k\big[(kh)^2+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}$,
whence on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$e_s=\chi_0(kh)S_0/\rho g$ with
$\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}\,a\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$.
The viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular
$\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
so the thin long-wave viscous pumping limit is
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$, the familiar $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.  This is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
form obtained by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,21, etc.

Writing the restoring stress on the deflected free surface in the
isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same solution
is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this
is quoted as
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^2+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.
The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is the only remaining density
book-keeping; with the $\rho g$ normal stress used in the statement the
bare factor is $\chi_0$.

A minority stream, Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7, keeps the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ together with the strict steady
impermeability $u_z(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, and obtains the odd
mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  The free-surface coupling then becomes
$\sigma_{zz}(0)\propto\Phi'''(0)$ with the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$
contributions combining to a $\sinh kh$ numerator,
$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$,
i.e. $e_s=S_0/\Delta\rho g\;a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$.
To $O(a)$ $\sinh a=a+O(a^{3})$, $\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$ so
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and the thin-plate limit
$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is unchanged.  The $\cosh$ and $\sinh$
forms differ only by the factor $\tanh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$ and coincide
to leading order in the long-wave limit; the degeneracy explains the
persistent $kh\cosh$ vs $kh\sinh$ split in the discussion.

Unresolved points carried forward: the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor in $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ versus the statement's
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$; whether the steady impermeability
$u_z(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, should be imposed in addition to $u_x(0)=0$,
i.e. whether the quoted numerator is strictly $\cosh kh$ or the
impermeable odd-mode $\sinh kh$; and sign conventions.  The thin-plate
limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and the
exponential viscous screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable across both
families.
reflection_text.1:
The steady mode can be written with the biharmonic stream
function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

the usual $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ normal stress.  In the steady,
material limit the locked free surface is

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e =0\iff 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e. the regular odd biharmonic
$\Phi=a\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+b\,z\sinh kz$.  
With $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ on the $(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ basis this
is $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
               =-4\mu k^{2}A\cos kx=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$.
The base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e. $\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ i.e. $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Writing $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$ the zero $zz$ condition at $h$ is
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with $U+V=-2khA$, so that

$$
U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ one obtains on the odd basis

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
=-\frac{2kA}{h\cosh kh}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big] ,
$$

hence

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kA}{h\cosh kh}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big] ,
$$

and with $\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,\qquad a=kh .
$$

The viscosity cancels out of the steady response.  On the $\rho g$
normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi_{0}=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\;kh\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\;kh\gg1,
$$

so that $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ in the thin long-wave limit,
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}
       \simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $kh\sinh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form quoted by a minority of colleagues is the
same expression to $O(kh)$,
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, and is obtained when the transient
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ term is kept in the normal stress balance before
the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ is imposed.  Once the strict
steady material condition $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together
with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode is selected and the $kh\cosh kh/
[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ viscous-isostatic factor above is the stable
time-independent topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$.  This
is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ response, often quoted in
the thin-plate limit as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, viscosity
cancelling out of the steady state. ∎

$$

i.e. on the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.  On the steady free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p ,
$$

and the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  The base
conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

which with $a=kh$ give

$$
q=p\,\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-2\mu p k\frac{\cosh a}{h}\Big[1+a^{2}{\rm sech}^{2}a\Big]=S_{0},
$$

so that

$$
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[\cosh^{2}a+a^{2}\big]},\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p .
$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},\qquad a=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping, with
exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $\chi\simeq kh$ for the
thin long-wave plate $kh\ll1$, and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$.

The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form that appears in several
derivations is the odd-mode expression obtained when the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is retained in the
transient $W(0)=\dot e$ book-keeping.  With the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ imposed, $\sinh a/\cosh a=
1+O(a^{2})$ and the two expressions coincide to $O(a)$,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=a+O(a^{3})$, i.e. the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift and
the exponential short-wave screening being robust.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
density ratio is the only remaining book-keeping difference between the
$\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement and the usual
$\Delta\rho g$ isostatic normalisation. ∎

4.text:
With the $k$ mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad \big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
       =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}\; ,
$$

the regular biharmonic solution is  

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
$$

In the steady material limit the deflected top is locked and
impermeable

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\;\;\dot e=0\iff u_{z}(0)=0\iff
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and, on the top,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\qquad\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

Hence in the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A . \tag{1}
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

Writing $U=A+Bh$ the zero normal traction gives $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with
$V=C+Dh$ and $U-V=-2khA$, i.e.

$$
U\big(1+e^{2kh}\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{4\mu kA}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big],
$$

so that with (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
       =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
\qquad a=kh,
$$

and the viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping law, with exponential screening for
$kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. in the long wave thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor
is the only density book-keeping; on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in
the statement the stable topography is $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{0}$ above, which with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is the quoted
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the $O(kh)$ interchange
$\sinh kh\leftrightarrow\cosh kh$ this is the
$kh\sinh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]$ odd-mode form; it coincides
with the expression above to $O(kh)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  The viscosity cancels in the steady state and the
shear-to-topography phase is the usual $\sin kx\to\cos kx$. ∎
