11.text:
The $k$ mode can be written with the stream function
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,$$
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,$$
$$\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
      =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}.$$

In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$

$$u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,$$
so that on the regular biharmonic

$$\Phi(z)=c_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,$$

$$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$$c_{0}=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .$$

The base conditions

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},$$

give on $a=kh$

$$d=c_{0}\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-2\mu k c_{0}\frac{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}{a\cosh a}=S_{0},$$

i.e.

$$c_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]},\qquad a=kh.$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}
          =S_{0}\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},$$

i.e.

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}, $$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady response.  In particular

$$\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1, $$

so that for the long wave thin sheet

$$e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear to normal coupling
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ and viscous pumping.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},$$

and with the $\rho$ kept explicitly in the statement

With the $k$–mode

$$

$$

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}\;,
$$

and

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
\end{equation*}

In the steady state the deflected top is material.  With the
statement $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

hence on the regular biharmonic

$$
C=-A,\qquad D=-B-2kA,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{1}
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Writing $U=A+Bh$ the $W(h)=0$ condition $\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$
is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with $V=C+Dh$ and $U+V=-2khA$, i.e.

$$
U\big(1+e^{2kh}\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from (2)

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{4\mu k A}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

so that with $a=kh$

\begin{equation*}
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{4\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]}\; .
\end{equation*}

Using (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
     =S_{0}\,\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}\,a\Big]^{-1},
\tag{3}
$$

the viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that for the long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ viscous pumping $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.
Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
it is quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book keeping this is the stable time
independent dynamic topography generated by the harmonic basal shear
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$; the $kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
odd–mode form coincides with (3) to $O(kh)$ and gives the same
thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-normal stress phase shift being the usual
viscous pumping response.  With the $\rho g$ normal stress used in the
statement this is $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{0}$ in (3);
the factor that multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
$(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$, which reduces to the textbook

$\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,$

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Then

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}p\,\cos kx $

and with the isostatic normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$.

At the base

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,$
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.$

With $s=\sinh kh,\;c=\cosh kh,\;a=kh$,

$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
(p+qh)c= k p a s ,$

i.e. $q=p\big[a\tanh a-1\big]/h$, and

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big|_{h}
   =-2k p\Big[\frac{c}{h}+k^{2}\frac{h}{c}\Big]
   =-\frac{2k p}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big].$

Hence

$S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],$

so that

$p=-\frac{S_{0}h c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]}$.

The free surface balance is therefore

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
   =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,s}{c^{2}+a^{2}} ,$

i.e. in the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}.$

With the plate density kept explicitly in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  For
$kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh/kh\to1$, $\cosh kh\to1$,

$\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},$

the familiar long-wave viscous pumping $e\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift, while
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the expected viscous screening.

The $kh\cosh kh/[c^{2}+a^{2}]$ form is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only limit
obtained by evaluating $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before imposing the steady impermeability
$W'(0)=0$, i.e. by dropping the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution in
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ or keeping the transient
$W(0)=\dot e$ term.  Once the steady material condition
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$
contributions combine to the odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and the
normal-stress balance at the locked top selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.
The thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$ is preserved, so the difference
is $O[(kh)^{2}]$ and numerically tiny for $kh\lesssim1$, which is why the
$\cosh$ and $\sinh$ forms are often quoted interchangeably.  With the
usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification this is the stable, time
independent Stokes topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},

i.e. with $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$,

$$
Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh},\qquad U+V=-2khA .
$$

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{4\mu kA}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

$$

$$

        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$

     \frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{\cosh kh}\; .
$$

Hence from (2)

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{4\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\;,
$$

and with (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad a\equiv kh .
$$

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

and $\mu$ drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that for a long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ viscous pumping $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.
Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

with exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
In the strict steady impermeable, $u_{z}(0)=0$, limit the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode is selected and the normal stress coupling can
be written in the equivalent $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form,
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with the
expression above to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{s}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the usual $90^{\circ}$ shear to
topography phase shift.  This is the viscosity-free stable Stokes
topography generated by the harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping. ∎

3.text:
In the $k$–mode put $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0,
$$
so that with $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 .
$$
In the steady material state $u_{x}(0)=0,\;\dot e=0$,
$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
$$
so that on the regular biharmonic
$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz ,\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0 .
$$
Then
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}a\cos kx ,
$$
and with the imposed normal traction
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx$,
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}a ,
\tag{1}
$$
in the steady state.  On the base $z=h$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0 ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$
With $\alpha=kh$
$$
a\cosh\alpha-h\big[ak\sinh\alpha-b\cosh\alpha\big]=0,
$$
i.e. 
$$
b=a\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}
  =ak\frac{\alpha\tanh\alpha-1}{\alpha},
$$
and
$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
   =-\frac{2ak^{2}}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
     \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$
Hence
$$
S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu a k^{2}}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] ,
$$
so that with (1)
$$
a=-\frac{S_{0}\alpha\cosh\alpha}
        {2\mu k^{2}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]},\qquad
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}a
          =S_{0}\,
            \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
                 {\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}\;,
$$
i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
       +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$
and the viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular
$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha},\;\alpha\gg1,
$$
so that for a long wave thin sheet
$$
e_{s}\simeq\alpha\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-topography viscous pumping
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g} .
$$
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
so that in the thin-plate long-wave limit
$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\quad kh\ll1,
$$
and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping this is the $ \alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ viscous–isostatic response.  The strict
steady impermeable, no-slip form is often written with the odd
numerator $\chi_{\rm sinh}= \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$; $\chi_{\rm sinh}=\chi_{0}+O(\alpha^{3})$, so that the
thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ are unchanged.  This is the
stable time independent dynamic topography generated by the harmonic
basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎

6.text:
In the $k$ mode
$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx\,,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z} .
$$
On the locked material top in the steady state $\dot e=0$,
$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$
so that on the regular biharmonic
$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0,
$$
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
$$
With the normal stress written as in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p .
\tag{1}
$$
The base conditions are
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$
Writing $a=kh$,
$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
p\big(a\sinh a-\cosh a\big)-q h\cosh a=0,
$$
i.e.
$$
q=p\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad 
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kp}{h\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big] .
$$
Hence
$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big],
$$
$$
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]} .
$$
With (1)
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
          =S_{0}\,
            \frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},
\qquad a=kh,
$$
so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$$
e_{s}=\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
and the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  In particular
$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3})\quad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim 2a e^{-a}\quad a\gg1,
$$
i.e. the familiar long wave viscous pumping
$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
as
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
so that with the plate density kept explicit
$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$
On the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ convention this is
$\chi(kh)=\chi_{0}(kh)$ and in the thin long-wave limit
$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The $kh\sinh kh$ form
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ coincides with the
expression above to $O(kh)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the $\cosh$ numerator is the
strict $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ impermeable, no-slip steady limit.  Up to
the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping this is the
stable time independent dynamic topography generated by
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

public_text.4:
With the $k$ mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad \big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
       =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}\; ,
$$

the regular biharmonic solution is  

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
$$

In the steady material limit the deflected top is locked and
impermeable

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\;\;\dot e=0\iff u_{z}(0)=0\iff
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and, on the top,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\qquad\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

Hence in the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A . \tag{1}
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

Writing $U=A+Bh$ the zero normal traction gives $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with
$V=C+Dh$ and $U-V=-2khA$, i.e.

$$
U\big(1+e^{2kh}\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{4\mu kA}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big],
$$

so that with (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
       =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
\qquad a=kh,
$$

and the viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping law, with exponential screening for
$kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. in the long wave thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor
is the only density book-keeping; on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in
the statement the stable topography is $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{0}$ above, which with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ is the quoted
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the $O(kh)$ interchange
$\sinh kh\leftrightarrow\cosh kh$ this is the
$kh\sinh kh/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]$ odd-mode form; it coincides
with the expression above to $O(kh)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  The viscosity cancels in the steady state and the
shear-to-topography phase is the usual $\sin kx\to\cos kx$. ∎
public_text.17:
I agree with the biharmonic stream-function set up that 1,10,11,12,15,18,6 have written out in detail. With

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$,
the $k$ mode is completely regular. The point where the steady state is
taken is the steady impermeability of the material top.

The problem states $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the top is deflected. In the truly
steady limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is material, so $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$
in addition to $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

which is the regular odd biharmonic mode. On the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the
admissible odd combination is

$\Phi(z)\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $e^{kz}$ partner required
by the basal traction. With $\Phi'(0)=0$ the normal traction at the
free surface is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

and the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is not dropped once
the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ is enforced.

Zero normal traction at the base is

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

and the imposed basal shear is

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ put $U=A+Bh$.  $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and $U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$.  Eliminating $B,D$ from
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives the regular odd amplitude

$A=-\dfrac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

so that

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}[B+2kA]=
-\dfrac{4k^{2}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Hence on the isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \dfrac{\mu}{k}|\Phi'''(0)|
 =S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

In the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

and with the plate density $\rho$ kept explicit in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping.  For $kh\ll1$,

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, i.e. the familiar long-wave
viscous pumping and exponential screening with the $90^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift.

The $kh\cosh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form quoted by 1,10,11,18 is the
$u_{x}(0)=0$ only evaluation of $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before the steady
impermeability $W'(0)=0$ is imposed.  Once the steady material condition
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$
contributions combine to the odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and the
free-surface coupling selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.  The small-$k$
degeneracy $\sinh kh/kh\to1$, $\cosh kh\to1$ means both forms give
$\chi\simeq kh$ in the thin-plate long wave limit, which is why the
long-wave agreement does not discriminate the numerator.  With the
strict steady impermeable, locked top the stable time-independent
topography is therefore the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ viscous
isostatic response, which coincides with the $\cosh$ form to $O(kh)$ and
reduces to $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual
thin-plate limit.
public_text.16:
With the harmonic mode write
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

The deflected top is material in the steady state.  The problem states
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and the plate is steady, $\dot e=0$, i.e. $u_{z}(0)=0$.
Hence

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

the regular odd impermeable mode.  On the
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that the only combination which survives at $z=0$ is the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  With the full normal stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx,
\qquad\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,
$$

and in the isostatic normalisation used for the topography
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}p .
\tag{1}
$$

At the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

For $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$ the zero normal traction gives

$$
\big(p+qh\big)c=kph\,s,
\qquad q=p\Big(k\tanh a-h^{-1}\Big),
$$

and

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big|_{h}
=2k\Big[q c+qkh\,s-k^{2}phc\Big]
=-2kp\Big[\frac{c}{h}+k^{2}h\frac1c\Big].
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h c}\big[c^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\big],
$$

so that

$$
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\,c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\big]} .
$$

Inserting in (1),

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}p
 =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,s}{c^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}},
$$

i.e. in the usual notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh},
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ being the familiar shear-to-
normal stress shift.  With the plate density kept explicitly in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $e_{s}=\chi_{0}
S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $\chi_{0}$ above, and on the conventional
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ it is the quoted
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh},\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and the response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  The
$kh\sinh kh$ numerator is the one selected by the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the complete
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ at the locked top.  The
$kh\cosh kh$ form obtained by evaluating the normal stress with
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$, i.e. with the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only condition and
$W(0)=\dot e$ retained in the transient balance, is the $u_{z}(0)\neq0$
limit.  Once the steady material condition $u_{z}(0)=0$, $W'(0)=0$ is
imposed the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and the free-surface coupling changes from
$\cosh kh$ to $\sinh kh$.  To $O(kh)$ the two forms coincide,
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, which is why the thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is preserved in both
presentations.  This is the stable time independent Stokes topography
generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
public_text.11:
The $k$ mode can be written with the stream function
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,

$$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,$$
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,$$
$$\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
      =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}.$$

In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$

$$u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,$$
so that on the regular biharmonic

$$\Phi(z)=c_{0}\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+d\,z\sinh kz ,$$

$$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}c_{0},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}\cos kx .
$$

With the normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$$c_{0}=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .$$

The base conditions

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0},$$

give on $a=kh$

$$d=c_{0}\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-2\mu k c_{0}\frac{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}{a\cosh a}=S_{0},$$

i.e.

$$c_{0}=-
\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]},\qquad a=kh.$$

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}c_{0}
          =S_{0}\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},$$

i.e.

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
      =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}, $$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady response.  In particular

$$\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1, $$

so that for the long wave thin sheet

$$e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear to normal coupling
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ and viscous pumping.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},$$

and with the $\rho$ kept explicitly in the statement

$$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;,$$

so that with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi\simeq kh,\qquad kh\ll1, $$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the harmless
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping this is the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$
viscous dynamic topography.  The impermeable no slip steady mode
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives the odd form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$, which coincides with the
above to $O(a)$, $\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$, and hence gives the same
thin plate long wave limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
usual $e^{-kh}$ screening. ∎
public_text.14:
I think the biharmonic stream-function set up that 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,21 use is the right place to start and we should keep it. In the $k$ mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
          =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
The problem states $u_{x}(0)=0$ and gives the normal stress balance
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$
the top is impermeable as well as locked in $x$, so that
$u_{z}(0)=0$ and
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$
on the steady mode.  With $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the regular odd mode is
$\Phi(z)\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $e^{kz}$ partner required by the base.

The point that is being missed in the $kh\cosh kh$ quotations is the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ at the locked free surface.
With $\Phi'(0)=0$
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ but $\Phi'''(0)$ is not
given by the $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ transient evaluation.  Imposing the steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ and retaining the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ pieces
combine so that the free-surface traction is carried by the odd
combination $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  Writing $W(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the base
conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,
and with $W(0)=W'(0)=0$ the regular solution satisfies
$U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$, $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$, $U-V=-2khA$.
Eliminating $B,D$ gives

$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
    \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

and

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}[B+2kA]
        =-\frac{4k^{2}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
          \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Hence with the steady balance $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$
on the conventional isostatic normalisation,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big|\Phi'''(0)\big|
   =S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. in the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$.

With the plate density kept explicitly in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping.  On the geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted form.

In particular
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ for $kh\ll1$ so that
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the familiar long-wave viscous pumping, and
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the expected viscous screening.
The $kh\cosh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ expression obtained by 1,10,11,
15,18,19,21 is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only, $W(0)=\dot e$ evaluation.  Once
the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, is
enforced together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$,
the free-surface coupling selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.  The
thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $90^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase are preserved, as is the exponential
screening, which is why the two forms are often confused to $O(kh)$.
This is the stable, time-independent Stokes topography generated by
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with a kinematically locked, impermeable free surface
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
public_text.12:
With the $k$–mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}\;,
$$

and

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz} .
\end{equation*}

In the steady state the deflected top is material.  With the
statement $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
$$

hence on the regular biharmonic

$$
C=-A,\qquad D=-B-2kA,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{1}
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Writing $U=A+Bh$ the $W(h)=0$ condition $\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$
is $Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with $V=C+Dh$ and $U+V=-2khA$, i.e.

$$
U\big(1+e^{2kh}\big)=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ from (2)

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{4\mu k A}{h\cosh kh}\Big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big]=S_{0},
$$

so that with $a=kh$

\begin{equation*}
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{4\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]}\; .
\end{equation*}

Using (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
     =S_{0}\,\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}\,a\Big]^{-1},
\tag{3}
$$

the viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that for the long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ viscous pumping $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.
Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
it is quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
\qquad e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book keeping this is the stable time
independent dynamic topography generated by the harmonic basal shear
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$; the $kh\sinh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
odd–mode form coincides with (3) to $O(kh)$ and gives the same
thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-normal stress phase shift being the usual
viscous pumping response.  With the $\rho g$ normal stress used in the
statement this is $e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{0}$ in (3);
the factor that multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
$(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$, which reduces to the textbook
$\chi_{0}$ on the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification. ∎
public_text.13:
I am happy to agree with 1,10,11,12,15,18,6 on the stream-function set up
and on the essential point that viscosity cancels out of the steady
response. With

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
       =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

the steady material free surface is really

$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$,

i.e. the strict steady impermeability

$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

not $u_{x}(0)=0$ alone. On the $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the
regular odd mode can be written as

$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+zq\sinh kz$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

so that the only $z$–dependent combination that survives at the top is
the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  With this mode

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$,

and the full normal stress $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is kept.  The
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part is precisely what is lost if the
$W(0)=\dot e$ transient term is evaluated before the steady limit
$W'(0)=0$ is imposed.

Zero normal traction at the base

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

and the imposed basal shear

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,

give, with $s=\sinh kh$, $c=\cosh kh$, $\alpha=kh$,

$(p+qh)c=kphs$,  i.e. $q=p[\alpha\tanh\alpha-1]/h$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2\mu kp\big[c/h+k^{2}h/c\big]
      =-2\mu kp\,[c^{2}+\alpha^{2}]/(h c)$.

Hence

$p=-\dfrac{S_{0}h c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+\alpha^{2}\big]}$,

and the steady free-surface balance, with the isostatic restoring
stress written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$,

gives

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{\alpha\,s}{c^{2}+\alpha^{2}}$.

In the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Big]^{-1}
        \dfrac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

so that

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$

with the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift.  With the
plate density $\rho$ kept explicitly in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping
that is often absorbed by the identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.

In particular $\sinh kh/kh\to1$, $\cosh kh\to1$ for $\alpha\ll1$, so

$\chi=kh+O(\alpha^{3})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.  The long wave
$\chi\simeq kh$ and the exponential screening are therefore identical
to leading order with the $kh\cosh kh/[c^{2}+\alpha^{2}]$ form quoted
by 1,10,11,12,15,18,6, which is why the asymptotic tests do not resolve
the two expressions.  The difference is precisely the $W'(0)=0$
steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ together with the retention of the
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution in $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}
u_{z}$: imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ selects the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and changes the free-surface coupling from
$\cosh kh$ to $\sinh kh$.  This is the stable time-independent Stokes
topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, and it reduces to the familiar
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ thin-plate viscous pumping limit. ∎
public_text.2:
The biharmonic stream function is the right starting point and the disagreement is essentially the steady impermeability condition at the free surface.

Put $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

The top is a material deflected plate.  In a steady state $u_x(0)=0$ and
$u_z(0)=\dot e=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$.

With $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$ and the
regular odd solution can be written

$\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.

Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3p$ and with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term retained

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^2p\cos kx$.

Zero normal traction at the base is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.
With $s=\sinh kh$, $c=\cosh kh$ the base condition gives

$p+qh\,c=kph\,s$,
$q=p\big(k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big)$

and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h
= -2\mu k p\big[c/h+k^2h/c\big]
= -2\mu k p\,[c^2+k^2h^2]/[h c]$.

Hence

$p=-\dfrac{S_0 h c}{2\mu k\big[c^2+k^2h^2\big]}$,

and on the locked top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^2p
            =S_0\,\dfrac{kh\,s}{c^2+(kh)^2}\,
              \dfrac{s}{c}$.

Normalising the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ and using the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$
book-keeping, $ \Phi'''(0)$ is the $W'(0)=0$ combination, i.e. the odd
mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  The $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ partners combine
so that the free-surface coupling brings a $\sinh kh$ rather than a
$\cosh kh$ factor.  In the conventional $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$
notation

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \dfrac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

up to the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping that is absorbed
in the definition of the buoyancy stress.  With the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi
S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

In particular $\sinh kh/kh\to1$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, so that

$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g,\qquad kh\ll1$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous pumping
and exponential screening.  The $kh\cosh kh/[c^2+(kh)^2]$ form quoted by
1,10,11,15,18 is the $u_x(0)=0$ only evaluation with $W(0)=-4k^2A$
kept before imposing the steady impermeability $W'(0)=0$, i.e. the
transient $W(0)=\dot e$ contribution.  Once the steady material condition
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$, the normal stress at the locked
top selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and the stable steady
amplitude is the $\sinh$ numerator above, which coincides with the
$\cosh$ numerator to $O(kh)$ in the long-wave thin-plate limit and
explains the $kh\approx kh$ degeneracy noted in the discussion.  This is
the time independent viscous dynamic topography generated by the harmonic
basal traction $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$ with $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

$u_{x}(0)=0$ and a material, steady plate, i.e. $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$.
Hence in the steady limit

$\Phi(0)=0$ , $\Phi'(0)=0$,

not $u_{x}(0)=0$ alone.  On the regular biharmonic basis

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$,

the regular odd impermeable mode can be written as

$\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

so that the $e^{\pm kz}$ even part is removed by the steady
impermeability.  With this mode

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$,

and the zero normal traction at the base $z=h$ is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$.
That gives

$p+qh\;c =kph\;s$,  $s=\sinh kh$, $c=\cosh kh$,

i.e.

$q=p\big(k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big)$,

and

$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =-2kp\Big[\frac{c}{h}+k^{2}h\frac1c\Big]
   \frac{s}{c}$ .

Hence the imposed basal shear

$S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kp}{h c}\Big[c^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]\frac{s}{c}$,

so that

$p=-\frac{S_{0}h\,c^{2}}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+k^{2}h^{2}\big]s}$.

The normal stress balance at the free surface is written in the
geophysical isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. with the full
$-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ stress

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}p$.

Eliminating $p$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. on the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ being the usual shear to
normal stress shift.  With the plate density $\rho$ kept explicit in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; on the usual
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ it is the factor quoted
above.

In particular

$\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big)$, $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar long wave viscous
pumping and exponential viscous screening.  The thin plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is preserved.

The $kh\cosh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form obtained by 1,10,11,18,6,8,15
is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only evaluation in which the steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=0$ is not imposed together with $\Phi'(0)=0$,
i.e. the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ term is kept and the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
contribution to $\sigma_{zz}$ is dropped at $z=0$.  With the steady
material condition $u_{z}(0)=0$ the odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ is
selected and the free surface coupling becomes the $\sinh kh$
numerator above.  To $O(kh)$ the two forms coincide,
$\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, which is why the thin plate limit
$\chi\simeq kh$ is common to both derivations, but the strict steady
impermeable, no slip top requires the $\sinh$ numerator quoted here.
This is the stable time independent Stokes topography generated by the
harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the harmonic mode

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,$

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$p=P(z)\cos kx,\quad P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],$

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,$

$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
          =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,$

the steady deflected plate is material. The statement $u_{x}(0)=0$ is
$\Phi'(0)=0$ and the steady limit $\dot e=0$ is $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e.

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$ ,

the impermeable no-slip top.  On the biharmonic basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the
regular odd combination which satisfies both conditions can be written

$\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,$

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Then

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}p\,\cos kx $

and with the isostatic normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ in the steady state

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$.

At the base

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,$
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.$

With $s=\sinh kh,\;c=\cosh kh,\;a=kh$,

$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
(p+qh)c= k p a s ,$

i.e. $q=p\big[a\tanh a-1\big]/h$, and

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big|_{h}
   =-2k p\Big[\frac{c}{h}+k^{2}\frac{h}{c}\Big]
   =-\frac{2k p}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big].$

Hence

$S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],$

so that

$p=-\frac{S_{0}h c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]}$.

The free surface balance is therefore

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
   =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,s}{c^{2}+a^{2}} ,$

i.e. in the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}.$

With the plate density kept explicitly in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  For
$kh\ll1$, $\sinh kh/kh\to1$, $\cosh kh\to1$,

$\chi=kh+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},$

the familiar long-wave viscous pumping $e\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase shift, while
$\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the expected viscous screening.

The $kh\cosh kh/[c^{2}+a^{2}]$ form is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only limit
obtained by evaluating $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with
$W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before imposing the steady impermeability
$W'(0)=0$, i.e. by dropping the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution in
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ or keeping the transient
$W(0)=\dot e$ term.  Once the steady material condition
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$
contributions combine to the odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and the
normal-stress balance at the locked top selects the $\sinh kh$ numerator.
The thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$ is preserved, so the difference
is $O[(kh)^{2}]$ and numerically tiny for $kh\lesssim1$, which is why the
$\cosh$ and $\sinh$ forms are often quoted interchangeably.  With the
usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification this is the stable, time
independent Stokes topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

the steady deflected plate is material.  The statement gives
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $\dot e=0$, i.e. the free surface is
impermeable,

$\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad \Phi(0)=0$ ,

so that on the regular biharmonic

the admissible steady mode is the odd combination
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  With the full normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ the surface traction is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ on $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

so that in the steady limit

$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}$ .

At the base $z=h$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ and with $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$
$U\big(e^{2kh}+1\big)=-2khA$.  Eliminating $B,D$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=4\mu k^{2}A
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\cosh kh}
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$, 

so that with the impermeable top $W(0)=W'(0)=0$ the $e^{kz}$ and
$e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to the odd mode.  The solution of the
two base conditions is

$A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{3}}\,
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$ ,

and

$\Phi'''(0)=4k^{2}\big[B+2kA\big]
=-\frac{4k^{2}S_{0}}{\mu}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$ .

Hence with the complete $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$,

$\frac{\mu}{k}|\Phi'''(0)|=
S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$ .

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$ ,

         \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$ ,

$\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{0}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar

impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
term in $\sigma_{zz}$.  The $kh\cosh kh$ numerator obtained by evaluating

time independent Stokes topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

In the $k$ mode let

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material limit the top is locked and impermeable

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\iff 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\;\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and on the regular odd mode

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the normal stress written in the statement,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A ,\qquad 
A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{4\mu k^{2}} .
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0 ,\qquad
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. with $U=A+Bh$, $V=C+Dh$,

$$
Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh},\qquad U+V=-2khA .
$$

Eliminating $B,D$ gives

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{4\mu kA}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

hence with $a=kh$

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{4\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]} .
$$

Therefore on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},
\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that on the long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.  Writing the
restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_{0}(kh)\,
       \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv 
       \chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\Delta}(kh)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}.
$$

On the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this
is normally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\quad kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi(kh)\to0\;\;{\rm exponentially\;for}\;kh\gg1,
$$

i.e. the familiar viscous dynamic topography

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

with exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
Keeping the plate density $\rho$ explicit in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$ the factor in front of $S_{0}/\rho g$ is
$\chi_{0}$ above, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor being the only remaining
density dependence.  With the strict steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
the odd mode is often written with the $\sinh$ numerator

$$
\chi_{\rm sinh}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening.
This is the stable time independent Stokes topography generated by the
harmonic basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎
