\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
      =-\frac{2k^{2}A}{a\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big],
$$

so that

$$
S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k^{2}A}{a\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $A$ with (1) gives the viscosity free steady coupling

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},
\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

and $\mu$ drops out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

is the familiar viscous pumping law and $\chi_{0}\to0$ exponentially
for $kh\gg1$.  Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     \equiv\chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
the factor normally quoted is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. up to the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book keeping

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the stable,
time independent Stokes dynamic topography generated by the harmonic
basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  The $kh\sinh kh/[ (kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$
form obtained if the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term is kept in the
transient $W(0)=\dot e$ balance coincides with the expression above to
$O(kh)$ and gives the same thin–plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$.  With the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement
$e_{s}=\chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$ is the viscosity free steady response,
the long–wave limit being the quoted $\chi\simeq kh$ viscous
normal–stress coupling. ∎
public_text.19:
In the $k$ mode put
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0 ,
$$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

On the locked top $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\Phi'(0)=0$, and in the steady state the material surface is
impermeable $\Phi(0)=0$ so that with the regularisation
$C=-A$,

$$
D=-B-2kA,\qquad\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

Hence

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
           =-4\mu k^{2}A\cos kx =\rho g e(t)\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that in the steady state

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A .
$$

On the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} .
\tag{2}
$$

Putting $U=A+Bh$ the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0 $ condition is
$Ue^{kh}=Ve^{-kh}$ with $V=-A+Dh$, i.e. $U(e^{2kh}+1)=-2khA$, and

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}= -\frac{4kA}{h}
     \frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{\cosh kh}\; .
$$

Hence from (2)

$$
A=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}{4\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\;,
$$

and with (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad a\equiv kh .
$$

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

and $\mu$ drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that for a long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ viscous pumping $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.
Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

with exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
In the strict steady impermeable, $u_{z}(0)=0$, limit the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode is selected and the normal stress coupling can
be written in the equivalent $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form,
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, which coincides with the
expression above to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{s}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the usual $90^{\circ}$ shear to
topography phase shift.  This is the viscosity-free stable Stokes
topography generated by the harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping. ∎
public_text.3:
In the $k$–mode put $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$$
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi=0,
$$
so that with $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad (\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 .
$$
In the steady material state $u_{x}(0)=0,\;\dot e=0$,
$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
$$
so that on the regular biharmonic
$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz ,\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0 .
$$
Then
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}a\cos kx ,
$$
and with the imposed normal traction
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx$,
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}a ,
\tag{1}
$$
in the steady state.  On the base $z=h$
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0 ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$
With $\alpha=kh$
$$
a\cosh\alpha-h\big[ak\sinh\alpha-b\cosh\alpha\big]=0,
$$
i.e. 
$$
b=a\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}
  =ak\frac{\alpha\tanh\alpha-1}{\alpha},
$$
and
$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
   =-\frac{2ak^{2}}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
     \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$
Hence
$$
S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu a k^{2}}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] ,
$$
so that with (1)
$$
a=-\frac{S_{0}\alpha\cosh\alpha}
        {2\mu k^{2}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]},\qquad
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}a
          =S_{0}\,
            \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
                 {\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}\;,
$$
i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
       +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$
and the viscosity drops out of the steady response.  In particular
$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha},\;\alpha\gg1,
$$
so that for a long wave thin sheet
$$
e_{s}\simeq\alpha\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-topography viscous pumping
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g} .
$$
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is
normally quoted as
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
so that in the thin-plate long-wave limit
$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\quad kh\ll1,
$$
and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the inessential
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping this is the $ \alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ viscous–isostatic response.  The strict
steady impermeable, no-slip form is often written with the odd
numerator $\chi_{\rm sinh}= \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$; $\chi_{\rm sinh}=\chi_{0}+O(\alpha^{3})$, so that the
thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ are unchanged.  This is the
stable time independent dynamic topography generated by the harmonic
basal traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
public_text.6:
In the $k$ mode
$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\,,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx\,,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z} .
$$
On the locked material top in the steady state $\dot e=0$,
$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$
so that on the regular biharmonic
$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0,
$$
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
$$
With the normal stress written as in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p .
\tag{1}
$$
The base conditions are
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$
Writing $a=kh$,
$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
p\big(a\sinh a-\cosh a\big)-q h\cosh a=0,
$$
i.e.
$$
q=p\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad 
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kp}{h\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big] .
$$
Hence
$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h\cosh a}\Big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\Big],
$$
$$
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh a}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\big]} .
$$
With (1)
$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
          =S_{0}\,
            \frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},
\qquad a=kh,
$$
so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$$
e_{s}=\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
and the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  In particular
$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3})\quad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim 2a e^{-a}\quad a\gg1,
$$
i.e. the familiar long wave viscous pumping
$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
as
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$
so that with the plate density kept explicit
$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$
On the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ convention this is
$\chi(kh)=\chi_{0}(kh)$ and in the thin long-wave limit
$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The $kh\sinh kh$ form
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ coincides with the
expression above to $O(kh)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; the $\cosh$ numerator is the
strict $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ impermeable, no-slip steady limit.  Up to
the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ density book-keeping this is the
stable time independent dynamic topography generated by
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode for the 2-D incompressible layer is now essentially settled in the group. With the stream-function ansatz
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$,
the top is locked $u_x(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady material limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is impermeable $u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$. 
Hence $C=-A$, $B+D+2kA=0$ and the regular odd basis is $\Phi\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$. The base conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$.
Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

The majority line in round 3, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20,21,3,4,6,8, continues to quote the viscosity-free steady coupling

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\chi_0(\alpha)$,
$\chi_0(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

i.e. $e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\rho g$ and with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

which on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is

$e_s=\chi(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.

$\chi_0=a+O(a^3)$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$, so the thin-plate long-wave limit

$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$, and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$, is robust across the majority.

A persistent minority, Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9, keeps the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ and obtains the odd-mode form

$\chi_{\rm sinh}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\chi_0(\alpha)\tanh\alpha$,

i.e. $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm sinh}S_0/\Delta\rho g$, with the same thin-plate limit $\chi_{\rm sinh}= \alpha+O(\alpha^3)$ and the same $2\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ screening. The two forms coincide to $O(\alpha)$, differ only by the $\sinh\alpha/\cosh\alpha$ factor, i.e. $O(\alpha^3)$ in the thin-plate limit.

Density book-keeping remains explicit: formally $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$. With the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the quoted factor is $\chi=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]\approx kh$.

Unresolved is the exact numerator in the $O(\alpha^3)$ term, i.e. whether the strict steady impermeable, $2\mu\partial_z u_z$-retaining mode selects the $\cosh\alpha$ or the $\sinh\alpha$ numerator. The long-wave viscous pumping law $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, viscosity independence, $90^{\circ}$ phase and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable across all derivations and were already present in the previous round.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady harmonic Stokes mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

Steady material top $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$ gives in the regular biharmonic
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi=c_0[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+d\,z\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^3c_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)
=-2\mu k^{2}c_0\cos kx$ and with the statement normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$c_0=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\!\iff\!\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\!\iff\!\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives 
$d=c_0[ kh\tanh kh-1]/h$ and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=-2\mu k c_0\,[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_0$.
Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]$,
$e_s=\chi_0(kh)S_0/\rho g$,
$\chi_0(a)=a\cosh a/[a^2+\cosh^2a]
=[\cosh a/a+a\,\operatorname{sech}a]^{-1}$, $a=kh$.
$\mu$ drops out. 
$\chi_0=a+O(a^3)$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}\to0$ for $a\gg1$,
$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Writing the restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[k^2h^2+\cosh^2kh]
=[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$.

Disagreement in the logs is the book-keeping of the steady impermeability.
Imposing the strict material steady top $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with
the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ selects the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  The free-surface traction is then carried by
the odd combination and the numerator becomes $\sinh kh$:
$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^2+\cosh^2a]=\chi_0(a)\tanh a$.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^3)$ and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2a e^{-a}$,
so the thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the exponential
screening are identical to $O(kh)$.  Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20,3,4,6,8
quote the $\cosh$ numerator $\chi_0$; colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21,9
quote the odd $\sinh$ numerator $\chi_{\rm odd}$.  The two forms coincide
to $O(kh)$, $\sinh kh/kh=1+O(a^2)$, $\cosh kh=1+O(a^2)$, hence the
commonly quoted thin-plate law $e_s\approx kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi\simeq kh$, is robust.
The remaining unresolved book-keeping is the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$
factor in $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ versus $e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\rho g$, and
the $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ numerator which is $O[(kh)^2]$ in the long-wave
limit normally quoted.

18.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$. 
Steady locked material top: $u_x(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$. The strict steady material limit also needs impermeability $u_z(0)=0$ i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. On the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the regular odd mode is $\Phi\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $z\sinh kz$ partner needed at the base.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$. Top: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ in the statement, normally quoted with isostatic $\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

Eliminating the constants gives a viscosity-free steady coupling. With the $u_x(0)=0$ only / $W(0)=\dot e$ evaluation that is used by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20 etc.

$\rho g e_s = S_0\,\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$, $a=kh$,

$e_s =\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$, $\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}$.

$\chi_0=a+O(a^3)$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$. Viscosity cancels in the steady state, $90^\circ$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.

Isostatic normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$. With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the factor quoted in $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$, $kh\ll1$, $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit.

This is the $a\cosh a/[a^2+\cosh^2a]$ viscous-isostatic response.

Unresolved/nuanced disagreement in the round: strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode. With that strict limit the free-surface coupling is carried by the odd combination and the numerator becomes $\sinh$ instead of $\cosh$:
$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=\dfrac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
 =\chi_0(a)\tanh a$,
i.e. $e_s= \chi_{\rm odd} S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^3)$ and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for large $a$, so the thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the $90^\circ$ phase and the exponential screening are identical to $O(kh)$. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21 highlight this $\sinh$ numerator as the correct steady impermeable no-slip result; colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20 keep the $u_x(0)=0$ only evaluation giving the $\cosh$ numerator.

Hence the robust stable physics is $e_s\propto S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with dimensionless factor $\sim kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential decay for $kh\gg1$, viscosity-free in steady state. The exact numerator is $a\cosh a$ in the $u_x(0)=0$ transient evaluation and $a\sinh a$ in the strict $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ steady impermeable limit, indistinguishable to $O(kh)$. With the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification the textbook factor is $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh]\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$.

19.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

Steady material top $u_x(0)=0$ gives $\Phi'(0)=0$. In the truly steady limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is also impermeable $u_z(0)=0$ i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$, hence on the regular biharmonic $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the admissible odd mode is $\Phi\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ up to the $z\sinh kz$ partner required at the base. Viscosity drops out of the steady coupling.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$. Top normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives $\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.

Eliminating $B,D$ gives the viscosity free steady response on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$$
\rho g e_s = S_0\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh},
$$
i.e.
$$
e_s =\chi_0(kh)\frac{S_0}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_0(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^2+\cosh^2a}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\quad a=kh,
$$
$$
\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^3),\;a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_0(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\;a\gg1,
$$
so $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. The $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase is standard.

Writing the restoring stress in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$. With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$$
e_s= \chi(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$
hence $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$.

Round 3 is split on the numerator. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20,21 derive the $kh\cosh kh/[a^2+\cosh^2a]$ form from $u_x(0)=0$ with the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ evaluation $ \sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9,21 enforce the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and keep the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$, which selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and gives the odd form
$$
\chi_{\rm sinh}(a)=\frac{a\sinh a}{a^2+\cosh^2a},
$$
i.e. $e_s= S_0\,\chi_{\rm sinh}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping. To $O(a)$, $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^2)$ so $\chi_{\rm sinh}=a+O(a^3)$ and $\chi_{\rm sinh}\equiv\chi_0$ to leading order. The thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the $kh$ viscous pumping law, the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening are robust across both presentations.

The remaining unresolved book keeping is the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor: the statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ while the requested normalisation is $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Hence formally $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$, which reduces to the textbook $\chi_0$ on the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification. Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-3 discussion is a repetition of the two-stream split established earlier. The Stokes set-up is common:

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, 
$p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

Steady material top is $u_x(0)=0$ and in the steady limit $\dot e=0$,
$u_z(0)=0$.  On the regular biharmonic this is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, $\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.

Basal conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ give with $a=kh$

$[A+Bh]e^{kh}=[C+Dh]e^{-kh}$, $U(1+e^{2a})=-2aA$, and

$A=-\dfrac{S_0 h\cosh a}{4\mu k\,[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]}$.

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\rho g e_s=-4\mu k^{2}A=S_0\,\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$,

$e_s=\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$,
$\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
      =\big[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a\big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$.

Viscosity cancels. $\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^3)$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2ae^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$ long wave, $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$, exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. This is the $kh\cosh$ form repeatedly given in round 3 by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,21.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is quoted as

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^2+\cosh^2 kh]$,
$\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

Minority stream Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7 keeps the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ together with the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. the odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$. The free-surface coupling then becomes

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$,

$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=\dfrac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
     =\chi_0(a)\tanh a$,

$e_s=\chi_{\rm odd}S_0/\Delta\rho g$, with the same $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping if the statement’s $\rho g$ normalisation is kept. To $O(a)$ $\sinh a=a+O(a^3)$, $\cosh a=1+O(a^2)$ so $\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^3)=\chi_0+O(a^3)$; the thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the $2ae^{-a}$ screening are unchanged. The $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ split is therefore $ \tanh kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$ and is degenerate in the long-wave limit.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $k$-mode set-up is now essentially fixed in round 3. With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$,
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

The steady material top is locked in $x$, $u_x(0)=0$, and in the
steady limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is impermeable,
$u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. On the regular biharmonic
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the admissible odd mode can be written
$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}a$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}a\cos kx$.

Base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$ the two base conditions give
$b=a\,[a\tanh a-1]h^{-1}a$, and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2\mu k a\,[a^{2}+c^{2}]/(a c/h)$,
so that, on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement,

$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
 =S_{0}\,\dfrac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh$,

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
          =[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a]^{-1}
          =[\cosh a/a+a\,\text{sech}a]^{-1}$,
and $\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  In particular
$\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a}$,
$a\gg1$, so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-normal shift $\sin kx\to\cos kx$,
with exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,
so that with the density kept explicit in the statement
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping the long-wave thin
plate limit is

$\chi(kh)=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$kh\ll1$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

Current round disagreement: a persistent minority, 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21,
imposes the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the

the free-surface coupling with the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode as

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.
$\chi_{\rm odd}= \chi_{0}\tanh kh$, so $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$
and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  To $O(kh)$ the two
forms coincide, $\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, and both give the

same exponential screening.  The difference is the $O[(kh)^{2}]$
book-keeping of the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term and the order in which
the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ condition $W'(0)=0$ is imposed.

The majority of colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20 in round 3 retain the

quoted as the stable viscous dynamic topography.  Viscosity cancels,

presentations.  The unresolved book-keeping remains the explicit

statement versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the question.

The regular biharmonic is

The material steady top is $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$, i.e. in the strictly
steady limit $u_z(0)=0$,

$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b\,z\sinh kz$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,

$b=a[a_0\tanh a_0-1]/h$ and
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2k a\,[c^{2}+a_0^{2}]/(h c)$.
Hence
$S_{0}= -2\mu k a\,[c^{2}+a_0^{2}]/(h c)$,
$a=-S_{0}h c/[2\mu k(c^{2}+a_0^{2})]$,
and on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,a_0c/(a_0^{2}+c^{2})$.

$e_s=\chi_{0}(a_0)S_{0}/\rho g$,

       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}$,

$e_s\simeq a S_{0}/\rho g=kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ with the $90^{\circ}$

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
On the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
this is normally quoted as
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,
$\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.

$q=p\big(a\tanh a-1\big)/h$,

+2k^{2}h\sinh a\,q
=-\dfrac{2kp}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]$.

Hence
$S_{0}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
     =-\dfrac{2\mu kp}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]$,
$p=-\dfrac{S_{0}h\,c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]}$,
and

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
       =S_{0}\dfrac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}}$,
$a=kh$,

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}$,
$\chi_{0}(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}$,

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state.
In particular

$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$,

so that for a thin long wave sheet

$e_{s}\simeq a\,S_{0}/\rho g=kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$e_{s}= \dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv
       \chi_{\Delta}(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,

which is the stable time independent Stokes topography generated by
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

The $a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ odd numerator quoted by a minority
of colleagues is the $W(0)=\dot e$ transient evaluation, i.e. the
$u_{x}(0)=0$ only limit before the steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the full $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ stress are
imposed.  It coincides with the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ form to
$O(a)$, $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$, and gives the same thin-plate
limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same
$2kh e^{-kh}$ screening.  With the strict steady impermeable, no-slip
top the odd $ \sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode is selected and the viscosity
free response is the $a\cosh a/(a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a)$ factor above,
normally quoted with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ as
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\simeq kh$. ∎

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $k$ mode can be written with the stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $p=P\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
           =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
A material steady top is $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$, i.e. $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  On the regular biharmonic
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the
regular odd mode can be written
$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}a$.
Hence
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}a\cos kx
               =\rho g e\cos kx$,
$a=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ and the viscosity drops out of the steady
response.

The base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.  With
$a=kh$, $C=\cosh a$, $S=\sinh a$
$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff a(-C+kzS)=bzC$,
so that $b=a\,[a\tanh a-1]/h$ and

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big|_{h}
     =-\frac{2ka}{hC}\big[C^{2}+a^{2}\big] .
$$

Hence
$S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
     =-\dfrac{2\mu k a}{hC}\big[C^{2}+a^{2}\big]$,
$a=-\dfrac{S_{0}hC}{2\mu k\big[C^{2}+a^{2}\big]}$ and with
$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}a$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{aC}{a^{2}+C^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
$$

with $\mu$ cancelled.  In particular
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$,
$\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$, so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping, and
exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.
The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the only remaining density book-keeping;
on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement the stable amplitude
is $e_{s}= \chi_{0}S_{0}/\rho g$.

The minority $\sinh$ form
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
is the odd-mode expression obtained with the strict steady impermeability
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$.
It coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{s}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the identical thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening.
The $kh\cosh kh$ and $kh\sinh kh$ forms are therefore equivalent to
leading order in $kh$, which is why the long-wave $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is universally quoted.  The sign/phase is the
usual $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shear-to-normal stress shift and the viscosity
cancels in the steady state. ∎

20.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream-function $ \psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.
With $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $ \dot e=0$ the material top is impermeable,
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$.  On the $e^{\pm kz}$ basis this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$
and the regular odd mode can be written
$\Phi=C_1[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+C_2z\sinh kz$
with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.
Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}C_1\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives $C_1=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
Zero normal traction at $z=h$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$, gives
$C_1\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]+C_2h\cosh kh=0$, i.e.
$C_2=-C_1\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/h\cosh kh$.
The basal shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$
becomes
$S_0= -2\mu kC_1\,[ \cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}]/[h\cosh kh]$.
Eliminating $C_1$,

$\rho g e_s=S_0\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_0(kh)S_0/\rho g$, $\qquad 
\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$, 
$\chi_0=a+O(a^3)$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.
Viscosity cancels in the steady state and the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear-to-normal stress shift.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
this is quoted as

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
=\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

and in the thin-plate long wave limit

$\chi(kh)=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The minority $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form appears if the
$2\mu\partial_z u_z$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is evaluated before imposing the
steady impermeability $W'(0)=0$, i.e. with the transient $W(0)=\dot e$
balance kept.  With the strict steady material conditions
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode is selected and the
free-surface coupling is the $\cosh$ numerator above; the two forms coincide
to $O(kh)$, $\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$, so both give the same thin-plate
limit $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the same exponential screening.
The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping is inessential; with $\rho$ kept
explicitly in the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ the factor in front
of $S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is $(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$, which reduces to the
textbook $\chi_0$ on the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification.  This
is the stable, viscosity-free Stokes topography generated by
$\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$ under $u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

reflection_text.3:
The harmonic Stokes mode for the 2-D incompressible layer is now essentially settled in the group. With the stream-function ansatz
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$,
the top is locked $u_x(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady material limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is impermeable $u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$. 
Hence $C=-A$, $B+D+2kA=0$ and the regular odd basis is $\Phi\propto\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$. The base conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$.
Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

The majority line in round 3, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20,21,3,4,6,8, continues to quote the viscosity-free steady coupling

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\chi_0(\alpha)$,
$\chi_0(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

i.e. $e_s=\chi_0 S_0/\rho g$ and with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

which on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is

$e_s=\chi(\alpha)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.

$\chi_0=a+O(a^3)$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$, so the thin-plate long-wave limit

$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

with the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$, and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$, is robust across the majority.

A persistent minority, Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9, keeps the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ and obtains the odd-mode form

$\chi_{\rm sinh}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\chi_0(\alpha)\tanh\alpha$,

i.e. $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm sinh}S_0/\Delta\rho g$, with the same thin-plate limit $\chi_{\rm sinh}= \alpha+O(\alpha^3)$ and the same $2\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ screening. The two forms coincide to $O(\alpha)$, differ only by the $\sinh\alpha/\cosh\alpha$ factor, i.e. $O(\alpha^3)$ in the thin-plate limit.

Unresolved is the exact numerator in the $O(\alpha^3)$ term, i.e. whether the strict steady impermeable, $2\mu\partial_z u_z$-retaining mode selects the $\cosh\alpha$ or the $\sinh\alpha$ numerator. The long-wave viscous pumping law $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, viscosity independence, $90^{\circ}$ phase and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable across all derivations and were already present in the previous round.

\chi_0(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\;a\gg1,

so $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. The $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase is standard.

Writing the restoring stress in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is $e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$. With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$$
e_s= \chi(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$
hence $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$.

Round 3 is split on the numerator. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20,21 derive the $kh\cosh kh/[a^2+\cosh^2a]$ form from $u_x(0)=0$ with the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ evaluation $ \sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9,21 enforce the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and keep the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$, which selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and gives the odd form
$$
\chi_{\rm sinh}(a)=\frac{a\sinh a}{a^2+\cosh^2a},
$$
i.e. $e_s= S_0\,\chi_{\rm sinh}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping. To $O(a)$, $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^2)$ so $\chi_{\rm sinh}=a+O(a^3)$ and $\chi_{\rm sinh}\equiv\chi_0$ to leading order. The thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the $kh$ viscous pumping law, the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening are robust across both presentations.

The remaining unresolved book keeping is the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor: the statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ while the requested normalisation is $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Hence formally $\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0$, which reduces to the textbook $\chi_0$ on the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification. Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

reflection_text.12:
The round-3 discussion is a repetition of the two-stream split established earlier. The Stokes set-up is common:

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, 
$p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$.

Steady material top is $u_x(0)=0$ and in the steady limit $\dot e=0$,
$u_z(0)=0$.  On the regular biharmonic this is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, $\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.

Basal conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ give with $a=kh$

$[A+Bh]e^{kh}=[C+Dh]e^{-kh}$, $U(1+e^{2a})=-2aA$, and

$A=-\dfrac{S_0 h\cosh a}{4\mu k\,[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]}$.

Hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\rho g e_s=-4\mu k^{2}A=S_0\,\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$,

$e_s=\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$,
$\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
      =\big[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a\big]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$.

Viscosity cancels. $\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^3)$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2ae^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$ long wave, $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$, exponential screening for $kh\gg1$. This is the $kh\cosh$ form repeatedly given in round 3 by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,21.

Writing the restoring stress in the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is quoted as

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(kh)=\chi_0(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^2+\cosh^2 kh]$,
$\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

Minority stream Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7 keeps the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ together with the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. the odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$. The free-surface coupling then becomes

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}$,

$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=\dfrac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
     =\chi_0(a)\tanh a$,

$e_s=\chi_{\rm odd}S_0/\Delta\rho g$, with the same $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book-keeping if the statement’s $\rho g$ normalisation is kept. To $O(a)$ $\sinh a=a+O(a^3)$, $\cosh a=1+O(a^2)$ so $\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^3)=\chi_0+O(a^3)$; the thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the $2ae^{-a}$ screening are unchanged. The $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ split is therefore $ \tanh kh=1+O[(kh)^2]$ and is degenerate in the long-wave limit.

Unresolved carried forward: 
- explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor: statement uses $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ whereas the requested form is $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$; the conventional identification absorbs $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.
- whether strict steady impermeability $u_z(0)=0,\;\Phi(0)=0$ is to be imposed in addition to $u_x(0)=0$. Imposing it selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and the $\sinh kh$ numerator; evaluating $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with only $u_x(0)=0$ gives the $kh\cosh kh$ numerator.
- sign convention.

The thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and exponential viscous screening for $kh\gg1$ are stable across both families and constitute the robust part of the deliberation.

The steady material top is locked in $x$, $u_x(0)=0$, and in the
steady limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is impermeable,
$u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. On the regular biharmonic
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the admissible odd mode can be written
$\Phi(z)=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}a$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}a\cos kx$.

Base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$ the two base conditions give
$b=a\,[a\tanh a-1]h^{-1}a$, and
$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2\mu k a\,[a^{2}+c^{2}]/(a c/h)$,
so that, on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement,

$\rho g e_{s}=-4\mu k^{2}A
 =S_{0}\,\dfrac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh$,

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
          =[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a]^{-1}
          =[\cosh a/a+a\,\text{sech}a]^{-1}$,
and $\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  In particular
$\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a}$,
$a\gg1$, so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-normal shift $\sin kx\to\cos kx$,
with exponential screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the conventional geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ as

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,\operatorname{sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,
so that with the density kept explicit in the statement
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping the long-wave thin
plate limit is

$\chi(kh)=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$kh\ll1$,

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

Current round disagreement: a persistent minority, 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21,
imposes the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the
full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ at the locked top and writes
the free-surface coupling with the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode as

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.
$\chi_{\rm odd}= \chi_{0}\tanh kh$, so $\chi_{\rm odd}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$
and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  To $O(kh)$ the two
forms coincide, $\sinh kh/\cosh kh=1+O[(kh)^{2}]$, and both give the
identical thin-plate law $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
same exponential screening.  The difference is the $O[(kh)^{2}]$
book-keeping of the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ term and the order in which
the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ condition $W'(0)=0$ is imposed.

The majority of colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20 in round 3 retain the
$kh\cosh kh/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$ form quoted above, with the usual
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ density conversion, and that is the form most often
quoted as the stable viscous dynamic topography.  Viscosity cancels,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase is preserved, and the thin-plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is robust across both
presentations.  The unresolved book-keeping remains the explicit
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor coming from $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$ in the
statement versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the question.

     =-2\mu kp\,[c^{2}+a^{2}]/[hc]$,

viscous-isostatic response.

$$p\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=qh\cosh kh,
\qquad 
q=p\frac{kh\tanh kh-1}{h}, $$

and

$$\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =-\frac{2kp}{h\cosh kh}\Big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] .$$

Hence

$$S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h\cosh kh}
       \Big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] , $$

$$p=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
          {2\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\; .$$

With (1)

$$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
      =S_{0}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad a\equiv kh , $$

so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
         =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad a=kh, $$

and the viscosity cancels out of the steady response.  In particular

$$\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\; a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\;a\gg1, $$

i.e. the familiar viscous pumping

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

with the $90^{o}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ and exponential screening
for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)e_{\rho}$, the same Stokes solution is
normally quoted with the conventional identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
as

$$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping kept explicit

$$e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}. $$

On the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1, $$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The odd–mode
$\chi_{s}=kh\sinh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ obtained with the strict
$W'(0)=0$ impermeability coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(kh)$,
$\chi_{s}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, and gives the same thin–plate limit
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the usual $2kh\,e^{-kh}$
screening.  The viscosity drops out of the steady state and the shear
to normal stress shift is the conventional $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous
dynamic topography. ∎

1.text:
With the harmonic mode put
$\psi (x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
        =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the time independent limit the deflected surface is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$, i.e.

$$
u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

the regular odd impermeable mode.  On the biharmonic basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and up
to an inessential constant

$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,\qquad
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Then
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
$$
With the normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p, \qquad p=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
$$

The base conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

With $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$,

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
p\big(a s-c\big)=q h c,
$$

$$
q=p\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad 
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kp}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big] .
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kp}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],
\qquad 
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\,c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]} .
$$

Using (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\tag{2}
$$

and $\mu$ drops out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that for the long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
e_{\rho}$, the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$
so that

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The viscosity free
steady Stokes topography is therefore the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$
response, $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the thin plate long
wave limit.  The odd–mode form
$\chi_{s}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}\tanh a$ coincides with
$\chi_{0}$ to $O(a)$, $\chi_{s}=a+O(a^{3})$, and gives the identical
thin–plate limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same
$2kh e^{-kh}$ screening, the $ \sinh/\cosh$ difference being the
$O[(kh)^{2}]$ transient $W(0)=\dot e$ term which vanishes in the strict
steady impermeable limit $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  This is the stable time
independent dynamic topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

         =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

and $\mu$ drops out of the steady response.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a\,e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that with the $90^{\circ}$ shear to normal phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar viscous pumping law, and $\chi_{0}\to0$ exponentially for
$kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_{0}(kh)
       \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\equiv 
       \chi_{\Delta}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;,
$$

and on the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

with the exponential screening $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
The $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is the usual shear to
normal-stress shift and the steady response is viscosity free.

With the strict steady impermeable, no-slip material top
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ the regular odd mode
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ is selected.  The free surface coupling is then
often written in the odd form

$$
\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=\frac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
               =\chi_{0}(a)\tanh a ,
$$

so that $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm odd}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for
$a\gg1$, hence

$$
\chi_{\rm odd}=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the same thin-plate long-wave limit and the same exponential screening
as the $\cosh$ form.  The $\cosh$ expression above is the
$u_{x}(0)=0$ evaluation commonly quoted; it coincides with the odd
$\sinh$ form to $O(kh)$ and gives the familiar stable time independent
Stokes topography $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ generated by
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase
shift.  Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping this is the
viscosity-free steady dynamic topography. ∎

The stream-function set-up is common and the only physical distinction is how the steady material top is imposed. With
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
       =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,

the $k$ mode is completely regular. The top is a deflected material plate. The statement gives $u_{x}(0)=0$ and, in the steady state, $\dot e=0$. The steady state is material, hence

$u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$,

i.e. the strict steady impermeability

$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

not $u_{x}(0)=0$ alone. On $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ with
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the regular odd mode is

$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q\,z\sinh kz$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. The $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is then retained,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$,

so that with the isostatic normalisation used for the topography
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$ .
$1$ .

At the base 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $s=\sinh kh$, $c=\cosh kh$, $\alpha=kh$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$(p+qh)c=kphs$, i.e. $q=p[\alpha\tanh\alpha-1]/h$, and

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi|_{h}
=-2kp\Big[c/h+k^{2}h/c\Big]
=-2kp\,[c^{2}+\alpha^{2}]/[h c]$.

Hence
$S_{0}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
     =-2\mu kp\,[c^{2}+\alpha^{2}]/[h c]$,

$p=-\,S_{0}h c/\{2\mu k[c^{2}+\alpha^{2}]\}$.

When the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is kept together with the steady impermeability $W'(0)=0$, the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ pieces combine so that the free-surface traction is carried by the odd combination $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$. The free-surface coupling then brings the factor $\sinh kh$, not $\cosh kh$, into the normal stress balance.

Eliminating $p$ from the surface balance,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
    =S_{0}\,\dfrac{\alpha\,s}{c^{2}+\alpha^{2}}$,

i.e. in the usual notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase being the familiar shear-to-normal stress shift. With the plate density kept explicitly in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping.

In particular
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the expected viscous pumping and exponential screening. The thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $90^{\circ}$ phase are preserved.

The $kh\cosh kh/[ \cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ form quoted by 1,10,11,12,15,18,6 is the evaluation of $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$, i.e. the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only evaluation with the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ retained and the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ contribution effectively dropped at $z=0$. Once the steady material condition $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is enforced together with the complete $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, the regular odd mode $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ is selected and the stable time-independent amplitude is the $\sinh$ numerator above. With the $k$ mode $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_x=\Phi' \sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,

the steady material free surface is locked and impermeable.  In the
time independent limit $\dot e=0$ the surface is material so that
$u_x(0)=0$ and $u_z(0)=0$,
\[
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
\]
and not $u_x(0)=0$ alone.  On the regular biharmonic
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the
regular odd impermeable mode can be written

\[
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
\]

so that the $e^{\pm kz}$ even part is removed by the steady
impermeability.  Then
\[
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
\]

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
in the steady state
\[
\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p,\qquad p=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_s}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\]

\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and the imposed basal shear is
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.
With $s=\sinh kh$, $c=\cosh kh$, $a=kh$,

\[
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff(p+qh)c=kp a s ,
\]

\[
\Phi''+k^2\Phi\big|_h
=-2kp\Big[\frac{c}{h}+k^{2}h\frac1c\Big]
=-\frac{2kp}{hc}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big].
\]

\[

   =-\frac{2\mu kp}{hc}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],\qquad
p=-\frac{S_0hc}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]} .
\]

\[

   =S_0\,\frac{a\,s}{c^{2}+a^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
\]
i.e. with the conventional notation $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
\[

\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase being the usual shear to
normal stress shift.  With the plate density kept explicit in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$
book keeping that is absorbed on the geophysical identification
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$.

In particular $\sinh kh/kh\to1$ for $kh\ll1$ and
\[

\qquad kh\ll1,
\]
and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous pumping
and exponential screening.  The $kh\cosh kh/[c^{2}+a^{2}]$ form is the

steady impermeability $W'(0)=0$, i.e. the transient $W(0)=\dot e$
contribution.  Once the steady material condition $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
is enforced together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$,
the $e^{kz}$ and $e^{-kz}$ contributions combine to the odd mode
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and the normal stress at the locked top selects the

$\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$ with $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and

the steady response.

In the $k$–mode put

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0  $$

and $p=P(z)\cos kx$.  Then

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}-k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}\big],
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx , $$

$$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
       =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}-3k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}\big]
         \cos kx . $$

In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$ the free surface is locked and
impermeable

$$u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff 
\Phi(0)=\Phi^{\prime}(0)=0 , $$

on the regular biharmonic

$$\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi^{\prime}(0)=0, $$

so that

$$\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx . $$

With the normalisation used in the statement

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\qquad\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p. \tag{1}$$

On the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)-3k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}(h)=0,
\qquad \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}, $$

i.e.

$$p\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big]=qh\cosh kh,
\qquad 
q=p\frac{kh\tanh kh-1}{h}, $$

and

$$\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =-\frac{2kp}{h\cosh kh}\Big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] .$$

Hence

$$S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu k p}{h\cosh kh}
       \Big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\Big] , $$

$$p=-\frac{S_{0}h\cosh kh}
          {2\mu k\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]}\; .$$

$$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
      =S_{0}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad a\equiv kh , $$

$$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad

         =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},

to normal stress shift is the conventional $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous

public_text.1:
With the harmonic mode put
$\psi (x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
        =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the time independent limit the deflected surface is material,
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$, i.e.

$$
u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

the regular odd impermeable mode.  On the biharmonic basis
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and up
to an inessential constant

$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,\qquad
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Then
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
$$
With the normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p, \qquad p=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
$$

The base conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
$$

With $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$,

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
p\big(a s-c\big)=q h c,
$$

$$
q=p\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},\qquad 
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kp}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big] .
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kp}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],
\qquad 
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\,c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]} .
$$

Using (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
$$

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\tag{2}
$$

and $\mu$ drops out of the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that for the long wave thin sheet

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
e_{\rho}$, the same Stokes solution is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and with the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$
so that

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  The viscosity free
steady Stokes topography is therefore the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$
response, $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the thin plate long
wave limit.  The odd–mode form
$\chi_{s}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}\tanh a$ coincides with
$\chi_{0}$ to $O(a)$, $\chi_{s}=a+O(a^{3})$, and gives the identical
thin–plate limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same
$2kh e^{-kh}$ screening, the $ \sinh/\cosh$ difference being the
$O[(kh)^{2}]$ transient $W(0)=\dot e$ term which vanishes in the strict
steady impermeable limit $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  This is the stable time
independent dynamic topography generated by $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

 =-\frac{2kp}{h\,c}\Big[c^{2}+a^{2}\Big] .

     =-\frac{2\mu kp}{h\,c}\Big[c^{2}+a^{2}\Big] ,

$$
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\,c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]} ,

          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}} .
$$

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1},
\;\;a=kh ,
$$

and the viscosity cancels in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad

       \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},

i.e. with the conventional geophysical identification

$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ generated by the harmonic basal

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream-function set up is now common ground.

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\;u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,  
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,   $p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,  
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,  
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

On the regular biharmonic $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.  In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$.  The $u_x(0)=0$ condition is $\Phi'(0)=0$.  The strict material condition adds $u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the odd impermeable mode

$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$.

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-4\mu k^2A\cos kx$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.

With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$, $U=A+Bh$,

$W(h)=0\iff U(e^{2a}+1)=-2aA$; the shear condition gives

$A=-\dfrac{S_0 h c}{4\mu k\,[a^2+c^2]}$,

hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\rho g e_s=-4\mu k^2A=S_0\,\dfrac{a c}{a^2+c^2}$,

$e_s=\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$,

$\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^2+\cosh^2 a}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels.  $\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^3)$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.  Long wave $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$, $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$, exponential screening.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ quoted as
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2 kh}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Disagreement carried from earlier rounds persists: imposing strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  With the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term kept at the locked top the free-surface coupling becomes

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,a s/(c^2+a^2)$,

$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/(a^2+\cosh^2 a)=\chi_0(a)\tanh a$.

$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^3)$, i.e. the thin plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the $2a e^{-a}$ screening are unchanged; $\sinh/\cosh$ difference is $O(a^2)$, degenerate in the long wave limit.  Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20 continue to quote the $\cosh$ numerator $\chi_0$ as the stable response, Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21 quote the odd $\sinh$ numerator $\chi_{\rm odd}$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor and sign convention remain book-keeping issues.  The robust part of the deliberation is viscosity-free steady response, $90^{\circ}$ phase, $\chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The k-mode Stokes problem is now essentially settled in form. With 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.
On the regular biharmonic $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

In the strict steady material limit $\dot e=0$ the deflected top is locked
and impermeable, $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  
Then $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the admissible odd impermeable mode can be written
$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q\,z\sinh kz$.
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$.
With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p$.  Base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$
give with $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$
$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$ and $[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=-2kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$.
Hence $S_0=-2\mu kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$ and
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,a c/(a^{2}+c^{2})$,

$e_s=\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$, $\chi_0(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
=[\cosh a/a+a\,\operatorname{sech}a]^{-1}$,
$\mu$ cancels.  $\chi_0=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$.
In particular $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$, with the familiar
$90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shift and exponential screening for
$kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is usually quoted as
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=[\cosh a/a+a\,\operatorname{sech}a]^{-1}$,
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The persistent minority 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21 imposes the steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ at the locked top and keeps the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ coupling.  The free-surface balance then becomes
$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p$ with the same base conditions, giving
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,a s/(c^{2}+a^{2})$,
i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_0(a)\tanh a$.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.
To $O(a)$ $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$ so $\chi_{\rm odd}=\chi_0+O(a^{3})$
and both give identical thin-plate law $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and
the same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening. The $\cosh$ form is the $u_x(0)=0$ only
evaluation $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before enforcing the steady impermeability
$W'(0)=0$; the $\sinh$ form is the strict $W'(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
odd-mode selection with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term retained.

The unresolved book-keeping remains the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor
coming from $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$ in the statement versus
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in the question.  Up to that harmless density
conversion the viscosity-free steady Stokes topography is the
$a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ response, $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$
in the long-wave thin-plate limit, with the $90^{\circ}$ phase and
exponential screening.  The odd-mode $\sinh$ numerator is the strict
steady-impermeable version and coincides with the $\cosh$ version to
$O(kh)$, which is why the thin-plate limit is robust across colleagues.
