PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ is the common set up.  
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,  
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

In the time independent limit the deflected top is material.  The statement gives $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $\dot e=0$ so that $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. the regular impermeable mode

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$.

With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$, $p=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$,

$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff p(a s-c)=qh c$,
$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$,

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kp[c/h+k^{2}h/c]=-2kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$.

Hence
$S_{0}= -2\mu kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$, $p=-S_{0}hc/[2\mu k(c^{2}+a^{2})]$,
and
$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p=S_{0}a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$.

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)S_{0}/\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
=[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

and $\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$,
so that for the long wave thin sheet
$e_{s}\simeq aS_{0}/\rho g=kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$,
the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh]^{-1}$,
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The odd-mode form $\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}\tanh a$
is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only, $W(0)=\dot e$, transient evaluation.  It coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(a)$, $\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$, and gives the identical thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening.  Imposing the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ selects the regular odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and the viscosity-free steady Stokes topography above, i.e. up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping the stable response is the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ viscous-isostatic factor, normally quoted as $\chi\approx kh$ in the long-wave limit. ∎

On the regular biharmonic $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$ this is $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the regular odd impermeable mode can be written $ \Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+qz\sinh kz$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  

With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$,

$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p$, $p=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.  With $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$, the no normal traction condition gives $(p+qh)c=k h p s$, $q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$, and

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kp[c/h+k^{2}h/c]=-2kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$.

Hence $S_{0}= -2\mu kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$ and with $\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p$

$\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$,

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_{0}(a)S_{0}/\rho g$, $\chi_{0}(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels in the steady state, the phase is $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$,

$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$,

so for a long-wave thin sheet $e_s\simeq a S_{0}/\rho g=kh S_{0}/\rho g$ and the response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is quoted as

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_s\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

Round-4 disagreement persists on the strict steady impermeability.  Imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  With $W'(0)=0$ retained the free-surface coupling is then carried by the odd combination and the free-surface balance can be written

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,a\sinh a/[c^{2}+a^{2}]$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}(a)\tanh a$.  Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21 advocate this $\sinh$ numerator, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20 keep the $u_x(0)=0$ only evaluation with $W(0)=\dot e$ retained, giving the $\cosh$ numerator above.  The two forms coincide to $O(a)$,

$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$, $\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$,

so the thin-plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening are robust.  The $kh\cosh kh/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ expression is the one most often quoted in the literature with the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification, and is the viscosity-free stable Stokes dynamic topography generated by $\tau_b=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

impermeable kinematics.  With the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$,
$\rho ge_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$, $p=-\rho ge_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$,

$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff p[a s-c]=qh c$, 
$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$,

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kp[c/h+k^{2}h/c]
=-2kp[a^{2}+c^{2}]/hc$.

Hence
$S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2\mu kp[a^{2}+c^{2}]/hc$,
$p=-S_{0}hc/[2\mu k(a^{2}+c^{2})]$ and

$\rho ge_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p=S_{0}\,a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$.

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
=[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a]^{-1}$,

$\mu$ drops out of the steady state. 
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)e_{\rho}$,
the same Stokes solution is

$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh]^{-1}$,

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$
and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Viscosity cancels in the
steady state and the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift is the usual shear-to-normal
stress conversion.

The minority $\chi_{s}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$ form is obtained if the
steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is not enforced together with the
full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$.  It coincides with $\chi_{0}$
to $O(a)$, $\chi_{s}=a+O(a^{3})$ is formally claimed but
$a\sinh a/(a^{2}+c^{2})=a^{2}+O(a^{4})$, so the strictly steady impermeable
locked top selects the odd mode with the $\cosh$ numerator above, the
$kh\sinh kh$ version being the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ evaluation.  The thin
plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $2kh e^{-kh}$
screening are robust to this $O(a^{2})$ interchange, which is why the
long-wave test does not discriminate the two forms. ∎

20.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $k$-mode is the usual Stokes stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$

\[
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_zu_z
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

In the time independent limit the deflected top is material,
$u_x(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$, so that in the strict steady limit
$u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  On the regular biharmonic this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and, up to a constant,

\[
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
\]

Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$ and

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
\]

With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

\[
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p ,\qquad p=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
\]

The base conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$,

\[
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
A\big[-c+a s\big]-hB c=0,
\qquad B=A\frac{a s-c}{h c},
\]

and

\[
[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
=-\frac{2kA}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big].
\]

Hence

\[
S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kA}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],
\qquad 
A=-\frac{S_{0}h c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]} .
\]

Using (1),

\[
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A
          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
\]

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\]

and $\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  In particular

\[
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\;a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\;a\gg1,
\]

so that with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shear-to-normal shift

\[
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\]

and the response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)e_{\rho}$,
the same Stokes solution is

\[
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

and on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
\]

so that $\chi(kh)=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the
viscosity-free steady Stokes dynamic topography, $90^{\circ}$ phase
shift and exponential screening.

The literature also quotes the odd-mode form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}\tanh a$.
It is obtained when the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is
enforced together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_zu_z$ at the
locked top, i.e. the $W'(0)=0$ combination.  To $O(a)$,
$\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$, so
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and

\[
\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a],
\qquad e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g,
\]

the same thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening as the $\cosh$ form.  The $kh\cosh kh/
[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ expression is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only evaluation,
i.e. the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ balance; once the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is imposed the two forms coincide to
$O(kh)$, which is why the long-wave limit is robust across the
deliberation.  Viscosity cancels, the $90^{\circ}$ phase is universal,
and the thin-plate viscous pumping law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is the common leading order result.

11.text:
The stream function of the $k$--mode can be written

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
\qquad \big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0 ,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
       =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the time independent limit the deflected top is material,
$\dot e=0$, so that on the steady surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

and on the regular biharmonic we may put

$$
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx ,
$$

so that on the normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p ,\qquad 
p=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}

On the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0 ,\qquad
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. with $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$,

$$
p\big(c-a s\big)+qh\,c=0,\qquad 
q=p\,\frac{a\tanh a-1}{h},
$$

and

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kp}{h c}\Big[a^{2}+c^{2}\Big] .
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kp}{h c}\Big[a^{2}+c^{2}\Big] ,
\qquad 
p=-\frac{S_{0}h\,c}{2\mu k\big[a^{2}+c^{2}\big]} ,
$$

and with (1)

$$
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh .
$$

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\tag{2}
$$

the viscosity cancelling out of the steady state. In particular

$$
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\qquad a\gg1,
$$

so that with the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shift

$$
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi_{0}\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.
Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
e_{\rho}$, the same Stokes solution is normally quoted with the
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. with the density kept explicit

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\chi_{0}(kh)
       \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g} .
$$

In the long-wave thin sheet limit

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\big[(kh)^{3}\big],\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the viscosity
free steady Stokes dynamic topography,
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, produced by the harmonic basal
traction $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and the $90^{\circ}$ shear-to-normal phase shift.
Up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping the thin plate limit
is the text-book viscous pumping law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The strict steady impermeable, no-slip material top
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ selects the regular odd mode
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.  In that odd-mode notation the free surface
coupling is often written

$$
\chi_{s}(a)=\frac{a\sinh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\chi_{0}(a)\tanh a ,
\qquad e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{s}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

which satisfies $\chi_{s}=a+O(a^{3})$ and
$\chi_{s}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.  Hence
$\chi_{s}=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$ and

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the same $O(kh)$ thin-plate viscous pumping law and the same
$2kh\,e^{-kh}$ viscous screening as the $\cosh$ form quoted in (2),
the $\sinh/\cosh$ difference being $O[(kh)^{2}]$ in the long wave
limit.  With the conventional identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this
is the quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi\simeq kh$ in the long-wave limit, i.e. the familiar
$e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous-isostatic response. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 2-D Stokes $k$-mode is
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $p=P\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$.
In the time independent material limit the deflected top is locked and
impermeable

$u_{x}(0)=0,\;u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\iff\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

the regular odd mode

$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+qz\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$.
On the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$, $p=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,
give with $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$

$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$,
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kA(c^{2}+a^{2})/(hc)$ with $A=p$,
$S_{0}= -2\mu k p(c^{2}+a^{2})/(hc)$,

$p=-S_{0}hc/[2\mu k(c^{2}+a^{2})]$.
Hence

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p=S_{0}\,
\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh$,

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
          =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  In particular
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$,
so

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,

with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shear to normal coupling and
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.
Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
The viscosity free steady response is therefore the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+
\cosh^{2}a]$ viscous-isostatic topography, $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ in the thin plate long wave limit.

The odd-mode form $\chi_{\rm sinh}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=
\chi_{0}\tanh a$ is obtained if the steady impermeability is not
enforced together with the full $-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ normal stress
at the locked top.  To $O(a)$ $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$ so
$\chi_{\rm sinh}=a+O(a^{3})$ and the thin plate limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening are
preserved.  The $a\cosh a$ form is the one obtained with the strict
steady material conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the complete
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, i.e. the $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ Stokes solution quoted by the majority
in rounds 0–4. density book-keeping remains $\chi_{\Delta}=
(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}$; with the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification the quoted factor is $\chi_{0}$ above. ∎

19.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode is now settled.  With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z
      =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
The regular biharmonic can be written
$\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.
In the time independent limit the deflected top is material,
$\dot e=0$, so with the stated $u_x(0)=0$ we have in the strict steady
limit $u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  On the regular basis this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the admissible steady mode is the odd impermeable
mode
$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q\,z\sinh kz$.
Viscosity cancels in the steady state.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
Top $z=0$: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$,
so that on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement
$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$.

With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$ the base conditions give
$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$ and
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kp\,[c^{2}+a^{2}]/[h c]$.
Hence
$S_{0}= -2\mu kp\,[c^{2}+a^{2}]/[h c]$,
$p=-S_{0}h c/[2\mu k(c^{2}+a^{2})]$ and
$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p
      =S_{0}\,a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$.
Thus on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a) S_{0}/\rho g$,   $\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[\,a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a\,]
     =[\cosh a/a+a\,\ {\rm sech}a]^{-1}$,

$\mu$ drops out, $\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, and
$\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.
In particular $e_{s}\simeq a S_{0}/\rho g=kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$,
the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same Stokes solution is
$e_{s}=S_{0}\chi_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ on the conventional
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  Keeping the
$\rho$ used in the statement explicit,
$e_{s}=S_{0}\chi_{0}/\rho g=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\chi_{0}$,
i.e. with the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ convention
$e_{s}= \chi(kh) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$,
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

The current round is split on the numerator.  Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,
18,20,21 keep the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only evaluation $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ and obtain
the $\cosh$ form above.  Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,9 argue for the
strict steady impermeable locked top $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with
the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$, which selects the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and gives the formally odd form
$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}(a)\tanh a$.
To $O(a)$ $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$, so
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for
$a\gg1$, i.e. the thin–plate limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
and the $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening are identical in both presentations.
The $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$ difference is the $O[(kh)^{2}]$ transient
$W(0)=\dot e$ term which vanishes in the strict steady impermeable limit.

The remaining book-keeping is the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor.  The
statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ but asks for the
normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Hence formally
$\chi=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\chi_{0}$ and with the conventional
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification the textbook factor is
$\chi_{0}(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$.
This is the viscosity-free stable dynamic topography generated by the
harmonic basal shear $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase shift. ∎

reflection_text.12:
The Stokes stream-function set up is now common ground.

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\;u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,  
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,   $p=P\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,  
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,  
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

On the regular biharmonic $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.  In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$.  The $u_x(0)=0$ condition is $\Phi'(0)=0$.  The strict material condition adds $u_z(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the odd impermeable mode

$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$.

$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx=-4\mu k^2A\cos kx$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^2\Phi'(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.

With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$, $U=A+Bh$,

$W(h)=0\iff U(e^{2a}+1)=-2aA$; the shear condition gives

$A=-\dfrac{S_0 h c}{4\mu k\,[a^2+c^2]}$,

hence on the $\rho g$ normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\rho g e_s=-4\mu k^2A=S_0\,\dfrac{a c}{a^2+c^2}$,

$e_s=\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$,

$\chi_0(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^2+\cosh^2 a}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+a\,{\rm sech}a\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels.  $\chi_0(a)=a+O(a^3)$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.  Long wave $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$, $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$, exponential screening.

With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ quoted as
$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2 kh}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,a s/(c^2+a^2)$,

$\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/(a^2+\cosh^2 a)=\chi_0(a)\tanh a$.

$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^3)$, i.e. the thin plate limit $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the $2a e^{-a}$ screening are unchanged; $\sinh/\cosh$ difference is $O(a^2)$, degenerate in the long wave limit. reflection_text.4:
The k-mode Stokes problem is now essentially settled in form. With 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.
On the regular biharmonic $\Phi=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$.

In the strict steady material limit $\dot e=0$ the deflected top is locked
and impermeable, $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  
Then $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and the admissible odd impermeable mode can be written
$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q\,z\sinh kz$.
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$.
With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p$.  Base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$
give with $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$
$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$ and $[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=-2kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$.
Hence $S_0=-2\mu kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$ and
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,a c/(a^{2}+c^{2})$,

$e_s=\chi_0(a)S_0/\rho g$, $\chi_0(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
=[\cosh a/a+a\,\operatorname{sech}a]^{-1}$,
$\mu$ cancels.  $\chi_0=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_0\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$.
In particular $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$, with the familiar
$90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shift and exponential screening for
$kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is usually quoted as
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=[\cosh a/a+a\,\operatorname{sech}a]^{-1}$,
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^3]$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The persistent minority 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21 imposes the steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ at the locked top and keeps the odd
$\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ coupling.  The free-surface balance then becomes
$\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}p$ with the same base conditions, giving
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,a s/(c^{2}+a^{2})$,
i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_0(a)\tanh a$.
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and $\chi_{\rm odd}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$.
To $O(a)$ $\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$ so $\chi_{\rm odd}=\chi_0+O(a^{3})$
and both give identical thin-plate law $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and
the same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening. The $\cosh$ form is the $u_x(0)=0$ only
evaluation $W(0)=-4k^{2}A$ before enforcing the steady impermeability
$W'(0)=0$; the $\sinh$ form is the strict $W'(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
odd-mode selection with the $2\mu\partial_z u_z$ term retained.

The unresolved book-keeping remains the explicit $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor
coming from $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$ in the statement versus
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ in the question.  Up to that harmless density
conversion the viscosity-free steady Stokes topography is the
$a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ response, $e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$
in the long-wave thin-plate limit, with the $90^{\circ}$ phase and
exponential screening.  The odd-mode $\sinh$ numerator is the strict
steady-impermeable version and coincides with the $\cosh$ version to
$O(kh)$, which is why the thin-plate limit is robust across colleagues.

The stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ is the common set up.  
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,  
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.

In the time independent limit the deflected top is material.  The statement gives $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $\dot e=0$ so that $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. the regular impermeable mode

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$\Phi(z)=p[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+q\,z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx$.

With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$, $p=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $a=kh$, $c=\cosh a$, $s=\sinh a$,

$\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff p(a s-c)=qh c$,
$q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$,

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kp[c/h+k^{2}h/c]=-2kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$.

Hence
$S_{0}= -2\mu kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$, $p=-S_{0}hc/[2\mu k(c^{2}+a^{2})]$,
and
$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p=S_{0}a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$.

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(a)S_{0}/\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
=[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a]^{-1}$,
$a=kh$,

and $\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$,
so that for the long wave thin sheet
$e_{s}\simeq aS_{0}/\rho g=kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$,
the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh]^{-1}$,
$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The odd-mode form $\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}\tanh a$
is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only, $W(0)=\dot e$, transient evaluation.  It coincides with $\chi_{0}$ to $O(a)$, $\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$, and gives the identical thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening.  Imposing the strict steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ selects the regular odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode and the viscosity-free steady Stokes topography above, i.e. up to the harmless $\rho/\Delta\rho$ book keeping the stable response is the $a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ viscous-isostatic factor, normally quoted as $\chi\approx kh$ in the long-wave limit. ∎

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.  With $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$, the no normal traction condition gives $(p+qh)c=k h p s$, $q=p[a\tanh a-1]/h$, and

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kp[c/h+k^{2}h/c]=-2kp[c^{2}+a^{2}]/hc$.

$\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$,

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_s=\chi_{0}(a)S_{0}/\rho g$, $\chi_{0}(a)=\dfrac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh a}{a}+\dfrac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity cancels in the steady state, the phase is $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$,

$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$, $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$, $a\gg1$,

so for a long-wave thin sheet $e_s\simeq a S_{0}/\rho g=kh S_{0}/\rho g$ and the response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is quoted as

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_s\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$, and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

Imposing $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_z u_z$ selects the odd $\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ mode.  With $W'(0)=0$ retained the free-surface coupling is then carried by the odd combination and the free-surface balance can be written

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,a\sinh a/[c^{2}+a^{2}]$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rm odd}(a)=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}(a)\tanh a$.  Colleagues 13,14,16,17,2,5,7,21 advocate this $\sinh$ numerator, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,20 keep the $u_x(0)=0$ only evaluation with $W(0)=\dot e$ retained, giving the $\cosh$ numerator above. $\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$, $\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}
       =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
In the time independent material limit the deflected top is locked
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and, with $\dot e=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. on the regular
biharmonic
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and in the $e^{\pm kz}$
basis

$\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p$.
The base conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $q=p\,[a\tanh a-1]/h$ and

=-2kp\,[c^{2}+a^{2}]/[hc]$, i.e.
$S_{0}= -\dfrac{2\mu kp}{hc}\,[c^{2}+a^{2}]$,
$p=-\dfrac{S_{0}hc}{2\mu k\,[c^{2}+a^{2}]}$.

$\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p=S_{0}\,a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$,

       =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1}$,

$S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2\mu kp[a^{2}+c^{2}]/hc$,
$p=-S_{0}hc/[2\mu k(a^{2}+c^{2})]$ and

$\rho ge_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p=S_{0}\,a c/[a^{2}+c^{2}]$.

On the $\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\rho g$, 
$\chi_{0}(a)=a\cosh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]
=[\cosh a/a+a/\cosh a]^{-1}$,

$\mu$ drops out of the steady state. 
$\chi_{0}=a+O(a^{3})$ for $a\ll1$, $\chi_{0}\sim2a e^{-a}$ for $a\gg1$,
so that

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $kh\ll1$,

the familiar $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ viscous pumping with
exponential screening $\chi_{0}\sim2kh e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)e_{\rho}$,
the same Stokes solution is

$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]
=[\cosh kh/kh+kh\,{\rm sech}kh]^{-1}$,

$\chi=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$
and $\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$.  Viscosity cancels in the
steady state and the $90^{\circ}$ phase shift is the usual shear-to-normal
stress conversion.

steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is not enforced together with the
full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$.  It coincides with $\chi_{0}$

locked top selects the odd mode with the $\cosh$ numerator above, the
$kh\sinh kh$ version being the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ evaluation.  The thin
plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the $2kh e^{-kh}$
screening are robust to this $O(a^{2})$ interchange, which is why the
long-wave test does not discriminate the two forms. ∎
reflection_text.20:
The $k$-mode is the usual Stokes stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$

\[
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -P+2\mu\partial_zu_z
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

In the time independent limit the deflected top is material,
$u_x(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$, so that in the strict steady limit
$u_z(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  On the regular biharmonic this is
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$ and, up to a constant,

\[
\Phi(z)=p\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+q\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
\]

Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}p$ and

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =-2\mu k^{2}p\cos kx .
\]

With the normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$

\[
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}p ,\qquad p=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{1}
\]

The base conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $a=kh$, $s=\sinh a$, $c=\cosh a$,

\[
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0\iff
A\big[-c+a s\big]-hB c=0,
\qquad B=A\frac{a s-c}{h c},
\]

and

\[
[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
=-\frac{2kA}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big].
\]

Hence

\[
S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kA}{h c}\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big],
\qquad 
A=-\frac{S_{0}h c}{2\mu k\big[c^{2}+a^{2}\big]} .
\]

Using (1),

\[
\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A
          =S_{0}\,\frac{a\,c}{a^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad a=kh,
\]

i.e. on the $\rho g$ normalisation

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
        =\Big[\frac{\cosh a}{a}+\frac{a}{\cosh a}\Big]^{-1},
\]

and $\mu$ cancels in the steady state.  In particular

\[
\chi_{0}(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\;a\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{0}(a)\sim2a e^{-a},\;a\gg1,
\]

so that with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ shear-to-normal shift

\[
e_{s}\simeq a\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}=kh\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
\]

and the response is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring traction in the isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)e_{\rho}$,
the same Stokes solution is

\[
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

and on the conventional geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+kh\,{\rm sech}kh\Big]^{-1},
\]

so that $\chi(kh)=kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\sim2kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  This is the
viscosity-free steady Stokes dynamic topography, $90^{\circ}$ phase
shift and exponential screening.

The literature also quotes the odd-mode form
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]=\chi_{0}\tanh a$.
It is obtained when the steady impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is
enforced together with the full $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_zu_z$ at the
locked top, i.e. the $W'(0)=0$ combination.  To $O(a)$,
$\sinh a/\cosh a=1+O(a^{2})$, so
$\chi_{\rm odd}=a+O(a^{3})$ and

\[
\chi_{\rm odd}=a\sinh a/[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a],
\qquad e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g,
\]

the same thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
same $2kh e^{-kh}$ screening as the $\cosh$ form.  The $kh\cosh kh/
[a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a]$ expression is the $u_{x}(0)=0$ only evaluation,
i.e. the transient $W(0)=\dot e$ balance; once the strict steady
impermeability $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is imposed the two forms coincide to
$O(kh)$, which is why the long-wave limit is robust across the
deliberation.  Viscosity cancels, the $90^{\circ}$ phase is universal,
and the thin-plate viscous pumping law $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is the common leading order result.
